\title{Ising Model Formalization: A Mathematical Guide to the Lean 4 Code}
\author{ising-model project}
\date{2026-04-17}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This document is a guide to reading the Lean~4 source code of the
\texttt{ising-model} project. Rather than reproducing full proofs,
it explains \emph{how to navigate the codebase}: which files to read
in which order, what each file's role is, and where the key ideas live.
Mathematical statements are included to orient the reader, but the
primary goal is to make the formal code accessible.

The project covers Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics: A Functional
Integral Point of View} (2nd ed., 1987), with particular emphasis on
the Ising-model discussions in \S4.1--4.6 (correlation inequalities,
Lee--Yang, free energy), \S5.1--5.4 (phase transitions, Peierls
argument), \S10.2--10.5 (conditioning), and the infinite-volume limit
theorems in \S4.2 (Thm~4.2.3) and \S4.6 (Prop~4.6.1).
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

%======================================================================
\section{Formalization regimes}
%======================================================================

We distinguish three formalization regimes in this project.

\subsection{Finite-volume}

The Ising model on a fixed finite interaction graph
$G : \texttt{SimpleGraph}~\iota$ with $[\texttt{Fintype}~\iota]$.
Most of the project lives here: correlation inequalities (GKS, FKG,
GHS), Lee--Yang, the partition-polynomial nonvanishing, the Peierls
bound, and the real-analyticity of $f(h)$ for $h > 0$.

\subsection{Discretized infinite-volume}

A fixed finite ambient type $\iota$ (so $[\texttt{Fintype}~\iota]$)
with a monotone increasing family of subgraphs $G_1 \le G_2 \le \cdots$.
``Growing'' the lattice then corresponds to adding edges.  The
GJ~\S4.2 Thm~4.2.3 and GJ~\S4.6 Prop~4.6.1 are formalized in this
regime: the proof mechanism (GKS + monotonicity + boundedness) is
identical to GJ, but the ambient lattice is finite.  Every
\texttt{*\_monotone\_subgraph} / \texttt{*\_convergent\_subgraph}
result in the codebase lives in this regime.

\subsection{Genuine infinite-volume (\texttt{AmbientLattice.lean})}

An ambient type $V : \texttt{Type}$ \emph{without} a
$[\texttt{Fintype}~V]$ assumption, and finite volumes $\Lambda :
\texttt{Finset}~V$.  Correlations on $\Lambda$ are defined by
instantiating the existing framework on the Fintype $(\uparrow\!\Lambda)$
using the induced subgraph $G.\texttt{induce}~(\uparrow\!\Lambda)$.
An \emph{exhaustion} $\Lambda_n \uparrow V$ is a monotone sequence
of finite volumes eventually containing any prescribed finite set;
this is the setting for the true thermodynamic limit.

At present \texttt{AmbientLattice.lean} establishes the types, the
basic lemmas (positivity of $Z_\Lambda$, $|\langle\sigma^A\rangle_\Lambda|
\le 1$, GKS-I on $\Lambda$), the \texttt{Exhaustion} structure, and
the eventually-defined \texttt{correlationAlongExhaustion}.  The
convergence theorem along an exhaustion is not yet proved in this
regime (it would require a compatibility argument across different
$\Lambda$'s).

%======================================================================
\section{How to read this codebase}
%======================================================================

\subsection{File dependency graph}

Read the files in this order. Each file imports only the files above it.

\begin{Verbatim}
Basic.lean                   Spin, Config, IsingParams
  |
Hamiltonian.lean             H(sigma), edgeSpin, spin flip
  |
GibbsMeasure.lean            Z, Gibbs expectation, correlation
  |
  +-- Inequalities/
  |     NonnegCorrelations.lean   HNC property, exp decomposition
  |     GKS.lean                  GKS-I, GKS-II
  |     FKG.lean                  FKG inequality
  |     GHS.lean                  truncated functions, GHS, Cor 4.3.3-5
  |
  +-- Asano.lean                  MultilinPoly, Asano contraction
  |     LeeYang.lean              Lee-Yang (Harcos/Ruelle, uses MultilinPoly only)
  |
  +-- InfiniteVolume.lean         boundedness, monotonicity, convergence
  |     FreeEnergy.lean           free energy, analyticity, Lee-Yang (Ising)
  |     Conditioning.lean         beta-monotonicity, Z bounds, reflection pos.
  |
  +-- PhaseTransition.lean        phase decomposition, mean field, symmetry
  |
  +-- Peierls.lean                Peierls bound, spontaneous magnetization
  |
  +-- Lattice.lean                lattice graph definitions
  |
  +-- ContinuousSpin/Phi4.lean    phi^4 identities (axioms)
  |
  +-- AmbientLattice.lean         ambient V : Type*, Lambda : Finset V, exhaustion
\end{Verbatim}

\subsection{Recommended reading paths}

\paragraph{Path 1: GKS inequalities (simplest).}
\texttt{Basic.lean} $\to$ \texttt{Hamiltonian.lean} $\to$
\texttt{GibbsMeasure.lean} $\to$ \texttt{NonnegCorrelations.lean} $\to$
\texttt{GKS.lean}.
\emph{Key idea:} the Boltzmann weight factors as a product of
$\cosh + \sinh \cdot \sigma_i\sigma_j$ terms, each with non-negative
coefficients (HNC). Fourier--Walsh expansion then gives GKS-I/II.

\paragraph{Path 2: Lee-Yang theorem.}
\texttt{Asano.lean} (for \texttt{MultilinPoly} type) $\to$
\texttt{LeeYang.lean} $\to$ \texttt{FreeEnergy.lean}.

\emph{Key idea:} the Harcos/Ruelle approach defines a polynomial
from a Hermitian matrix, uses a torus identity to relate complementary
coefficients, and applies the maximum modulus principle.
Induction on $n$ eliminates one variable at a time.
Asano contraction is \emph{not} used.

\paragraph{Path 3: GHS and truncated functions.}
\texttt{GHS.lean} (imports \texttt{InfiniteVolume.lean}).

\emph{Key idea:} the Lebowitz inequality (axiom from $\varphi^4$ theory)
bounds the 3-point function, giving $\langle\sigma_i;\sigma_j;\sigma_k\rangle \le 0$.
Spin-flip symmetry at $h=0$ kills odd correlations.

\paragraph{Path 4: Peierls argument.}
\texttt{Peierls.lean}.

\emph{Key idea:} the Hamiltonian--boundary identity
$H = -J(|E| - 2|\partial\sigma|)$ rewrites the Boltzmann weight.
Contour counting gives the Peierls bound.

\subsection{Conventions used throughout}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Type variables.} $\iota$ is the site type
    (\texttt{[Fintype $\iota$] [DecidableEq $\iota$]}), $G$ is a
    \texttt{SimpleGraph $\iota$} with \texttt{[Fintype G.edgeSet]}.
  \item \textbf{Field genericity.} Definitions use a generic ordered
    field $K$; main theorems specialize to $\mathbb{R}$.
  \item \textbf{Sign convention.} $H = -J\sum_e s_i s_j - h\sum_i s_i$
    (negative coupling = ferromagnetic).
  \item \textbf{Boltzmann weight.} $w(\sigma) = \exp(-\beta H(\sigma))$
    (\texttt{boltzmannWeight}).
  \item \textbf{Axioms.} \emph{None.} The formalization carries \textbf{no
    declared axioms} (modulo Mathlib). The former $\varphi^4$ axiom
    \texttt{phi4\_single\_\allowbreak site\_nonneg} is now a proven theorem; the
    Lebowitz/GHS axioms \texttt{lebowitz\_\allowbreak third/\allowbreak four}
    were found \emph{false as stated} and replaced by corrected theorems
    (\texttt{lebowitz\_inductive} discharged); and the three §17.8 axioms behind
    $\eta\le1$ (\texttt{ball\_boundary\_tight\_infinite},
    \texttt{shellSup\_contraction},
    \texttt{polynomialDecay\_contraction\_factor\_tendsto}) are now all proven
    theorems.
  \item \textbf{Edge representation.} Edges are \texttt{Sym2 $\iota$}
    (unordered pairs). The edge spin product
    \texttt{edgeSpin $\sigma$ $e$} $= s(\sigma_i) \cdot s(\sigma_j)$
    is defined via \texttt{Sym2.lift}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{How the key proofs work in Lean}

Many proofs follow a common pattern:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Unfold definitions} to expose the sum
    $Z^{-1} \sum_\sigma (\cdots)$.
  \item \textbf{Factor the Boltzmann weight} using
    $\exp(\alpha s) = \cosh\alpha + s\sinh\alpha$
    (\texttt{exp\_edgeSpin\_decomp}).
  \item \textbf{Expand products} to get a polynomial in spin products
    $\sigma^S$.
  \item \textbf{Apply non-negativity} of each coefficient
    (HNC, \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations}).
  \item \textbf{Close with} \texttt{nlinarith}, \texttt{linarith},
    or \texttt{Finset.sum\_nonneg}.
\end{enumerate}

%======================================================================
\section{Basic definitions (\texttt{Basic.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} None (this is the root file).

\textbf{Role:} Defines the alphabet of the Ising model --- spin values,
configurations, parameters. Everything else builds on these types.

\textbf{What to look for:} the \texttt{Spin} type and its arithmetic
(\texttt{toSign}, \texttt{flip}, \texttt{sign}), and the
\texttt{Ferromagnetic} structure ($J \ge 0$, $h \ge 0$, $\beta > 0$).

\begin{definition}[Spin]
$\mathrm{Spin} = \{\mathrm{up}, \mathrm{down}\}$ with sign function
$s : \mathrm{Spin} \to \mathbb{Z}$, $s(\mathrm{up})=+1$,
$s(\mathrm{down})=-1$.
\end{definition}

\noindent\textbf{Lean:} \texttt{inductive Spin}, \texttt{Spin.toSign}

\begin{definition}[Configuration]
A configuration on a type $\iota$ is a function
$\sigma : \iota \to \mathrm{Spin}$.
\end{definition}

\noindent\textbf{Lean:} \texttt{abbrev Config ($\iota$) := $\iota$ $\to$ Spin}

\begin{definition}[Ising parameters]
Over an ordered field $K$: coupling $J : K$, external field $h : K$,
inverse temperature $\beta : K$.
Ferromagnetic condition: $J \geq 0$, $h \geq 0$, $\beta > 0$.
\end{definition}

\noindent\textbf{Lean:} \texttt{structure IsingParams},
\texttt{structure Ferromagnetic}

\section{Hamiltonian (\texttt{Hamiltonian.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{Basic.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Defines the energy function $H(\sigma)$ and
the edge spin product. The spin flip symmetry theorem lives here.

\textbf{What to look for:} \texttt{edgeSpin} (the $\pm 1$ product
for an edge, defined via \texttt{Sym2.lift}) and
\texttt{hamiltonian\_flip\_eq} (the $h=0$ symmetry).

\begin{definition}[Ising Hamiltonian]
For a simple graph $G$ on $\iota$,
\[
  H_G(\sigma) = -J \sum_{\{i,j\} \in E(G)} s(\sigma_i)\,s(\sigma_j)
  - h \sum_{i \in \iota} s(\sigma_i).
\]
\end{definition}

\noindent\textbf{Lean:} \texttt{interactionEnergy} $+$
\texttt{externalFieldEnergy} $=$ \texttt{hamiltonian}

Key auxiliary definitions (in \texttt{Basic.lean}):
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{Spin.flip}: $\mathrm{up} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{down}$
  \item \texttt{Spin.sign $K$ $s$}: cast $s(\cdot)$ into the field $K$
  \item \texttt{Config.flip}, \texttt{Config.flipAt}: global and single-site spin flip
\end{itemize}
Key auxiliary definitions (in \texttt{Hamiltonian.lean}):
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{edgeSpin}: $s(\sigma_i) \cdot s(\sigma_j)$ for an edge
    $\{i,j\}$, defined via \texttt{Sym2.lift}
\end{itemize}

\begin{lemma}[Spin flip symmetry --- \texttt{hamiltonian\_flip\_eq}]
If $h = 0$, then $H_G(\bar{\sigma}) = H_G(\sigma)$ where
$\bar{\sigma}_i = \mathrm{flip}(\sigma_i)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Each edge factor satisfies $(-s_i)(-s_j) = s_i s_j$
(\texttt{edgeSpin\_flip}), and the field term vanishes since $h=0$.
\end{proof}

\section{Partition function and Gibbs measure (\texttt{GibbsMeasure.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{Hamiltonian.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Defines the three central objects: partition function $Z$,
Gibbs expectation $\langle\cdot\rangle$, and correlation function
$\langle\sigma^A\rangle$. Also contains the spin product algebra
($\sigma^A \cdot \sigma^C = \sigma^{A \triangle C}$, $(\sigma^A)^2 = 1$).

\textbf{What to look for:} \texttt{partitionFunction\_pos} ($Z > 0$)
and \texttt{spinProduct\_mul} (the key algebraic identity for GKS proofs).

\begin{definition}[Partition function]
$Z_G = \sum_{\sigma : \iota \to \mathrm{Spin}} \exp(-\beta\, H_G(\sigma))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[$Z > 0$ --- \texttt{partitionFunction\_pos}]
$Z_G > 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each summand $\exp(\cdot) > 0$ (\texttt{Real.exp\_pos}), and the
index set $\iota \to \mathrm{Spin}$ is nonempty
(\texttt{Finset.univ\_nonempty}).
Apply \texttt{Finset.sum\_pos}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Gibbs expectation, correlation]
$\langle F \rangle = Z^{-1} \sum_\sigma F(\sigma)\,e^{-\beta H}$, \quad
$\langle \sigma^A \rangle = \langle \prod_{i \in A} s(\sigma_i) \rangle$.
\end{definition}

\noindent\textbf{Lean:} \texttt{gibbsExpectation},
\texttt{spinProduct}, \texttt{correlation}

\subsection{Spin product algebra}

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{spinProduct\_sq}]
$(\sigma^A)^2 = 1$ for any $A$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{spinProduct\_mul}]
$\sigma^A \cdot \sigma^C = \sigma^{A \bigtriangleup C}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $\sigma^A = \prod_{i \in \iota}
(\text{if } i \in A \text{ then } s_i \text{ else } 1)$
(using \texttt{Finset.prod\_filter}).
Multiply pointwise (\texttt{Finset.prod\_mul\_distrib}).
At each site: if $i \in A \cap C$, $s_i \cdot s_i = 1$ (by
\texttt{Spin.toSign\_sq}); otherwise the factor is $s_i$ or $1$,
matching $A \bigtriangleup C$.
\end{proof}

\section{GKS-I proof (\texttt{Inequalities/GKS.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{GibbsMeasure.lean},
\texttt{NonnegCorrelations.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Proves the first and second Griffiths inequalities.

\textbf{What to look for:} The proof reduces GKS to the HNC property
of the Boltzmann weight (\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_hasNonnegCorrelations}).
Once HNC is established, GKS-I is a one-liner.

\subsection{Reduction to non-negative correlations}

\begin{theorem}[GKS-I --- \texttt{gks\_first}]
For ferromagnetic parameters, $\langle \sigma^A \rangle \geq 0$
for all $A$.
\end{theorem}

The proof factors as:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Since $Z > 0$, it suffices to show the numerator
    $\sum_\sigma \sigma^A e^{-\beta H} \geq 0$
    (\texttt{gibbsExpectation\_nonneg\_of\_numerator\_nonneg}).
  \item This follows from a property of $e^{-\beta H}$ called
    \emph{non-negative correlations}
    (\texttt{gks\_numerator\_nonneg}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Non-negative correlations (HNC)}

\begin{definition}[\texttt{HasNonnegCorrelations}]
A function $f : (\iota \to \mathrm{Spin}) \to \mathbb{R}$ has
\textbf{non-negative correlations} (HNC) if
$\sum_\sigma \sigma^S \cdot f(\sigma) \geq 0$ for every
$S \subseteq \iota$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Base case --- \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_one}]
$f \equiv 1$ has HNC.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $S = \emptyset$: $\sum_\sigma 1 = 2^{|\iota|} > 0$.
For $S \neq \emptyset$: $\sum_\sigma \sigma^S = 0$.

The vanishing is proved via the involution
$\mathrm{flipAt}(j)$ for any $j \in S$
(\texttt{sum\_config\_spinProduct\_eq\_zero}).
Each pair $(\sigma, \mathrm{flipAt}(j, \sigma))$ contributes
$\sigma^S + (-\sigma^S) = 0$ because flipping at $j \in S$ negates
the spin product (\texttt{spinProduct\_flipAt\_neg}).
The involution is applied via \texttt{Finset.sum\_ninvolution}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Preservation --- \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_mul}]
\label{lem:mul}
If $f$ has HNC and $a, b \geq 0$, then
$\sigma \mapsto f(\sigma)(a + b\,\sigma^C)$ has HNC.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\[
  \sum_\sigma \sigma^S f(\sigma)(a + b\,\sigma^C)
  = a \underbrace{\sum_\sigma \sigma^S f(\sigma)}_{\geq 0}
  + b \underbrace{\sum_\sigma \sigma^{S \bigtriangleup C} f(\sigma)}_{\geq 0}
\]
using $\sigma^S \sigma^C = \sigma^{S \bigtriangleup C}$
(\texttt{spinProduct\_mul}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Iterated product --- \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_finset\_prod},
\texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_mul\_prod}]
A product of factors $(a_k + b_k \sigma^{C_k})$ with $a_k, b_k \geq 0$
has HNC. More generally, multiplying an HNC function by such a product
preserves HNC.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By induction on the index set, applying Lemma~\ref{lem:mul} at each step.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Factoring the Boltzmann weight}

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{exp\_sign\_decomp}, \texttt{exp\_edgeSpin\_decomp}]
For $x \in \{+1, -1\}$ and $\alpha \geq 0$:
$e^{\alpha x} = \cosh\alpha + x\,\sinh\alpha$,
with $\cosh\alpha > 0$ and $\sinh\alpha \geq 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{bwFactored\_eq\_boltzmannWeight}]
\[
  e^{-\beta H_G(\sigma)}
  = \prod_{\{i,j\} \in E(G)} (\cosh(\beta J) + \sinh(\beta J)\,s_i s_j)
  \cdot \prod_{i \in \iota} (\cosh(\beta h) + \sinh(\beta h)\,s_i).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$-\beta H = \beta J \sum_e s_i s_j + \beta h \sum_i s_i$.
Apply $\exp(\text{sum}) = \prod\exp$ (\texttt{Real.exp\_sum}),
then decompose each factor.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Conclusion}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_hasNonnegCorrelations}]
$e^{-\beta H_G}$ has HNC for ferromagnetic parameters.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The factored form is a product of $(a+b\,\sigma^C)$ terms with
$a,b \geq 0$. Start from $f \equiv 1$ (HNC by base case),
multiply by each edge factor, then by each site factor. HNC is
preserved at each step by Lemma~\ref{lem:mul}.
\end{proof}

\noindent
GKS-I follows: $\langle \sigma^A \rangle
= Z^{-1}\sum_\sigma \sigma^A e^{-\beta H} \geq 0$
since $Z > 0$ and the numerator $\geq 0$ by HNC.

\section{GKS-II proof (\texttt{Inequalities/GKS.lean})}

\noindent\textbf{What to look for:} The proof introduces the
\emph{doubled system} --- a product of two independent copies of the
Ising model --- and a $45^\circ$ rotation $(t, q) = (\sigma + \tau,
\sigma - \tau)/\sqrt{2}$. The key step is showing that the doubled
Boltzmann weight has the HNC property in the $(t, q)$ variables.

The second Griffiths inequality is proved by the duplicate variable trick,
following Friedli--Velenik~\cite{friedli-velenik}, Theorem~3.49~(3.55),
pp.~127--128.

\begin{theorem}[GKS-II --- \texttt{gks\_second}]
For ferromagnetic parameters,
$\langle\sigma^A\sigma^B\rangle \geq \langle\sigma^A\rangle\langle\sigma^B\rangle$
for all $A, B$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Proof outline}

\begin{enumerate}
\item Introduce an independent copy $\chi$ of $\sigma$. Then
  \[
    Z^2\bigl(\langle\sigma^{A\triangle B}\rangle
      - \langle\sigma^A\rangle\langle\sigma^B\rangle\bigr)
    = \sum_{\omega,\omega'} \omega^A(\omega^B - \omega'^B)\,w(\omega)\,w(\omega').
  \]
  (\texttt{duplicateSum\_eq})

\item Change variables: $t_i = \omega_i \cdot \omega'_i$
  (\texttt{Spin.mul}). For fixed $\omega$, this is a bijection on
  $\mathrm{Config}\;\iota$. Under this substitution:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\omega^A(\omega^B - \omega'^B) = \omega^{A\triangle B}(1 - t^B)$
    \item $w(\omega)\,w(\omega\cdot t) = \mathrm{modifiedWeight}(t, \omega)$
      where each coupling $K_C$ is replaced by $K_C(1 + t^C) \geq 0$.
  \end{itemize}
  After swapping sums:
  \[
    \sum_t (1 - t^B) \sum_\omega \omega^{A\triangle B}\,
      \mathrm{modifiedWeight}(t, \omega).
  \]
  (\texttt{duplicateSum\_eq\_changed})

\item For each fixed $t$:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $(1 - t^B) \geq 0$ since $t^B \in \{-1,+1\}$
      (\texttt{one\_sub\_spinProduct\_nonneg}).
    \item The inner sum $\geq 0$ by
      \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_edge\_site\_product} applied to
      the modified couplings $K_C(1 + t^C)$
      (\texttt{modifiedWeight\_nonneg\_corr}).
  \end{itemize}

\item Since $Z^2 > 0$ and the duplicate sum $\geq 0$, GKS-II follows.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Key new definitions}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{Spin.mul}: spin multiplication ($\mathrm{up}$ acts as
    identity, $\mathrm{down}$ acts as flip).
    $\mathrm{toSign}(a \cdot b) = \mathrm{toSign}(a) \cdot \mathrm{toSign}(b)$.
  \item \texttt{modifiedWeight}: Boltzmann weight with couplings
    $K_C(1 + t^C)$.
  \item \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_edge\_site\_product}: shared
    lemma for GKS-I and GKS-II (product of $\exp(K \cdot \text{spin})$
    factors with $K \geq 0$ has HNC).
\end{itemize}

\section{Numerical tests (\texttt{test/IsingModel/GKSTest.lean})}

A Float-based reference implementation verifies:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $Z > 0$ for 4 graph types
  \item Spin flip symmetry ($h = 0$)
  \item GKS-I for 6 parameter sets (2--4 sites, all subsets)
  \item GKS-II ($\langle\sigma^A\sigma^B\rangle \geq
    \langle\sigma^A\rangle\langle\sigma^B\rangle$)
    for 6 parameter sets (2--4 sites, all subset pairs)
  \item GKS-I and GKS-II violation for anti-ferromagnetic $J < 0$
\end{itemize}

\section{FKG inequality (\texttt{Inequalities/FKG.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{GKS.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Proves $\langle fg \rangle \ge \langle f \rangle\langle g \rangle$
for monotone $f, g$.

\textbf{What to look for:} The Holley criterion approach. The proof
shows that the Gibbs measure satisfies the FKG lattice condition
by reducing to GKS-II.

The FKG inequality is proved by applying Mathlib's
\texttt{Combinatorics.\allowbreak SetFamily.\allowbreak FourFunctions.\allowbreak fkg}
to the Ising Boltzmann weight, following
Friedli--Velenik~\cite{friedli-velenik}, Theorem~3.21
(p.~98) and Theorem~3.50 (pp.~128--130).

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{fkg\_ising}]
For ferromagnetic parameters and monotone nondecreasing nonneg
$f, g : \mathrm{Config}\;\iota \to \mathbb{R}$,
$\langle fg \rangle \geq \langle f \rangle \langle g \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Proof outline}
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define a \texttt{LinearOrder} on \texttt{Spin}: $\mathrm{down} < \mathrm{up}$
  ($-1 < +1$). The product order on $\mathrm{Config}\;\iota = \iota \to
  \mathrm{Spin}$ makes it a \texttt{DistribLattice}.
\item Prove log-supermodularity of the Boltzmann weight
  (\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_log\_supermodular}):
  $w(\sigma)w(\sigma') \leq w(\sigma \vee \sigma')w(\sigma \wedge \sigma')$.
  This reduces to the edge inequality
  $\sigma_i\sigma_j + \sigma'_i\sigma'_j \leq
  (\sigma_i \vee \sigma'_i)(\sigma_j \vee \sigma'_j) +
  (\sigma_i \wedge \sigma'_i)(\sigma_j \wedge \sigma'_j)$
  (\texttt{spin\_edge\_supermodular}, verified by exhaustive case analysis).
\item Apply Mathlib's \texttt{fkg} with $\mu = w$, then convert from
  unnormalized sums to \texttt{gibbsExpectation} form.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Generic weighted-expectation linearity
(\texttt{Inequalities/WeightedExpectation.lean})}

Every Gibbs expectation in the FKG/Holley development has the shape
$\langle F \rangle = Z^{-1} \sum_\sigma F(\sigma)\, w(\sigma)$ for a partition
value $Z = \sum_\sigma w(\sigma)$ and a weight $w$ (the Boltzmann weight, the
inhomogeneous Boltzmann weight, or the boundary-condition Boltzmann weight). The
constant / additivity / scalar linearity of such a normalised weighted average is
purely algebraic and is proved once, generic in $w$ and $Z$, as
\texttt{weightedExpectation\_const} ($Z^{-1}\sum c\,w = c$),
\texttt{weightedExpectation\_add}, and \texttt{weightedExpectation\_const\_mul}.
The nine \texttt{gibbsExpectation\_*} / \texttt{gibbsExpectationJ\_*} /
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_*} wrappers delegate to these helpers (single source of
truth).

\subsection{General FKG for arbitrary monotone observables
(\texttt{Inequalities/FKGGeneral.lean})}

The theorem \texttt{fkg\_ising} above, inheriting the interface of Mathlib's
\texttt{fkg}, additionally requires the observables to be \emph{nonnegative}
($0 \le f$, $0 \le g$). The genuine Friedli--Velenik Theorem~3.21 holds for
\emph{any} monotone nondecreasing $f, g$ of arbitrary sign. We remove the
nonnegativity hypothesis by covariance shift-invariance.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{fkg\_ising\_of\_monotone}]
For ferromagnetic parameters and \emph{arbitrary} monotone nondecreasing
$f, g : \mathrm{Config}\;\iota \to \mathbb{R}$,
$\langle f \rangle \langle g \rangle \le \langle fg \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof.} The Gibbs covariance
$\mathrm{Cov}(f, g) = \langle fg \rangle - \langle f \rangle\langle g \rangle$
is invariant under adding constants to $f$ and $g$: by linearity of
$\langle \cdot \rangle$ and the normalisation $\langle 1 \rangle = 1$, the
constant terms cancel. Since $\mathrm{Config}\;\iota$ is finite (and nonempty),
each monotone observable attains a minimum; subtracting it gives nonnegative
monotone observables $f' = f - \min f \ge 0$ and $g' = g - \min g \ge 0$ with
$\mathrm{Cov}(f', g') = \mathrm{Cov}(f, g)$. Applying \texttt{fkg\_ising} to
$f', g'$ yields $\mathrm{Cov}(f, g) = \mathrm{Cov}(f', g') \ge 0$. The argument
uses the Gibbs-expectation linearity lemmas \texttt{gibbsExpectation\_const}
($\langle c \rangle = c$), \texttt{gibbsExpectation\_add}
($\langle F + H \rangle = \langle F \rangle + \langle H \rangle$), and
\texttt{gibbsExpectation\_const\_mul} ($\langle cF \rangle = c\langle F \rangle$),
all proved in the same file. \hfill$\square$

\subsection{FKG with inhomogeneous per-edge couplings
(\texttt{Inequalities/FKGInhomogeneous.lean})}

Friedli--Velenik Theorem~3.21 is stated for a \emph{collection of nonnegative
couplings} $J = (J_{ij})$ (one per edge) and an \emph{arbitrary} field $h$, not
just the uniform scalar coupling \texttt{IsingParams.J}. We build the
inhomogeneous Gibbs stack
\[
  H_J(\sigma) = -\sum_{e \in E} J(e)\, s(\sigma_i) s(\sigma_j)
                - h \sum_i s(\sigma_i),
  \qquad w_J(\sigma) = e^{-\beta H_J(\sigma)},
\]
with \texttt{interactionEnergyJ}, \texttt{hamiltonianJ}, \texttt{boltzmannWeightJ},
\texttt{partitionFunctionJ}, and \texttt{gibbsExpectationJ} (with linearity
lemmas).

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{boltzmannWeightJ\_log\_supermodular}]
For $\beta \ge 0$ and every coupling $J(e) \ge 0$ (the field $h$ may have any
sign, its term being modular),
$w_J(\sigma) w_J(\sigma') \le w_J(\sigma \vee \sigma') w_J(\sigma \wedge \sigma')$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent The proof is the uniform-coupling argument with the single $J$ replaced
by the per-edge weights: each edge term is supermodular
(\texttt{spin\_edge\_supermodularJ}, 16-case check), and the nonnegative weights
$J(e)$ preserve the inequality under summation, while the field term is modular.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{fkg\_isingJ\_of\_monotone}, FV Thm 3.21 free boundary]
For nonnegative per-edge couplings $J(e) \ge 0$, $\beta \ge 0$, arbitrary field
$h$, and arbitrary monotone nondecreasing $f, g$,
$\langle f \rangle \langle g \rangle \le \langle fg \rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent Proved from \texttt{fkg\_isingJ} (the nonnegative-observable case, via
Mathlib's \texttt{fkg} applied to $w_J$) by the same covariance shift-invariance
as \texttt{fkg\_ising\_of\_monotone}. This matches FV~3.21 exactly for the
free-boundary case; arbitrary boundary conditions remain follow-up (Issue~3558).

\subsection{FKG with arbitrary boundary conditions
(\texttt{Inequalities/FKGBoundaryCondition.lean})}

Friedli--Velenik Theorem~3.21 allows an \emph{arbitrary boundary condition}: the
spins outside the finite volume $\Lambda$ are frozen to a fixed external
configuration $\eta$. We obtain the boundary-condition Gibbs measure from the
inhomogeneous Boltzmann weight by \emph{conditioning} on configurations agreeing
with $\eta$ off $\Lambda$ --- no new Hamiltonian is needed, since the boundary
interactions are already present in $w_J$. Writing
$\mathrm{agreesOff}\;\Lambda\;\eta\;\sigma := (\forall i \notin \Lambda,\;
\sigma_i = \eta_i)$, the conditioned weight is
\[
  w^{\eta}_\Lambda(\sigma)
    = \mathbf{1}_{\{\sigma : \mathrm{agreesOff}\;\Lambda\;\eta\;\sigma\}}(\sigma)
      \cdot w_J(\sigma).
\]
The crucial point is that $\{\sigma : \mathrm{agreesOff}\;\Lambda\;\eta\;\sigma\}$
is a \emph{sublattice}: if $\sigma, \sigma'$ agree with $\eta$ off $\Lambda$ then so
do $\sigma \vee \sigma'$ and $\sigma \wedge \sigma'$ (off $\Lambda$ both equal
$\eta_i$, so the join/meet stay $\eta_i$; \texttt{agreesOff\_sup} /
\texttt{agreesOff\_inf}). Hence the indicator of that sublattice times the
log-supermodular weight is again log-supermodular
(\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_log\_supermodular}).

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{fkg\_isingBC\_of\_monotone}, FV Thm 3.21 full form]
For nonnegative per-edge couplings $J(e) \ge 0$, $\beta \ge 0$, arbitrary field
$h$, an arbitrary boundary condition $\eta$ outside $\Lambda$, and arbitrary
monotone nondecreasing $f, g$,
$\langle f \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda \langle g \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda
  \le \langle fg \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent Proved exactly as the free-boundary case (Mathlib \texttt{fkg} on the
conditioned weight, then the covariance shift). Together with the inhomogeneous
case this realizes the complete FV~3.21 statement.

\subsection{Field monotonicity via Holley's inequality
(\texttt{Inequalities/MonotonicityField.lean})}

Increasing the external field $h$ increases the Gibbs expectation of every
monotone observable:
\[
  h \le h' \;\Longrightarrow\; \langle \varphi \rangle_h \le \langle \varphi
  \rangle_{h'}
  \qquad (\varphi \text{ nondecreasing}).
\]
This is foundational for the stochastic ordering of Ising measures, the $\pm$
extremal states, and the infinite-volume limit. It is proved via Mathlib's
\texttt{holley} inequality. The two normalised Boltzmann weights at fields
$h \le h'$ satisfy the Holley domination condition
(\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_field\_cross\_supermodular})
\[
  w_h(a)\, w_{h'}(b) \le w_h(a \wedge b)\, w_{h'}(a \vee b),
\]
whose interaction part is the edge log-supermodularity (weight $\beta J \ge 0$)
and whose field part is the per-site inequality
$h\, s(a) + h'\, s(b) \le h\, s(a \wedge b) + h'\, s(a \vee b)$
(\texttt{field\_site\_mono}, valid for $h \le h'$, weight $\beta \ge 0$; the only
nontrivial case gives $(h'-h)(s(a)-s(b)) \ge 0$).

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{gibbsExpectation\_field\_mono}]
For a ferromagnetic Ising model ($\beta, J \ge 0$), $h \le h'$, and any monotone
nondecreasing $\varphi$,
$\langle \varphi \rangle_h \le \langle \varphi \rangle_{h'}$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent The nonnegative case is \texttt{holley} applied to the normalised
measures; the general case follows by the constant shift (the inequality is
invariant under $\varphi \mapsto \varphi - c$).

\subsection{Boundary-condition monotonicity via Holley
(\texttt{Inequalities/MonotonicityBoundary.lean})}

Raising the boundary condition raises the Gibbs expectation of every monotone
observable:
\[
  \eta \le \eta' \;\Longrightarrow\; \langle \varphi \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda
  \le \langle \varphi \rangle^{\eta'}_\Lambda
  \qquad (\varphi \text{ nondecreasing}).
\]
This is the cornerstone of the theory of extremal ($\pm$) Gibbs states and the
infinite-volume limit: the maximal ($+$) boundary condition yields the maximal
state. It is proved via \texttt{holley} on the conditioned boundary-condition
weights. The crucial point is the order-aware conditioning closure: if $a$ agrees
with $\eta$ off $\Lambda$ and $b$ with $\eta'$, then (since $\eta \le \eta'$)
$a \wedge b$ agrees with $\eta$ (as $\eta \wedge \eta' = \eta$) and $a \vee b$
agrees with $\eta'$ (as $\eta \vee \eta' = \eta'$); hence the domination
condition
$w^{\eta}(a)\, w^{\eta'}(b) \le w^{\eta}(a \wedge b)\, w^{\eta'}(a \vee b)$
(\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_cross\_supermodular}) reduces to
\texttt{boltzmannWeightJ\_log\_supermodular} on the agreeing case and is $0 \le$
nonnegative otherwise.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_boundary\_mono}]
For $\beta, J \ge 0$, $\eta \le \eta'$, and any monotone nondecreasing $\varphi$,
$\langle \varphi \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda \le \langle \varphi
\rangle^{\eta'}_\Lambda$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Extremal $\pm$ states and magnetization ordering
(\texttt{Inequalities/MonotonicityExtremal.lean})}

The boundary-condition monotonicity is sharpest at the two extremal
configurations $\texttt{plusConfig}$ (all spins up, maximal) and
$\texttt{minusConfig}$ (all spins down, minimal): every configuration satisfies
$\texttt{minusConfig} \le \sigma \le \texttt{plusConfig}$. Hence, for any boundary
condition $\eta$ and any monotone $\varphi$,
\[
  \langle \varphi \rangle^{-}_\Lambda \le \langle \varphi \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda
  \le \langle \varphi \rangle^{+}_\Lambda
  \qquad (\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_extremal\_sandwich}),
\]
so the $\pm$ boundary conditions bracket all boundary conditions: at this finite
volume the $+$ boundary condition gives the largest expectation of every monotone
observable (the foundation for the extremal infinite-volume $\pm$ states,
constructed as thermodynamic limits). As a concrete application, the single-spin observable
$\sigma \mapsto s(\sigma_i)$ is monotone (\texttt{singleSpinObs\_monotone}), so the
local magnetization is squeezed:
$\langle \sigma_i \rangle^{-}_\Lambda \le \langle \sigma_i \rangle^{\eta}_\Lambda
\le \langle \sigma_i \rangle^{+}_\Lambda$
(\texttt{magnetizationBC\_extremal\_sandwich}).

\subsection{Volume monotonicity of the $+$ state
(\texttt{Inequalities/VolumeMonotonicity.lean})}

The $+$ boundary expectation of a monotone observable \emph{decreases as the
volume grows}:
\[
  \Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2 \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \langle \varphi \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_2} \le \langle \varphi
  \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_1}
  \qquad (\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_volume\_antitone}).
\]
With the dual $-$ bound this exhibits the $\pm$ states as monotone limits over an
exhaustion --- the construction of the extremal infinite-volume Gibbs states. The
proof uses the conditioning structure: the $\Lambda_1$ $+$ state is the
$\Lambda_2$ $+$ state conditioned on the shell $\Lambda_2 \setminus \Lambda_1$
being all $+$ (\texttt{agreesOff\_plus\_iff\_shell}). The shell event is an
up-set, so its indicator $\mathbf{1}_A$ is monotone
(\texttt{upShellIndicator\_monotone}); the weight identity
$w^{+}_{\Lambda_1} = \mathbf{1}_A \cdot w^{+}_{\Lambda_2}$
(\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_plus\_eq\_shell\_mul}) gives
$\langle \varphi \cdot \mathbf{1}_A \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_2}
= \langle \varphi \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_1} \cdot
\langle \mathbf{1}_A \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_2}$, and the FKG inequality
$\langle \varphi \cdot \mathbf{1}_A \rangle \ge \langle \varphi \rangle
\langle \mathbf{1}_A \rangle$ then yields the claim after cancelling
$\langle \mathbf{1}_A \rangle^{+}_{\Lambda_2} > 0$.

\subsection{$+$ boundary expectation on a cubic box
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxPlusState.lean})}

The first step toward the infinite-volume $+$ Gibbs state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
(Issue~3565): \texttt{plusBoxExpectation}~$d\,n\,m\,J\,h\,\beta\,\varphi$ is the
expectation of $\varphi$ under the Ising measure on the box
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m$ with the annulus
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m \setminus \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ frozen to $+$ --- i.e.
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC} over the induced cubic-lattice graph with inner region
\texttt{plusBoxInterior}~$d\,n\,m$ and boundary configuration \texttt{plusConfig}.
Within a fixed ambient box $m$, growing the inner region makes the $+$ expectation
of a monotone observable decrease
(\texttt{plusBoxExpectation\_antitone\_interior}), the cubic-box instance of
FV~Lemma~3.22. Lifting this to a genuine thermodynamic limit (growing $m$ as well)
is the subject of the later PRs of Issue~3565.

\subsection{Bounded BC observables and the single-site $+$ box spin
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxPlusStateBounds.lean})}

Two generic reusable bounds: the boundary-condition expectation of a bounded
observable is bounded by the pointwise bound (it is a nonnegative-weight average),
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_le\_of\_forall\_le} and
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_ge\_of\_forall\_ge}. The single-site $+$ box spin
\texttt{plusBoxSpin}~$d\,n\,m\,J\,h\,\beta\,x$ (the $+$ boundary expectation of
$s(\sigma_x)$) then lies in $[-1, 1]$ (\texttt{plusBoxSpin\_mem\_Icc}, the
bounded-below input for the eventual monotone-convergence limit) and is antitone in
the inner region (\texttt{plusBoxSpin\_antitone\_interior}, the single-site
cubic-box instance of FV~Lemma~3.22). The remaining ingredient --- the
nearest-neighbour screening lemma (ambient-box independence) --- is the next PR of
Issue~3565.

\subsection{Cubic-box adjacency geometry
(\texttt{Concrete/CubicBoxAdjacencyGeometry.lean})}

The geometric facts underlying the screening of the $+$ box state.
\texttt{latticeGraph\_adj\_abs\_le\_one}: adjacent sites differ by at most $1$ in
each coordinate. \texttt{cubicBox\_adj\_mem\_succ}: a neighbour of a
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ site lies in $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+1)$, so the inner
free region reaches only one box further out (shielded from the outer shell).
\texttt{cubicBox\_shell\_adj\_not\_mem\_inner}: for $n+1 \le m$, a shell site of
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(m+1) \setminus \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m$ and any of its
neighbours lie outside $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$, so every shell-touching
interaction is between frozen $+$ spins --- the geometric input to the
constant-factor cancellation in the screening proof.

\subsection{Induced-graph energy split over the extension graph
(\texttt{AmbientLattice/Monotonicity/InducedEnergySplit.lean})}

The energy-level heart of the $+$-state screening, reusing the extension-graph
factoring of \texttt{EdgeSiteSums.lean}. The interaction energy on
$\texttt{inducedGraph}\,G\,\Lambda_2$ equals that on
$\texttt{extendGraphFromΛ₁}\,G\,\Lambda_1\,\Lambda_2$ plus the $-J$-weighted
edge-spin sum over the \emph{extra edges}
$(\texttt{inducedGraph}\,G\,\Lambda_2).\mathrm{edgeFinset} \setminus
(\texttt{extendGraphFromΛ₁}\,G\,\Lambda_1\,\Lambda_2).\mathrm{edgeFinset}$
(\texttt{interactionEnergy\_inducedGraph\_extendGraph\_split}, via
\texttt{edgeFinset\_mono} and \texttt{Finset.sum\_sdiff}). Composing the full
Hamiltonian split with \texttt{hamiltonian\_extendGraph\_factor} gives
(\texttt{hamiltonian\_inducedGraph\_restrict\_add})
\[
  H_{\texttt{induce}\,\Lambda_2}(\sigma)
    = H_{\texttt{induce}\,\Lambda_1}(\mathrm{restrict}\,\sigma)
      + (\text{complement field}) + (\text{extra-edge interaction}).
\]
On the cubic box the extra edges all touch the frozen $+$ shell (\S above), so the
extra-edge interaction is a constant that cancels in the normalised expectation
--- the screening.

\subsection{Boltzmann-weight factoring of an induced graph
(\texttt{AmbientLattice/Monotonicity/InducedWeightFactor.lean})}

Exponentiating the energy split gives
(\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_inducedGraph\_restrict\_factor})
\[
  w_{\texttt{induce}\,\Lambda_2}(\sigma)
    = w_{\texttt{induce}\,\Lambda_1}(\mathrm{restrict}\,\sigma)
      \cdot \exp\!\big(-\beta\,(\text{complement field} + \text{extra-edge
      interaction})\big).
\]
When the complement sites are all $\mathrm{up}$ and the extra edges all have
$\mathrm{edgeSpin} = 1$ (the frozen $+$ case),
\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_inducedGraph\_restrict\_factor\_const} collapses the
exponential factor to a constant depending only on the complement-site count and
the extra-edge count --- the constant that cancels in the normalised $+$
boundary-condition expectation (the screening).

\subsection{Cubic-box screening conditions
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxScreening.lean})}

The frozen-$+$ ingredients turning the generic weight factoring into the cubic-box
screening. \texttt{boltzmannWeightJ\_uniform\_eq}: at a uniform coupling
$\texttt{fun \_} \Rightarrow J$, the inhomogeneous Boltzmann weight equals the
ordinary one, $w_J^{(\texttt{fun \_}\Rightarrow J)} = w_{\langle J,h,\beta\rangle}$,
bridging the boundary-condition framework
($w^{\mathrm{BC}} = \mathbf{1}_{\mathrm{agrees}} \cdot w_J$) to the
uniform-coupling factoring lemmas.
\texttt{cubicBox\_extra\_edge\_endpoints\_not\_mem\_inner}: for $n+1 \le m$, both
endpoints of an extra edge (in the induced graph on $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(m+1)$
but not in the extension graph over $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m$) lie outside
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ --- by \texttt{Sym2.ind} case analysis, an endpoint lies
in the shell, and \texttt{cubicBox\_shell\_adj\_not\_mem\_inner} then places both
outside $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$. Hence on a $+$-off-$\texttt{box}\,n$
configuration every extra edge has $\mathrm{edgeSpin} = 1$ --- the $\texttt{hextra}$
input to the screening.

\subsection{Configuration-split decomposition for the cubic-box screening
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxScreeningDecomp.lean})}

The configuration-side ingredients. \texttt{restrictConfig\_plusConfig}:
restricting the all-$+$ configuration is all-$+$. \texttt{mem\_plusBoxInterior}:
$j \in \texttt{plusBoxInterior}\,d\,n\,m \iff (j : \mathbb Z^d) \in
\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$. \texttt{agreesOff\_plus\_configEquiv\_iff}: under the
configuration split $\texttt{configEquivSubtypeProd}\,(\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m
\subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(m+1))$, a recombined configuration
$(\mathrm{equiv})^{-1}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2)$ agrees with $+$ off
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ iff $\sigma_1$ agrees with $+$ off
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ \emph{and} $\sigma_2$ is all-$+$ on the shell (case
analysis on $i.\mathrm{val} \in \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m$, via the equiv component
lemmas). This is the $+$-shell indicator collapse that makes the $+$ box partition
function and numerator factor over the box-$m$ ones times a shell constant (the
final assembly of the screening).

\subsection{Cubic-box screening: pointwise $+$ weight factoring
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxScreeningCapstone.lean})}

The per-configuration heart of the screening.
\texttt{edgeSpin\_eq\_one\_of\_agreesOff\_extra}: for $\sigma$ agreeing with $+$ off
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$, every extra edge has $\mathrm{edgeSpin} = 1$ (both
endpoints outside $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ by \S above). \texttt{cubicBoxShellConst}
is the shell constant
$\exp(-\beta\,(-h\cdot\#\mathrm{compl} - J\cdot\#\mathrm{extra}))$. Then
\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_cubicBox\_succ\_pointwise}: under
\texttt{configEquivSubtypeProd},
\[
  w^{+}_{\texttt{box}\,(m+1)}\big((\mathrm{equiv})^{-1}(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)\big)
    = w^{+}_{\texttt{box}\,m}(\sigma_1) \cdot
      \begin{cases} \mathrm{shellConst} & \sigma_2 \equiv +\\ 0 & \text{else}
      \end{cases}
\]
(agreeing case: \texttt{boltzmannWeight\_inducedGraph\_restrict\_factor\_const} $+$
the BC$\leftrightarrow$uniform bridge $+$ the agrees-decomposition; non-agreeing
case $= 0$ via the boundary indicator). This factors the $+$ box partition function
and numerator over the box-$m$ ones (final $Z/N$ assembly next).

\subsection{Cubic-box screening: single-step ambient independence
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxScreeningLimit.lean})}

The $+$ box state is independent of the ambient box size (nearest-neighbour
screening). \texttt{bcSum\_cubicBox\_succ\_factor}: for an observable depending only
on the inner configuration, the boundary-condition sum over
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(m+1)$ factors as the box-$m$ sum times the shell constant
(reindex by \texttt{configEquivSubtypeProd} $+$ the pointwise factoring $+$ the
shell collapse \texttt{sum\_shell\_ite\_eq}). Hence
$Z^{+}_{m+1} = Z^{+}_m \cdot \mathrm{shellConst}$
(\texttt{partitionFunctionBC\_cubicBox\_succ}) and the shell constant cancels in the
normalised ratio (\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_cubicBox\_succ}). In particular
(\texttt{plusBoxSpin\_screening\_succ})
\[
  \texttt{plusBoxSpin}\,d\,n\,(m+1)\,\dots\,x
    = \texttt{plusBoxSpin}\,d\,n\,m\,\dots\,x
  \qquad (n+1 \le m,\ x \in \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,m):
\]
the single-site $+$ box spin depends only on the immediate $+$ boundary layer, not
the ambient box size. The remaining steps (induction to full ambient independence
and the $n \to \infty$ monotone-convergence limit) complete the infinite-volume $+$
state.

\subsection{Infinite-volume $+$ expectation of a single spin on $\mathbb Z^d$
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/InfiniteVolumePlusState.lean})}

The culmination of the cubic-box $+$-state programme: the infinite-volume $+$
boundary expectation of a single spin exists as the monotone limit along the cubic
exhaustion. For a fixed site $x \in \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,N$, the screened
single-site $+$ box spins
$k \mapsto \texttt{plusBoxSpin}\,d\,(N+k)\,(N+k+1)\,\dots\,x$ (free inner box
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(N+k)$, immediate $+$ boundary layer) are \emph{antitone}
(\texttt{plusBoxSpin\_infiniteVolume\_antitone}: FV~Lemma~3.22
$+$ the ambient screening) and bounded in $[-1, 1]$, so they converge
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusBoxSpin\_infiniteVolume}, via \texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciInf}):
\[
  \texttt{plusBoxSpin}\,d\,(N+k)\,(N+k+1)\,\dots\,x
    \;\longrightarrow\;
  \inf_{k} \texttt{plusBoxSpin}\,d\,(N+k)\,(N+k+1)\,\dots\,x
  \qquad (k \to \infty),
\]
the infinite-volume $+$ expectation of $\sigma_x$ --- a contribution to the
project's central long-term goal, the thermodynamic limit / extremal $+$ state.
Extending the limit to all local observables (the full state functional) is
follow-up.

\subsection{Infinite-volume $+$ expectation of a monotone local observable
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/LocalObservableLimit.lean})}

The single-spin limit generalises verbatim to an arbitrary \emph{monotone local
observable}, giving the standard $+$-state API. A
\texttt{LocalMonotoneObservable}~$d$ bundles a finite support
$S : \texttt{Finset}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,d \to \mathbb Z)$, a function
$\varphi : \texttt{Config}\,S \to \mathbb R$, and a proof that $\varphi$ is
monotone in the spin order. Its lift to a containing box,
$\texttt{lift}\,h_S = \varphi \circ \texttt{restrictConfig}\,h_S$, is again
monotone (\texttt{lift\_monotone}, via \texttt{restrictConfig\_monotone}), and
depends only on the inner configuration (\texttt{restrictConfig\_trans}), so the
ambient screening applies unchanged
(\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation\_screening\_succ}). Being a monotone function on
the \emph{finite} configuration space $\texttt{Config}\,S$, $\varphi$ attains a
minimum, which bounds the screened expectations from below
(\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation\_ge}) --- the bounded-below input replacing
$[-1,1]$. Hence for $S \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,N$ the screened
$+$ local expectations are antitone
(\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation\_infiniteVolume\_antitone}) and converge
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusBoxLocalObservable\_infiniteVolume}, via
\texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciInf}):
\[
  \texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation}\,(N+k)\,(N+k+1)\,\dots\,O
    \;\longrightarrow\;
  \inf_{k} \texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation}\,(N+k)\,(N+k+1)\,\dots\,O
  \qquad (k \to \infty).
\]
Since any local observable is a difference of monotone ones, this is the building
block of the full $+$-state functional.

\subsection{The cubic-exhaustion $+$-state functional
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/LocalObservableState.lean})}

The monotone limit extends to \emph{all} local observables, yielding the
cubic-exhaustion $+$-state functional and its \emph{same-support} linearity,
normalisation, and positivity (a step towards the FV~Theorem~3.17 $+$ state;
sequence independence, translation invariance, the $-$ state, and cross-support
union linearity remain follow-up).  A \texttt{LocalObservable}~$d$ is an arbitrary real function
$\varphi : \texttt{Config}\,S \to \mathbb R$ on a finite support (no
monotonicity).  The key elementary fact is the \emph{monotone-difference
decomposition}, playing the role of FV~Lemma~3.19: writing
$\texttt{rank}\,\sigma = \#\{i \in S : \sigma_i = +\}$ (monotone,
\texttt{configUpRank\_mono}, strictly increasing along covering steps,
\texttt{configUpRank\_lt\_of\_lt}) and $K = 2\max_\sigma |\varphi(\sigma)|$, the
function
\[
  \varphi = \underbrace{(K\cdot\texttt{rank} + \varphi)}_{=:~\varphi_+}
            - \underbrace{(K\cdot\texttt{rank})}_{=:~\varphi_-}
\]
is a difference of two \emph{monotone} functions: across any single covering step
$\texttt{rank}$ increases by at least $1$, and $K$ dominates the variation
$|\varphi(\sigma') - \varphi(\sigma)| \le 2\max|\varphi| = K$, so $\varphi_+$ is
nondecreasing (\texttt{LocalObservable.upper}/\texttt{lower},
\texttt{phi\_eq\_upper\_sub\_lower}).

The $+$ box expectation of an arbitrary observable
(\texttt{plusBoxObsExpectation}) is linear in $\varphi$ (from
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_add}/\texttt{const\_mul}/\texttt{const}) and splits as
$\langle\varphi\rangle = \langle\varphi_+\rangle - \langle\varphi_-\rangle$
(\texttt{plusBoxObsExpectation\_eq\_sub}).  Defining the $+$-state functional as
the difference of the two monotone limits
(\texttt{plusStateExpectation}), the screened box expectations converge to it
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusStateExpectation}), and uniqueness of limits propagates the
finite-volume algebra: the functional is linear (on a fixed support,
\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_add}, \texttt{\_const\_mul}), normalised
($\langle c\rangle = c$, \texttt{\_const}), positive
($\varphi \ge 0 \Rightarrow \langle\varphi\rangle \ge 0$, \texttt{\_nonneg}),
monotone (\texttt{\_mono}), and agrees with the monotone-observable limit on
monotone observables (\texttt{\_of\_monotone}).

\subsection{The $-$ state and the $\pm$ extremal ordering (FV~Lemma~3.23)
(\texttt{Inequalities/BoundaryFlip.lean},
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MinusStateExtremal.lean})}

The global spin-flip involution $\sigma \mapsto \sigma.\texttt{flip}$ maps the $-$
boundary state to the $+$ boundary state with the field reflected $h \mapsto -h$.
At the level of the inhomogeneous boundary-condition Gibbs expectation this is the
\emph{flip bridge}
\[
  \langle F\rangle^{-}_{\Lambda}(h)
    = \langle F\circ\texttt{flip}\rangle^{+}_{\Lambda}(-h)
  \qquad(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_minus\_eq\_plus\_neg\_h\_flip}),
\]
proved from $H_G(\sigma; J, -h) = H_G(\sigma.\texttt{flip}; J, h)$
(\texttt{hamiltonianJ\_neg\_h\_flip}: the $J$-term is flip-invariant, the field
term reflects), the boundary-condition exchange
\texttt{agreesOff\_minusConfig\_flip\_iff} ($\sigma$ agrees with $-$ off $\Lambda$
iff $\sigma.\texttt{flip}$ agrees with $+$), the per-configuration weight identity
\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_minus\_eq\_plus\_neg\_h\_flip}, and the
\texttt{flipEquiv} reindexing of the configuration sum (numerator and partition
function).

Hence the $-$-state functional is obtained for free:
$\texttt{minusStateExpectation}\,J\,h\,\beta\,O
   := \texttt{plusStateExpectation}\,J\,(-h)\,\beta\,O.\texttt{flipObs}$, where
$O.\texttt{flipObs} = \sigma \mapsto \varphi(\sigma.\texttt{flip})$, inheriting
convergence (\texttt{tendsto\_minusStateExpectation}) and the same-support
linearity / normalisation / positivity (\texttt{minusStateExpectation\_\{add,
const\_mul, const, nonneg\}}).  Finally, for a monotone observable and
$\beta, J \ge 0$, the flip bridge turns the finite-volume boundary monotonicity
$\langle\varphi\rangle^{-}_{\Lambda} \le \langle\varphi\rangle^{+}_{\Lambda}$
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_minus\_le}) into the $\pm$ extremal ordering
(FV~Lemma~3.23)
\[
  \mu^{-}(\varphi) \le \mu^{+}(\varphi)
  \qquad(\texttt{minusStateExpectation\_le\_plusStateExpectation}),
\]
passing to the limit through the two convergent box-expectation sequences (here
along the cubic exhaustion; the sequence-independent FV~Theorem~3.17 limit is
follow-up).

\subsection{Cross-support union linearity
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/LocalObservableUnion.lean})}

The same-support linearity extends to observables on \emph{different} supports.
\texttt{LocalObservable.extend}~$h_{SS'}$ enlarges the support $S \subseteq S'$ by
ignoring the new coordinates ($\varphi \circ \texttt{restrictConfig}$); the box
expectation is unchanged by restriction transitivity
(\texttt{plusBoxObsExpectation\_extend\_eq}, definitionally), hence so is the
$\pm$-state functional (\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_extend\_eq},
\texttt{minusStateExpectation\_extend\_eq}, via uniqueness of limits).  Lifting
$\varphi_1$ on $S_1$ and $\varphi_2$ on $S_2$ to the common support
$S_1 \cup S_2 \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,N$ and applying same-support
additivity gives the cross-support union linearity
\[
  \mu^{\pm}(\varphi_1 + \varphi_2) = \mu^{\pm}(\varphi_1) + \mu^{\pm}(\varphi_2)
  \qquad(\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_union\_add},
  \texttt{minusStateExpectation\_union\_add}).
\]

\subsection{Boundary-condition translation covariance
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslation.lean})}

The first step towards translation invariance of the cubic-exhaustion
$\pm$-state functional (Issue~3581) is the boundary-condition analogue of
\texttt{correlationΛ\_vaddFinset\_eq}.  On a translation-invariant graph with
uniform coupling and constant field, the boundary-condition Gibbs expectation is
covariant under the lattice translation $\tau = \texttt{configVaddEquiv}\,t\,\Omega$:
\[
  \langle F \circ \tau^{-1}\rangle^{\tau\eta}_{\tau\Lambda}
    = \langle F\rangle^{\eta}_{\Lambda}
  \qquad(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_vaddFinset\_eq}),
\]
built from the all-$+$ configuration's translation invariance
(\texttt{plusConfig\_configVaddEquiv}), the boundary-agreement transport
(\texttt{agreesOff\_map\_configVaddEquiv\_iff}), and the uniform-Hamiltonian
invariance \texttt{hamiltonian\_configVaddEquiv\_symm}, reindexing the conditioned
configuration sum via \texttt{configVaddEquiv}.  The geometric squeeze relating the
centered cubic boxes to their translates (and hence the translation invariance of
the limit) is the next step of Issue~3581.

\subsection{Cubic-box interlacing geometry
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/CubicBoxInterlacing.lean})}

A centered cubic box \texttt{cubicBox}\,$d\,n$ (the sup-norm ball of radius $n$) is
not preserved by a lattice translation $a$, but it interlaces with its translate up
to the index shift $R = \texttt{latticeRadius}\,a = \max_i |a_i|$:
\[
  a + \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+R),
  \qquad
  \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n \subseteq a + \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+R)
\]
(the translation action is pointwise addition on $\mathbb Z^d$)
(\texttt{vaddFinset\_cubicBox\_subset}, \texttt{cubicBox\_subset\_vaddFinset}).
Specialising the boundary-condition covariance to the translation-invariant all-$+$
boundary gives \texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_vaddFinset\_eq}.  Combining this
interlacing with a generalized-ambient screening and a monotone squeeze (the next
step of Issue~3581) will yield the translation invariance of the cubic-box limit.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17, pp.~100--104.

\subsection{General-ambient $+$ boundary screening
(\texttt{AmbientLattice/Monotonicity/PlusScreening.lean})}

The cubic-box $+$ screening generalises to an arbitrary ambient pair
$\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ with an inner region $I$ whose extra-edge shell is
separated from $I$ (hypothesis \texttt{hsep}).  Under that hypothesis, the $+$
boundary expectation of an observable depending only on the inner configuration is
\emph{independent of the ambient}:
\[
  \langle\varphi\rangle^{+}_{I,\,\Lambda_2}
    = \langle\varphi'\rangle^{+}_{I,\,\Lambda_1}
  \qquad(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_extendGraph\_screening}),
\]
proved by the per-configuration weight factoring
\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_extendGraph\_pointwise} (the frozen-$+$ shell factors out
as \texttt{plusShellConst}, via
\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_inducedGraph\_restrict\_factor\_const}) and the shell-sum
collapse.  Since a translated cubic box is not itself a cubic box, the cubic
screening does not apply directly to the translation squeeze, but this general
screening does.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4
Theorem~3.17, pp.~100--104.

\subsection{Translated observable and the interlacing antitone sandwich
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationInvariance.lean})}

The translation $\tau_a$ of a monotone observable is
\texttt{LocalMonotoneObservable.vadd}~$a$ (support $a + S$, observable pulled back
through \texttt{configVaddEquiv}, monotonicity preserved), with support inside
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(N + \texttt{latticeRadius}\,a)$.  Writing
\texttt{translatedInner}~$a\,n\,M$ for the sites of the common ambient
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,M$ whose value lies in $a + \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$, the
cubic interlacing transfers to the inner regions,
\[
  \texttt{plusBoxInterior}\,d\,(n-R)\,M \subseteq \texttt{translatedInner}\,a\,n\,M
    \subseteq \texttt{plusBoxInterior}\,d\,(n+R)\,M
  \qquad(R = \texttt{latticeRadius}\,a),
\]
so the volume monotonicity \texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_volume\_antitone} gives
the antitone sandwich \texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_translatedInner\_sandwich}:
$E^{+}_{n+R} \le E^{+}_{a + n} \le E^{+}_{n-R}$ on the common ambient.  Recentering
the middle term (covariance) and passing to the limit along the cubic exhaustion
(the next step of Issue~3581) yields $\mu^{+}(\tau_a\varphi) = \mu^{+}(\varphi)$.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17, pp.~100--104.

\subsection{Recentering covariance for the translation squeeze
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationCapstone.lean})}

The recentering step identifies the sandwich middle term with a cubic expectation
of the original observable.  Applying the boundary-condition covariance with
$t = -a$ keeps the centered cubic box as the original volume $\Omega$ and sends the
\emph{translated} box to the $\texttt{vaddFinset}\,t\,\Omega$ side, so no
ambient-equality transport is needed
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_translatedInner\_recenter}), built from the inner-region
pullback \texttt{translatedInner\_map\_vaddSubtypeEquiv} and the observable
recentering \texttt{vadd\_lift\_comp\_configVaddEquiv\_symm}.  The general screening
relating the translated ambient back to the cubic exhaustion, and the limit
squeeze, complete the translation invariance (the next step of Issue~3581).
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17, pp.~100--104.

\subsection{Screening the translated ambient back to the cubic exhaustion
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationFinal.lean})}

The recentered middle term lives on the translated ambient
$\texttt{vaddFinset}\,(-a)\,(\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,M)$.  The general-ambient
screening brings it back onto the cubic exhaustion.  The shell-separation
hypothesis \texttt{hsep\_translated} holds because a $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$
site's neighbours lie in $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+1)$
(\texttt{cubicBox\_adj\_mem\_succ}), so no extra edge touches the centered inner
region.  Hence
$\langle O.\texttt{lift}\rangle^{+}_{\texttt{innerOf}\ldots,\;\text{translated}}
  = \texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation}\,n\,(n+1)\,O$
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_innerOf\_translated\_eq\_plusBoxLocal}), and composing
with the recentering covariance gives the translated sandwich middle term as a
cubic local expectation
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_translatedInner\_vadd\_eq\_plusBoxLocal}).  The bounds
screening and the limit squeeze (the next step of Issue~3581) then complete the
translation invariance.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4
Theorem~3.17, pp.~100--104.

\subsection{Translation invariance of the cubic-exhaustion $+$-state functional
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationHeadline.lean})}

The culmination of the translation-invariance arc: the cubic-exhaustion $+$-state
functional is invariant under lattice translations on a monotone observable,
\[
  \mu^{+}(\tau_a\varphi) = \mu^{+}(\varphi)
  \qquad(\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_vadd\_monotone}).
\]
Writing $R = \texttt{latticeRadius}\,a$ and $n = N + 2R + k$, the per-stage squeeze
\texttt{plusBoxLocal\_vadd\_squeeze} brackets the translated $+$ local expectation
$E^{+}_{n}$ (recentered, on a monotone observable) between the cubic local
expectations of the translated observable at inner indices $n+R$ and $n-R$ (the
interlacing antitone sandwich, the recentered middle term, and the multi-step
ambient independence \texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation\_screening\_eq}).  Both shifted
subsequences and the middle sequence converge to their respective $+$-state limits
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusBoxLocalObservable\_infiniteVolume} composed with the index
shift), so \texttt{le\_of\_tendsto\_of\_tendsto'} and \texttt{le\_antisymm} give the
equality.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17
(statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Translation-invariance infrastructure for general observables
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationGeneral.lean})}

The infrastructure to extend translation invariance from monotone observables to
all local observables via the monotone-difference decomposition: the up-spin count
(\texttt{configUpRank\_configVaddEquiv\_symm}) and the monotone bound
(\texttt{monoBound\_vadd}) are translation-invariant, so the upper/lower monotone
parts commute with translation (\texttt{vadd\_upper\_phi\_eq},
\texttt{vadd\_lower\_phi\_eq}); with \texttt{plusStateExpectation\_congr\_phi} this
reduces the general-observable translation invariance to the monotone case
(\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_vadd\_monotone}).  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Translation invariance for all local observables
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateTranslationGeneralHeadline.lean})}

The final assembly: the cubic-exhaustion $+$-state functional is invariant under
lattice translations on \emph{any} local observable, $\mu^{+}(\tau_a\varphi) =
\mu^{+}(\varphi)$ (\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_vadd}).  Through the
monotone-difference decomposition (\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_eq\_upper\_sub\_lower})
and the fact that translation commutes with the upper/lower parts, the general case
reduces to the monotone case \texttt{plusStateExpectation\_vadd\_monotone}.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement
p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Translation invariance of the $-$-state functional
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MinusStateTranslation.lean})}

The $-$-state translation invariance $\mu^{-}(\tau_a\varphi) = \mu^{-}(\varphi)$
(\texttt{minusStateExpectation\_vadd}) follows from the $+$-state one via the
spin-flip bridge $\mu^{-}(\varphi) = \mu^{+}_{-h}(\varphi\circ\texttt{flip})$, since
translation commutes with the flip (\texttt{flipObs\_vadd\_phi\_eq}).  Reference:
Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof
pp.~102--103).

\subsection{General shell separation and ambient independence
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateExhaustion.lean})}

Towards exhaustion independence: the shell-separation hypothesis of the general
screening holds whenever every inner-region site has all its lattice neighbours in
the smaller ambient (\texttt{hsep\_of\_neighbors\_subset}, generalising the
cubic-specific \texttt{hsep\_translated}).  Hence the $+$ boundary expectation of an
observable depending only on the inner configuration is ambient-independent
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_screening\_of\_neighbors}).  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Ambient independence of the cubic $+$ local expectation
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateAmbientCubic.lean})}

A step towards exhaustion independence: the cubic $+$ local expectation
$\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation}\,n\,(n+1)\,O$ is realised on \emph{any} ambient
$\Omega \supseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+1)$
(\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation\_eq\_on\_ambient}), by the general ambient
independence since a $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$ site's neighbours lie in
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n{+}1)$.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4
Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{General two-ambient independence of the $+$ boundary expectation
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusStateAmbientIndep.lean})}

The compatibility lemma that makes the $+$ state ambient-free: for a free region
$I$ whose lattice neighbours lie in $\Lambda_1$, and an observable $O$ supported in
$\Lambda_1$, the $+$ boundary expectation of $O$ with inner region $I$ on $\Omega_1$
equals that on $\Omega_2$, for \emph{any} two ambients
$\Omega_1, \Omega_2 \supseteq \Lambda_1$
(\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_ambient\_indep}); both sides reduce to the value on
$\Lambda_1$ by two applications of
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_screening\_of\_neighbors}.  This is the key compatibility
for the directed-infimum formulation of the $+$ state: different finite free regions
are compared by routing each through its own ambient.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Region $+$ expectation and its nearest-neighbour closure
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusRegionExpectation.lean})}

For a finite region $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ we model the FV finite-volume $+$
measure $\mu^+_A$ --- the Ising measure in $A$ with the configuration \emph{outside}
$A$ frozen to $+1$ --- as a \texttt{gibbsExpectationBC} on the \emph{nearest-neighbour
closure} $\texttt{nnClosure}\,d\,A = A \cup \partial A$, with free region $A$ and the
boundary layer $\partial A$ frozen $+$ (\texttt{plusRegionExpectation}).  The closure
satisfies $A \subseteq \texttt{nnClosure}\,d\,A$ (\texttt{subset\_nnClosure}), every
neighbour of an $A$-site lies in it (\texttt{nnClosure\_neighbors\_subset}), it is
monotone in $A$ (\texttt{nnClosure\_mono}), and
$\texttt{nnClosure}\,d\,(\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n) \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(n+1)$
(\texttt{nnClosure\_cubicBox\_subset\_succ}).  The region $+$ expectation is
ambient-independent: it is realised on \emph{any} ambient
$\Omega \supseteq \texttt{nnClosure}\,d\,A$
(\texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_eq\_on\_ambient}, via
\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_screening\_of\_neighbors}); antitone in the region (FV
Lemma~3.22: growing $A$ pushes the $+$ boundary away and decreases the monotone
expectation, compared on the common ambient $\texttt{nnClosure}\,d\,A'$,
\texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_antitone}); and agrees with the cubic
$\texttt{plusBoxLocalExpectation}\,n\,(n+1)$ on $A = \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n$
(\texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_cubicBox\_eq}), connecting the region functional to the
cubic-exhaustion $+$ state.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4
Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Cubic-radius convergence of the region $+$ expectation
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusRegionCubicConvergence.lean})}

The region $+$ expectation $\texttt{plusRegionExpectation}\,(\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,r)$
of a monotone observable converges, as the radius $r \to \infty$, to the
cubic-exhaustion $+$ state $\texttt{plusStateExpectation}$.  This is the
radius-reindexed form of the monotone-convergence limit
$\texttt{tendsto\_plusBoxLocalObservable\_infiniteVolume}$.  It is antitone in the
cubic radius (FV Lemma~3.22, \texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_cubicBox\_antitone}).  The
convergence is packaged as a \emph{total} sequence
$\texttt{regionCubicValue}\,r = \texttt{plusRegionExpectation}\,(\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(\max N\,r))$
(the $\max N\,r$ keeps the support hypothesis $O.S \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(\max
N\,r)$ available for every $r$; \texttt{regionCubicValue\_eq} gives its value for
$N \le r$), ready to be composed with the inner/outer radii of a general exhaustion.
The $N+k$-indexed convergence
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusRegionExpectation\_cubicBox}) follows from
\texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_cubicBox\_eq} and the monotone limit; the
radius-reindexed convergence (\texttt{tendsto\_regionCubicValue}) follows by the
reindexing $r \mapsto r - N$ (\texttt{tendsto\_sub\_atTop\_nat}), cofinal at infinity,
with the equal-radius congruence
\texttt{plusRegionExpectation\_cubicBox\_index\_congr}.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Exhaustion independence of the $+$ state (FV Theorem 3.17)
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusRegionExhaustion.lean})}

The headline of the exhaustion-independence programme: for \emph{any} exhaustion
$\Lambda$ of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d \ge 1$) and a monotone local observable $O$, the region
$+$ expectations $\texttt{plusRegionExpectation}\,(\Lambda.\texttt{volume}\,(N_0+k))$
converge to the cubic-exhaustion $+$ state $\texttt{plusStateExpectation}$ as
$k \to \infty$ (\texttt{tendsto\_plusRegionExpectation\_exhaustion}) --- the
finite-volume $+$ measures $\mu^+_{\Lambda_k}$ converge to the \emph{same}
infinite-volume $+$ state regardless of the exhaustion.  The proof is a \emph{squeeze}:
each volume is sandwiched between two cubic boxes
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(\texttt{innerRadius}\,k) \subseteq \Lambda.\texttt{volume}\,k
\subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(\texttt{outerRadius}\,k)$, both radii tending to
$\infty$ (\texttt{exhaustionInnerRadius\_tendsto},
\texttt{exhaustionOuterRadius\_tendsto}); region antitonicity (FV Lemma~3.22) turns the
inclusions into inequalities, and both cubic bounds converge to
$\texttt{plusStateExpectation}$ (\texttt{tendsto\_regionCubicValue}), closing the
squeeze by \texttt{tendsto\_of\_tendsto\_of\_tendsto\_of\_le\_of\_le'}.  The strict
monotonicity of cubic boxes ($\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,a \subseteq \texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,b
\iff a \le b$, \texttt{cubicBox\_subset\_iff\_le}, for $d \ge 1$ via a
$\texttt{Pi.single}$ separating vertex) underlies the outer-radius divergence.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95,
proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Exhaustion independence for general observables and the $-$ state
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PlusRegionObsExhaustion.lean})}

The monotone-observable headline extends to \emph{all} local observables and to the
$-$ state, completing FV Theorem~3.17 ($d \ge 1$).  The region $+$ expectation of a
general observable is the difference of those of its upper/lower monotone parts
($\texttt{plusRegionObsExpectation} = \texttt{plusRegionExpectation}\,O.\texttt{upper}
- \texttt{plusRegionExpectation}\,O.\texttt{lower}$,
\texttt{plusRegionObsExpectation\_eq\_sub}), so for any exhaustion $\Lambda$ it
converges to $\texttt{plusStateExpectation}$
(\texttt{tendsto\_plusRegionObsExpectation\_exhaustion}, the difference of the two
monotone headlines via \texttt{plusStateExpectation\_eq\_upper\_sub\_lower}).  The
$-$ state is the $(-h, \texttt{flipObs})$ specialisation: the global spin-flip bridge
gives $\texttt{minusStateExpectation} = \texttt{plusStateExpectation}$ at
$(-h, \texttt{flipObs})$, so $\texttt{minusRegionObsExpectation}$ converges to
$\texttt{minusStateExpectation}$
(\texttt{tendsto\_minusRegionObsExpectation\_exhaustion}).  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 Theorem~3.17 (statement p.~95, proof pp.~102--103).

\subsection{Infinite-volume magnetization $m^\pm(\beta,h)$
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/InfiniteVolumeMagnetization.lean})}

The order parameter of the Ising phase transition is the single-spin expectation
$m^\pm(\beta,h) = \mu^\pm(\sigma_x)$ in the cubic-exhaustion $\pm$ state.  The single
spin is a monotone observable ($\texttt{singleSpinMonoObs}\,x$, support $\{x\}$,
$\varphi = s(\sigma_x)$), so $\texttt{plusMagnetization}$ and
$\texttt{minusMagnetization}$ inherit from the $\pm$-state machinery: the finite-volume
$\pm$ box magnetizations converge to $m^\pm$ (\texttt{tendsto\_plusMagnetization},
\texttt{tendsto\_minusMagnetization}); the bounds $m^\pm \in [-1,1]$
(\texttt{plusMagnetization\_le\_one}, \texttt{neg\_one\_le\_plusMagnetization}, and the
$-$ analogues via the flip form) follow from monotonicity and normalisation of the
state functional; and the extremal ordering $m^- \le m^+$
(\texttt{minusMagnetization\_le\_plusMagnetization}) is FV Lemma~3.23 / Theorem~3.17.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.4 (Theorem~3.17), \S3.6
(magnetization, phase transition).

\subsection{Spin-flip symmetry of the magnetization
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MagnetizationFlipSymmetry.lean})}

The global spin-flip $\sigma \mapsto \sigma.\texttt{flip}$ (with $h \mapsto -h$)
exchanges the $\pm$ states and negates the single spin
($\texttt{singleSpinMonoObs\_phi\_flip}$, from $\texttt{Spin.sign\_flip}$), giving the
magnetization symmetry $m^-(\beta,h) = -m^+(\beta,-h)$
(\texttt{minusMagnetization\_eq\_neg\_plusMagnetization\_neg\_h} and its reverse) via
the $-$-state-as-flipped-$+$-state definition together with
\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_congr\_phi} and
\texttt{plusStateExpectation\_const\_mul}.  At zero field this gives the antisymmetry
$m^-(\beta,0) = -m^+(\beta,0)$
(\texttt{minusMagnetization\_zero\_eq\_neg\_plusMagnetization\_zero}).  Reference:
Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.6 (the $\pm$ magnetizations and spin-flip
symmetry).

\subsection{Field monotonicity of the magnetization
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MagnetizationFieldMonotone.lean})}

Increasing the field increases the magnetization (Holley's inequality, FV
Theorem~3.50).  The unconditioned field monotonicity
($\texttt{gibbsExpectation\_field\_mono}$) is lifted to the boundary-condition Gibbs
expectation: the $\eta$-boundary Boltzmann weights are field-cross-supermodular
($\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_field\_cross\_supermodular}$ --- when both configurations
agree with $\eta$ off $\Lambda$ the boundary-agreement sublattice closure
$\texttt{agreesOff\_inf}$ / $\texttt{agreesOff\_sup}$ reduces it to
$\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_field\_cross\_supermodular}$, and otherwise the left side
vanishes), so Holley gives
$\langle\varphi\rangle^\eta_h \le \langle\varphi\rangle^\eta_{h'}$ for monotone
$\varphi$ ($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_field\_mono\_of\_nonneg}$,
$\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_field\_mono}$ via subtracting the finite minimum).
Passing to the limit, $m^+(\beta,\cdot)$ is nondecreasing in the field
($\texttt{plusMagnetization\_mono\_h}$, by
$\texttt{le\_of\_tendsto\_of\_tendsto'}$ on the finite-volume box magnetizations), and
$m^-(\beta,\cdot)$ likewise through the flip symmetry
($\texttt{minusMagnetization\_mono\_h}$).  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge,
2017), \S3.6 (magnetization, monotonicity in the field; Holley's inequality,
Theorem~3.50).

\subsection{Spontaneous magnetization $m^*(\beta)$
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/SpontaneousMagnetization.lean})}

The order parameter of the Ising phase transition is the zero-field $+$ magnetization
at the origin, $m^*(\beta) = m^+(\beta,0)$
($\texttt{plusStateSpontaneousMagnetization}$).  Its key property is non-negativity
$0 \le m^*(\beta)$ ($\texttt{plusStateSpontaneousMagnetization\_nonneg}$): the
zero-field antisymmetry $m^-(\beta,0) = -m^+(\beta,0)$ and the extremal ordering
$m^- \le m^+$ give $-m^+(\beta,0) \le m^+(\beta,0)$, hence $0 \le m^+(\beta,0)$.  It is
bounded above by $1$ ($\texttt{plusStateSpontaneousMagnetization\_le\_one}$), and the
$-$ order parameter is its negative
($\texttt{minusStateSpontaneousMagnetization\_eq\_neg}$,
$-m^*(\beta) \le 0 \le m^*(\beta)$).  This is the $+$-state-route spontaneous
magnetization, distinct from the existing GKS-route
$\texttt{Ambient.spontaneousMagnetization}$.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge,
2017), \S3.6 (spontaneous magnetization, the order parameter).

\subsection{Sign of the magnetization
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MagnetizationSign.lean})}

The sign of the magnetization follows from field monotonicity and zero-field
non-negativity.  At zero field $0 \le m^+(\beta,0)$ at every site
($\texttt{plusMagnetization\_zero\_field\_nonneg}$, the general-site form of the
spontaneous non-negativity).  Hence for $h \ge 0$ the $+$ magnetization is
non-negative ($\texttt{plusMagnetization\_nonneg\_of\_field\_nonneg}$, dominating its
zero-field value), and by the spin-flip symmetry, for $h \le 0$ the $-$ magnetization
is non-positive ($\texttt{minusMagnetization\_nonpos\_of\_field\_nonpos}$,
$m^-(\beta,h) = -m^+(\beta,-h)$ with $-h \ge 0$).  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.6 (magnetization, sign and the order parameter).

\subsection{GKS-I for the $+$ boundary-condition state
(\texttt{Inequalities/GKSBoundaryCondition.lean})}

The first Griffiths inequality, extended from the free Gibbs state to the $+$ boundary
state (the foundation for $\beta$/$J$-monotonicity of the $+$ magnetization).  The $+$
boundary Boltzmann weight is the free weight times a product of \emph{pinning factors}
$w^+_\Lambda(\sigma) = w(\sigma)\cdot\prod_{i\in\Lambda^c}(\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sigma_i)$
($\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_plus\_eq\_prod}$ --- each factor is $1$ when $\sigma_i=+1$
and $0$ when $\sigma_i=-1$, realising the boundary indicator).  Each factor has the
form $(a+b\,\sigma^C)$ with $a,b\ge 0$, so
$\texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_mul\_prod}$ shows the $+$ weight has non-negative
correlations ($\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_plus\_hasNonnegCorrelations}$), hence
$\langle\sigma^A\rangle^+_\Lambda \ge 0$
($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_spinProduct\_nonneg}$).  Reference:
Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.6, Theorem~3.49 (GKS-I, pp.~127--128).

\subsection{GKS-II for the $+$ boundary-condition state
(\texttt{Inequalities/GKSBoundaryConditionII.lean})}

The second Griffiths inequality for the $+$ boundary state,
$\langle\sigma^A\rangle^+_\Lambda\,\langle\sigma^B\rangle^+_\Lambda \le
\langle\sigma^{A\triangle B}\rangle^+_\Lambda$
($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_gks\_second}$), by the duplicate-variable argument
applied to the pinned weight $w^+ = w\cdot\mathrm{pin}$.  The change of variables
$\omega' = \varphi_t\omega$ ($(\varphi_t\omega)_i = \omega_i\cdot t_i$) \emph{collapses
the pinning}, $\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(\omega)\,\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(\varphi_t\omega) =
\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(\omega)\,\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(t)$
($\texttt{bcPin\_duplicate\_eq}$, from
$(\tfrac12+\tfrac12 a)(\tfrac12+\tfrac12 ab) = (\tfrac12+\tfrac12 a)(\tfrac12+\tfrac12
b)$ since $a^2=1$), so the doubled $+$ weight is
$w^+(\omega)\,w^+(\varphi_t\omega) =
\texttt{bcModExp}(t,\omega)\,\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(\omega)\,\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(t)$
($\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_plus\_duplicate\_eq}$), which has non-negative
correlations in $\omega$ ($\texttt{bcModifiedWeight\_nonneg\_corr}$: the exp-product is
HNC, times the $\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(\omega)$ product, times the non-negative constant
$\mathrm{pin}_\Lambda(t)$).  Mirrors the free-state $\texttt{gks\_second}$ and the
scaled-state $\texttt{scaledCorrelation\_gks\_second}$.  Reference: Friedli--Velenik
(Cambridge, 2017), \S3.6, Theorem~3.49 (GKS-II, pp.~127--128).

\subsection{Coupling monotonicity of the $+$ boundary correlation
(\texttt{Inequalities/MonotonicityJBoundaryCondition.lean})}

$\langle\sigma^B\rangle^+_\Lambda$ is monotone increasing in the uniform coupling $J$
(boundary analogue of $\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_J}$, Glimm--Jaffe Prop.~4.2.1).
The $+$-state covariance bound for an HNC factor $f$
($\texttt{cov\_hnc\_boltzmannBC\_nonneg}$) follows from the Walsh/Fourier expansion of
$f$ and the boundary GKS-II inequality $\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_gks\_second}$
(a mirror of $\texttt{cov\_hnc\_boltzmann\_nonneg}$).  The reweighting factor
$R(\sigma) = \exp(\beta(J_2-J_1)\sum\mathrm{edgeSpin})$ satisfies
$w^+_{J_2} = R\cdot w^+_{J_1}$ ($\texttt{boltzmannWeightBC\_plus\_reweight}$, via the
boundary indicator and $\texttt{boltzmannWeightJ\_uniform\_eq}$) and is HNC, giving the
$J$-reweighting inequality ($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_reweighting\_nonneg}$)
and hence the monotonicity ($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_monotone\_J}$).
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.6; Glimm--Jaffe Prop.~4.2.1.

\subsection{$\beta$-monotonicity of the $+$ boundary single-spin correlation
(\texttt{Inequalities/MonotonicityBetaBoundaryCondition.lean})}

$\langle\sigma_x\rangle^+_\Lambda$ is monotone increasing in the inverse temperature
$\beta$.  The rescaling identity $\langle F\rangle^+_{(J,h,\beta)} =
\langle F\rangle^+_{(\beta J,\beta h,1)}$
($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_beta\_rescale}$, the inverse temperature factoring into
the couplings while the boundary indicator is unchanged) reduces $\beta$-monotonicity
to the $J$-monotonicity ($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_plus\_monotone\_J}$) and the
$h$-monotonicity ($\texttt{gibbsExpectationBC\_field\_mono}$): increasing $\beta$ from
$\beta_1$ to $\beta_2$ moves $(\beta_1 J,\beta_1 h)$ to $(\beta_2 J,\beta_2 h)$ with
