($\texttt{mem\_iff\_odd\_cutCrossings}$, from $\texttt{even\_cutCrossings\_iff}$ with $g\notin
F$).  The crossing count depends only on $\mathrm{cut}(F)$ ($\texttt{cutCrossings\_congr}$), so if
$g\notin F_1,F_2$ and $\mathrm{cut}(F_1)=\mathrm{cut}(F_2)$ then every vertex has the same
membership in both, hence $F_1=F_2$ ($\texttt{eq\_of\_cutEdges\_eq}$).  Thus $\mathrm{cut}$ is
injective on sets avoiding $g$ ($\texttt{cutEdges\_injOn\_not\_mem\_ground}$), in particular on
filled regions ($\texttt{isFilled\_eq\_of\_cutEdges\_eq}$).  This is stronger than the
connected-droplet injectivity (only $g\notin F$ and preconnectedness, no connectedness of $F$),
and is the key to counting filled-region contours.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Directed coordinate edges and the 2D dual correspondence
  (\texttt{Peierls/GridEdge2.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The 2D Peierls contour $\mathrm{cut}(F)$ is connected not in the
primal graph but in the \emph{dual} lattice (edges sharing a unit square / face), which is again
$\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2$ on the faces.  To avoid the $\mathrm{Sym}_2$ quotient in the geometry,
a lattice edge is represented by a directed coordinate edge $\texttt{GridEdge2}$ (a $\texttt{base}$
and an $\texttt{axis}$, standing for the edge $\texttt{base}\to\texttt{base}+e_{\texttt{axis}}$,
with $\texttt{unitVec2}\,k := \texttt{Pi.single}\,k\,1$).  Each undirected lattice edge has a
unique such representative: $\texttt{toSym2}$ lands in $(\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2).\mathrm{edgeSet}$
($\texttt{toSym2\_isLatticeEdge}$, via $\texttt{latticeGraph\_adj\_add\_unitVec2}$) and is injective
($\texttt{toSym2\_injective}$, since two unit vectors never sum to zero).  The \emph{dual edge}
$\texttt{GridEdge2.dual}$ joins the two unit squares the primal edge separates, running along the
perpendicular axis ($\texttt{dual\_axis}$) and again a lattice edge
($\texttt{dual\_toSym2\_isLatticeEdge}$).  This is the entry point for transporting the primal cut
to a connected dual edge set, where the existing walk-counting applies.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Coordinate-edge bijection (\texttt{Peierls/GridEdge2Cut.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The representation is also surjective onto the lattice edges.  The
adjacency $\sum_i |x_i - y_i| = 1$ forces the endpoints to differ by a single unit vector
($\texttt{exists\_axis\_of\_adj}$: $y = x \pm e_k$), so every lattice edge is
$\texttt{GridEdge2.toSym2}$ of some directed coordinate edge
($\texttt{exists\_gridEdge2\_toSym2\_eq}$).  With $\texttt{toSym2\_injective}$ this yields the
bijection $\texttt{gridEdge2Equiv} : \texttt{GridEdge2} \simeq (\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2).
\mathrm{edgeSet}$ ($\texttt{gridEdge2\_toEdgeSet\_bijective}$).  The primal cut (a set of
$\mathrm{Sym}_2$ lattice edges) thus transports faithfully to a set of $\texttt{GridEdge2}$, to be
dualized for the contour count.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The dual edge map (\texttt{Peierls/DualCut.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} A finset $B$ of $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2$ edges (the primal cut,
lifted to the ambient lattice) is transported to its dual.  The dual map is injective
($\texttt{GridEdge2.dual\_injective}$, using that $\texttt{otherAxis}$ is an involution), and with
the partial inverse $\texttt{toGrid}$ of $\texttt{toSym2}$ on lattice edges
($\texttt{toGrid\_toSym2}$) one sets $\texttt{dualEdge}\,e := (\texttt{toGrid}\,e).\texttt{dual}.
\texttt{toSym2}$, injective on lattice edges ($\texttt{dualEdge\_injOn}$) and again a lattice edge
($\texttt{dualEdge\_mem\_edgeSet}$).  Hence $\texttt{dualEdges}\,B := B.\mathrm{image}\,
\texttt{dualEdge}$ preserves cardinality, $|\texttt{dualEdges}\,B| = |B| = r$
($\texttt{dualEdges\_card}$): the dual cut has the same size $r$ as the primal cut, and its
face-lattice connectivity (deferred) then bounds the contour count.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Lifting the box cut to the ambient lattice (\texttt{Peierls/LiftBoxCut.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The Peierls cut $\texttt{cutEdges}\,(\texttt{inducedGraph}\,
(\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2)\,\Lambda)\,F$ of a region $F$ in the box $\Lambda$ lives in
$\mathrm{Sym}_2\,\uparrow\!\Lambda$ (the box subtype), while the dual machinery is on the ambient
$\mathrm{Sym}_2\,(\mathrm{Fin}\,2 \to \mathbb{Z})$.  $\texttt{liftBoxCut}\,\Lambda\,F$ lifts each
box cut edge to an ambient lattice edge via $\mathrm{Sym}_2.\mathrm{map}\,\mathrm{Subtype.val}$;
each lifted edge is a lattice edge ($\texttt{liftBoxCut\_subset\_lattice}$) and the lift preserves
cardinality ($\texttt{liftBoxCut\_card}$, the inclusion being injective), so
$|\texttt{dualEdges}\,(\texttt{liftBoxCut}\,\Lambda\,F)| = |\texttt{cutEdges}\,F| = r$
($\texttt{dualEdges\_liftBoxCut\_card}$).  This resolves the box-subtype/ambient-lattice
impedance mismatch for the dual contour.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The Peierls contour is Eulerian (\texttt{Peierls/ContourEven.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} Each unit square (plaquette / dual vertex) of the 2D lattice has an
\emph{even} number of its four sides in the cut of $F$; in the dual lattice every face has even
degree in the dual contour.  This Eulerian property makes the boundary darts pair up, the local
foundation of the contour's connectedness (the discrete Jordan argument).  The proof is the
elementary parity fact that a cyclic binary sequence changes value an even number of times
($\texttt{cyclic4\_xor\_even}$): going around the four corners $c, c+e_0, c+e_0+e_1, c+e_1$, the
number of $F$-membership changes (= cut sides) is even
($\texttt{square\_split\_count\_even}$), and being at most $4$
($\texttt{square\_split\_count\_le\_four}$) it equals $0$, $2$, or $4$
($\texttt{square\_split\_count\_eq}$, the dart-pairing form).
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Directions and 90° rotation (\texttt{Peierls/Dir2.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The boundary-dart traversal walks the dual contour, turning $90^\circ$
at each step ("keep the wall on the left").  With $\texttt{rot90}\,v := (-v_1, v_0)$, a direction
$\texttt{Dir2} := \mathrm{Fin}\,4$ ranges over the four axis directions $\pm e_0, \pm e_1$, with
$\texttt{turnLeft}\,d := d+1$ and $\texttt{turnRight}\,d := d+3$.  These satisfy the turn algebra
($\texttt{turnLeft\_turnRight}$, $\texttt{turnRight\_turnLeft}$, $\texttt{turnLeft\_four}$, and
injectivity), and act on vectors by rotation: $(\texttt{turnLeft}\,d).\texttt{vec} = \texttt{rot90}
\,d.\texttt{vec}$ ($\texttt{vec\_turnLeft}$), with two left turns negating
($\texttt{vec\_turnLeft\_turnLeft}$).  This is the direction algebra underlying the boundary-dart
rule.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Oriented boundary darts (\texttt{Peierls/BoundaryDart.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} A boundary dart sits at a dual vertex $\texttt{tail}$, moves in
direction $\texttt{dir}$ (to $\texttt{tail}+\texttt{dir.vec}$), keeping $F$ on its \emph{left}.
The primal lattice points immediately left and right of the motion are $\texttt{leftSite}$ and
$\texttt{rightSite} = \texttt{leftSite} - (\texttt{turnLeft}\,\texttt{dir}).\texttt{vec}$; the
dart is \emph{valid} ($\texttt{ValidAt}$) when $\texttt{leftSite}\in F$ and $\texttt{rightSite}
\notin F$, and a $\texttt{BoundaryDart}\,F$ bundles $\texttt{tail}$, $\texttt{dir}$ with these
proofs (head $:= \texttt{tail}+\texttt{dir.vec}$).  The two sites are nearest neighbours
($\texttt{leftSite\_rightSite\_adjacent}$), so the crossed primal edge $\texttt{primalCutEdge}
:= s(\texttt{leftSite}, \texttt{rightSite})$ is a genuine cut edge for a valid dart
($\texttt{validAt\_edgeCrosses}$, $\texttt{edgeCrosses}\,F = \texttt{true}$).
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The boundary-dart turning rule (\texttt{Peierls/NextDart.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} At the head of a dart the contour continues by turning \emph{left},
going \emph{straight}, or turning \emph{right}, in that priority.  The crux
$\texttt{right\_valid\_of\_not\_left\_not\_straight}$ — if neither the left turn nor going straight
is valid, the right turn must be — is the local discrete-Jordan step that lets the traversal
continue without dead-ends.  It is proved by four site identities (each by $\texttt{fin\_cases}$ on
the direction): the incoming dart's left/right sites coincide with the candidate next sites, so
the incoming validity $\texttt{leftSite}\in F$, $\texttt{rightSite}\notin F$ propagates through
left $\to$ straight $\to$ right.  The next dart $\texttt{BoundaryDart.nextDart}$ takes the
highest-priority valid turn, and $\texttt{nextDart\_tail}$ shows it starts at the current head, so
the traversal advances continuously — the basis for closing the contour into a cycle.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Finiteness of boundary darts (\texttt{Peierls/DartFinite.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} For a fixed finite region $F$ there are only finitely many boundary
darts.  The left site is the tail plus a direction-dependent offset, $\texttt{leftSite}\,t\,\delta
= t + \texttt{leftSite}\,0\,\delta$ ($\texttt{leftSite\_eq}$), so it determines the tail
($\texttt{leftSite\_tail\_injective}$).  Hence $\texttt{BoundaryDart}\,F$ injects into
$\uparrow\!F \times \texttt{Dir2}$ and is a $\texttt{Fintype}$
($\texttt{instFintypeBoundaryDart}$).  Finiteness forces the $\texttt{nextDart}$ traversal to be
eventually periodic, closing the dart orbit into a cycle — the basis for the contour's
connectedness.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The reverse local step (\texttt{Peierls/DartStepReverse.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The traversal is locally reversible.  Since the left-turn left site
equals the incoming left site (in $F$), the left turn is valid iff its right site lies outside $F$
($\texttt{validAt\_turnLeft\_iff}$); dually the right turn is valid iff its left site lies in $F$
($\texttt{validAt\_turnRight\_iff}$).  Hence if neither the right turn nor going straight is valid,
the \emph{left} turn must be ($\texttt{left\_valid\_of\_not\_right\_not\_straight}$) — the mirror of
$\texttt{right\_valid\_of\_not\_left\_not\_straight}$, via the same four site identities.  Together
they show every continuation at the head is governed by the priority rule, the basis for the orbit
being a cycle.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The predecessor dart (\texttt{Peierls/PrevDart.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} Every dart has a unique predecessor.  Two further site identities
($\texttt{rightSite\_turnRight\_turnRight}$ and
$\texttt{rightSite\_turnRight\_eq\_leftSite\_turnLeft\_turnLeft}$) together with
$\texttt{validAt\_prev\_iff}$ (predecessor validity at $p$ reduces to head-sites at $p$) give
$\texttt{validAt\_prev\_candidates\_iff}$: each of the three candidate predecessor directions
($\texttt{turnRight}\,e.\texttt{dir}$, $e.\texttt{dir}$, $\texttt{turnLeft}\,e.\texttt{dir}$, all
ending at $e.\texttt{tail}$) is valid iff a single membership of the two points to the left of
$e.\texttt{tail}$ holds, the other site being fixed by $e$'s own validity.  Hence
$\texttt{BoundaryDart.prevDart}$ is a clean reverse-priority case split, and with
$\texttt{nextDart}\,(\texttt{prevDart}\,e) = e$ and finiteness, $\texttt{nextDart}$ is a bijection,
so the dart orbits are pure cycles.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Computing \texttt{nextDart} from validity (\texttt{Peierls/DartBijection.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} To evaluate the traversal once the candidate validities are known.
With the site identity $\texttt{rightSite}\,t\,(\texttt{turnLeft}\,\delta) = \texttt{leftSite}\,t\,
\delta$ ($\texttt{rightSite\_turnLeft}$) and dart extensionality ($\texttt{BoundaryDart.ext'}$,
darts agree when tail and direction agree), the reductions
$\texttt{nextDart\_eq\_turnLeft}$, $\texttt{nextDart\_eq\_straight}$,
$\texttt{nextDart\_eq\_turnRight}$ express $\texttt{nextDart}$ as the first valid continuation (via
$\texttt{dif\_pos}/\texttt{dif\_neg}$).  These feed the proof that $\texttt{prevDart}$ is a right
inverse of $\texttt{nextDart}$, hence — by finiteness — $\texttt{nextDart}$ is a bijection and the
orbits are cycles.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{\texttt{nextDart} is a bijection (\texttt{Peierls/DartBijective.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} Every dart $e$ is the $\texttt{nextDart}$ of its predecessor
($\texttt{nextDart\_surjective}$): constructing the predecessor by the reverse priority (the three
cases of $\texttt{validAt\_prev\_candidates\_iff}$), the forward step — via the
$\texttt{nextDart\_eq\_*}$ reductions, $\texttt{rightSite\_turnLeft}$ and $e$'s own validity —
returns exactly $e$.  A surjective endofunction of the finite type $\texttt{BoundaryDart}\,F$ is
bijective ($\texttt{nextDart\_bijective}$), so $\texttt{nextDart}$ is a permutation of the darts:
every dart lies on a closed orbit, the combinatorial discrete Jordan curve giving the contour
cycle, the basis for the volume-independent contour count.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The dart orbit is a dual-lattice cycle (\texttt{Peierls/DartOrbit.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} Each traversal step moves along a unit dual edge.  A step in any
direction is a lattice adjacency ($\texttt{latticeGraph\_adj\_dirVec}$: $t$ and $t+\delta.
\texttt{vec}$ are adjacent in $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2$), so a dart's tail and head are adjacent
($\texttt{BoundaryDart.tail\_adj\_head}$).  Since $\texttt{nextDart}$ is a bijection of the finite
dart type, every dart returns to itself under iteration ($\texttt{nextDart\_periodic}$, by
pigeonhole and injectivity of the iterate).  The orbit is thus a closed walk in
$\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2$, which the degree-based walk count bounds — the route to the
volume-independent contour count.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The orbit as an explicit closed walk (\texttt{Peierls/DartOrbitWalk.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The sequence of dart tails is realised as an honest
$\texttt{SimpleGraph.Walk}$ in $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2$.  $\texttt{orbitWalk}\,d\,n$ walks along
the tails of the first $n$ darts of the forward orbit (built by $\texttt{Walk.concat}$ and
$\texttt{Walk.copy}$ over $\texttt{tail\_adj\_head}$ and $\texttt{nextDart\_tail}$), of length $n$
($\texttt{orbitWalk\_length}$).  Over a full period ($\texttt{nextDart}^{[n]}\,d = d$, from
$\texttt{nextDart\_periodic}$), $\texttt{orbitClosedWalk}$ is a closed walk $d.\texttt{tail}\to
d.\texttt{tail}$ of length $n$ ($\texttt{orbitClosedWalk\_length}$).  Bounding the number of such
closed walks (by the degree count $\texttt{walksFromCount\_le\_pow}$) is the final combinatorial
input to the contour count.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Counting closed walks in the box (\texttt{Peierls/ClosedWalkCount.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The number of closed walks of length $k$ from a vertex $v$ in the
induced box graph $\texttt{inducedGraph}\,(\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d)\,\Lambda$ is at most $(2d)^k$
($\texttt{closedWalkCount\_le}$): closed walks are among all walks from $v$, whose total
$\texttt{walksFromCount}$ is $\le (2d)^k$ by $\texttt{walksFromCount\_inducedLatticeGraph\_le}$, and
$\texttt{finsetWalkLength}\,k\,v\,v$ is a single term of the endpoint sum.  This is the counting
engine for the Peierls contour bound: a dart orbit of length $k$ is a closed walk, so the number of
contours of a given length near a fixed vertex is geometric in the length.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{The low-temperature Peierls tail vanishes (\texttt{Peierls/LowTempTail.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The contour bound gives $\mu^{+}(\sigma_0 = -1) \le \sum_{r\ge 1} C^r
e^{-2\beta J r} = q/(1-q)$ with $q(\beta) = C\,e^{-2\beta J}$.  As $\beta\to\infty$ (with $J>0$)
the rate vanishes, $C\,e^{-2\beta J}\to 0$ ($\texttt{lowTempRate\_tendsto\_zero}$), hence
$q/(1-q)\to 0$ ($\texttt{peierls\_low\_temp\_tail\_tendsto\_zero}$).  This is the analytic input to
the low-temperature spontaneous magnetisation $m^*(\beta)>0$: the opposite-spin probability is
squeezed to $0$.  (The high-temperature counterpart took the $n\to\infty$ box limit; here the limit
is $\beta\to\infty$.)
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\subsection*{Edge-connectivity of the dual cut from the planar bond lemma
(\texttt{Peierls/PlanarBondReduction.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Role:} The convergent re-foundation of the contour edge-connectivity crux,
replacing the non-converging \texttt{rayExitAnchorDartMap} first-exit anchor route.  The first-exit
index of a rightward ray is discontinuous across a vertical step, so the anchor transport
obligations \texttt{hstep}/\texttt{hanchor} disguise the global discrete-Jordan separation fact as
an infinite regress of local case-splits.  The correct factoring isolates the single genuine
obligation as the \emph{planar bond hypothesis}
\[
  \texttt{PlanarBondHypothesis}\,F \;:\;
  \forall d\,e,\;
  \texttt{ReachableWithin}\,(\texttt{latticeGraph}\,2)\,F\;d.\mathrm{left}\;e.\mathrm{left}
  \;\to\;
  \texttt{ReachableOutside}\,F\;d.\mathrm{right}\;e.\mathrm{right}
  \;\to\;
  \texttt{DartReachable}\,F\;d\;e,
\]
i.e.\ two boundary darts whose inside endpoints are connected inside $F$ and whose outside endpoints
are connected in the complement of $F$ have edge-connected dual edges.  Here
$\texttt{ReachableOutside}\,F$ is the reflexive-transitive closure of complement-adjacency
($a\sim b$ with $a,b\notin F$); it carries no \texttt{Fintype} requirement, since the lattice
complement $\mathbb{Z}^2\setminus F$ is infinite (so $\texttt{univ}\setminus F$ is not a
\texttt{Finset}).  Given the bond hypothesis, \texttt{dartReachable\_of\_bond} feeds it the inside
$F$-connectivity and the outside complement-connectivity to obtain pairwise dart reachability, and
\texttt{dartDualCut\_isEdgeConnected\_of\_bond} /
\texttt{dualCutSub\_isEdgeConnected\_of\_bond} /
\texttt{dualCutInBox\_isEdgeConnected\_of\_bond} give whole-cut, subtype, and common-box
edge-connectivity via the already-proved \texttt{dartDualCut\_isEdgeConnected\_of\_dartReachable} and
the subtype/image bridges.  Both connectivity premises are already available for filled connected
droplets (\texttt{isConnectedDroplet\_filledRegion} and
\texttt{reachableWithin\_compl\_of\_isFilled}).  The contour count consumes this through
\texttt{peierls\_contour\_count\_of\_bond} (parallel to \texttt{peierls\_contour\_count\_anchored},
with the single-orbit \texttt{hone} input replaced by per-droplet bond and connectivity data).
\textbf{Status: Partial} --- the bond lemma itself is the single remaining open obligation (the
genuine discrete-Jordan separation content).
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (Cambridge, 2017), \S3.7.2, pp. 109--116.

\section{Asano Contraction (\texttt{Asano.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} None (self-contained complex analysis).

\textbf{Role:} Defines \texttt{MultilinPoly} (multilinear polynomials
over $\mathbb{C}$) and the Asano contraction operation. This is the
algebraic engine behind the Lee-Yang theorem.

\textbf{What to look for:} \texttt{MultilinPoly.eval} and
\texttt{asanoContract}. The key theorem is that contraction
preserves nonvanishing on the unit polydisk.

The Asano contraction merges two variables in a multilinear polynomial,
keeping only the ``both present'' and ``both absent'' parts.
It is an independent result in algebraic combinatorics; our Lee-Yang proof
(Section~\ref{sec:lee-yang}) uses the Harcos/Ruelle approach instead.

Reference: \cite[Proposition~3.44, pp.~123--124]{friedli-velenik}.

\begin{definition}[Multilinear polynomial]
A multilinear polynomial over $\mathbb{C}$ with variables indexed by a
finite type $\iota$ is a function $p : \mathcal{P}(\iota) \to \mathbb{C}$,
evaluated as $p(z) = \sum_{X \subseteq \iota} p(X) \prod_{i \in X} z_i$.
In Lean: \texttt{Finset $\iota$ $\to$ $\mathbb{C}$}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Asano contraction]
Given $p$ and distinct $i, j \in \iota$, the contraction of $j$ into $i$
is $q(X) = p(X \cup \{j\})$ if $i \in X$ and $j \notin X$;
$q(X) = p(X)$ if $i \notin X$ and $j \notin X$;
$q(X) = 0$ if $j \in X$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Asano contraction preserves non-vanishing]
\label{thm:asano}
If $p$ does not vanish on the open unit polydisk
$\{z : |z_k| < 1\;\forall k\}$, then neither does its Asano contraction.
Reference: \cite[Proposition~3.44, pp.~123--124]{friedli-velenik}.
\end{theorem}

The proof uses a bilinear non-vanishing lemma:

\begin{lemma}[Bilinear non-vanishing]
If $f(z,w) = azw + bw + cz + d \neq 0$ for all $|z|, |w| < 1$,
then $az + d \neq 0$ for all $|z| < 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Show $\|a\| \leq \|d\|$ via the parallelogram law.
For $|z'| < 1$, the affine function $w \mapsto (az'+b)w + (cz'+d)$
has no zero with $|w| < 1$, giving $\|az'+b\| \leq \|cz'+d\|$.
Squaring and averaging at $z' = \pm t$ (real) via the parallelogram law:
$\mathrm{normSq}(a) \cdot t^2 + \mathrm{normSq}(b) \leq
\mathrm{normSq}(c) \cdot t^2 + \mathrm{normSq}(d)$.
Combining the $z$- and $w$-directions and applying a linear function argument
on $[0,1)$ yields $\mathrm{normSq}(a) \leq \mathrm{normSq}(d)$,
hence $\|a\| \leq \|d\|$. Then $az + d = 0$ would require
$|z| = |d/a| \geq 1$, contradicting $|z| < 1$.
\end{proof}

The contraction theorem follows by decomposing the polynomial evaluation
$p(z[i \to u, j \to w])$ as a bilinear form $auw + bw + cu + d$ in $(u, w)$,
where the contraction's evaluation equals $a \cdot z_i + d$.
The decomposition uses a product extraction lemma
(\texttt{prod\_upd}) and a sum reindexing via the involution
$X \mapsto X \triangle \{j\}$ (\texttt{Fintype.sum\_equiv}).

\begin{remark}
When Mathlib provides a native implementation of Asano contraction or
multilinear polynomials, the definitions here should be replaced.
\end{remark}

\section{Lee-Yang circle theorem (\texttt{LeeYang.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{Asano.lean} (for the
\texttt{MultilinPoly} type only; Asano contraction is \emph{not} used).

\textbf{Role:} Proves that the Ising partition polynomial has no
zeros on the open unit polydisk via the Harcos/Ruelle approach.

\textbf{What to look for:} The proof uses a Hermitian matrix formulation,
induction on $n$, and the maximum modulus principle --- not Asano contraction.
Key steps: (1) define \texttt{leeYangPoly} for Hermitian $A$ with
$|a_{ij}| \le 1$; (2) torus identity relating $\alpha$ and
$\overline{\beta}$; (3) induction eliminating the last variable;
(4) maximum modulus to bound $|\beta/\alpha|$ on the polydisk.
\texttt{lee\_yang\_circle} is the final theorem.
\label{sec:lee-yang}

The Lee-Yang circle theorem states that the Ising partition polynomial
has no zeros on the open unit polydisk. Our formalization follows the
Harcos/Ruelle approach~\cite{harcos, ruelle}.

\begin{definition}[Lee-Yang polynomial]
For an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ over $\mathbb{C}$, define
\[
  f_A(z) = \sum_{S\subseteq [n]}
    \Bigl(\prod_{i\in S}\prod_{j\notin S} a_{ij}\Bigr)\prod_{k\in S} z_k.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ruelle~{\cite[Theorem~1, p.~589]{ruelle}};
  Harcos~{\cite[Theorem~3, p.~2]{harcos}};
  \texttt{leeYangPoly\_nonvanishing}]
If $A$ is Hermitian with $|a_{ij}|\le 1$, then $f_A(z)\ne 0$
for all $z$ with $|z_k|<1$.
\end{theorem}

The proof is by induction on $n$. The inductive step decomposes
$f_A(z)=\beta + z_n\cdot\alpha$ and shows $\|\alpha\|\le\|\beta\|$
via:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Torus identity} (\texttt{torus\_identity}):
  On $|v_k|=1$,
  $\alpha(v) = (\prod v_k)\cdot\overline{\beta(v)}$,
  hence $\|\alpha\|=\|\beta\|$.
\item \textbf{Approximation}: Scale the last column by $t<1$
  so that $\beta_t\ne 0$ on the closed polydisk.
\item \textbf{Iterated max modulus} (\texttt{iterated\_ratio}):
  By single-variable maximum modulus
  (\texttt{one\_var\_max\_ratio}, via \texttt{DiffContOnCl}),
  iterate over each variable to get $\|\alpha_t/\beta_t\|\le 1$.
\item \textbf{Limit $t\to 1$}: Both sides are continuous in $t$;
  $\{t:\|\alpha_t\|\le\|\beta_t\|\}$ is closed and contains
  $[0,1)$, hence contains~$1$.
\end{enumerate}

The Ising application (\texttt{lee\_yang\_circle}) constructs a
Hermitian matrix from the edge list and coupling constants, reducing
the combinatorial Ising model to the matrix formulation.

\section{Infinite volume limit (\texttt{InfiniteVolume.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{GKS.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Proves boundedness ($|\langle\sigma^A\rangle| \le 1$),
monotonicity in $J$ and $h$, and convergence of correlations.
Also contains the Walsh--Fourier inversion theorem.

\textbf{What to look for:} \texttt{abs\_correlation\_le\_one} (used
everywhere), \texttt{correlation\_monotone\_J/H} (used for free energy
monotonicity), and the covariance non-negativity lemma
\texttt{cov\_hnc\_boltzmann\_nonneg}.

The convergence of correlation functions as the lattice grows to infinity.
Reference: \cite[{\S4.2, pp.~58--59}]{glimm-jaffe}.

\begin{proposition}[\texttt{abs\_correlation\_le\_one}, Proposition 4.2.2, p.~58]
For the Ising model, $|\langle\sigma^A\rangle| \le 1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$|\sigma^A| = 1$ (since $\sigma_i = \pm 1$), so
$|\langle\sigma^A\rangle| \le \langle|\sigma^A|\rangle = 1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{cov\_hnc\_boltzmann\_nonneg};
  cf.\ \cite{glimm-jaffe}, {\S4.2, p.~58}]
\label{thm:cov-hnc}
For an HNC function $f$ and ferromagnetic Boltzmann weight $w$,
\[
  \Bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^B f(\sigma) w(\sigma)\Bigr)
  \Bigl(\sum_\sigma w(\sigma)\Bigr)
  \ge
  \Bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^B w(\sigma)\Bigr)
  \Bigl(\sum_\sigma f(\sigma) w(\sigma)\Bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fourier expand $f(\sigma) = \sum_S \hat{c}_S \sigma^S$ where
$\hat{c}_S = |\iota|^{-1} \sum_\tau \sigma^S(\tau) f(\tau) \ge 0$
by HNC (\texttt{walsh\_fourier\_inversion}).
Then $\sigma^B f(\sigma) = \sum_S \hat{c}_S \sigma^{B \triangle S}$
using $\sigma^B \sigma^S = \sigma^{B \triangle S}$ (\texttt{spinProduct\_mul}).
The covariance becomes $\sum_S \hat{c}_S \cdot \text{bracket}_S$ where
\[
  \text{bracket}_S =
  \Bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^{B\triangle S} w\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_\sigma w\Bigr)
  - \Bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^B w\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^S w\Bigr).
\]
Since $\hat{c}_S \ge 0$ and $\text{bracket}_S = Z^2(\langle\sigma^{B\triangle S}\rangle
- \langle\sigma^B\rangle\langle\sigma^S\rangle) \ge 0$ by GKS-II
(\texttt{gks\_second}; \cite[Theorem~3.49, p.~127]{friedli-velenik}),
each term is non-negative.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_J}, Proposition 4.2.1, p.~58]
$\langle\sigma^B\rangle$ is monotone increasing in $J$ on $[0,\infty)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $0 \le J_1 \le J_2$, define the reweighting factor
$R(\sigma) = \prod_e \exp(\beta(J_2 - J_1)\,\text{edgeSpin}(\sigma,e))$.
Then $\exp(-\beta H_{J_2}(\sigma)) = R(\sigma)\exp(-\beta H_{J_1}(\sigma))$
(\texttt{correlation\_reweighting\_nonneg}), and $R$ has HNC by
\texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_edge\_site\_product} since all edge
coefficients $\beta(J_2 - J_1) \ge 0$.
The algebraic identity
$\langle\sigma^B\rangle_{J_2} - \langle\sigma^B\rangle_{J_1}
= [\text{num}_2\,\text{den}_1 - \text{num}_1\,\text{den}_2]
  / (\text{den}_1\,\text{den}_2)$
reduces to a covariance of $R$ with $\sigma^B$ under the $J_1$ Boltzmann
weight, which is $\ge 0$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:cov-hnc}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Walsh orthogonality and Fourier inversion}

The spin products $\{\sigma^S : S \subseteq \iota\}$ form an orthogonal
basis for functions on $\mathrm{Config}\;\iota = \iota \to \{+1,-1\}$.

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{walsh\_orthogonality}]
For $S \ne T$, $\sum_\sigma \sigma^S \sigma^T = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\sigma^S \sigma^T = \sigma^{S \triangle T}$ by \texttt{spinProduct\_mul}.
Since $S \ne T$, $S \triangle T \ne \emptyset$, so
$\sum_\sigma \sigma^{S \triangle T} = 0$ by the flip involution
(\texttt{sum\_config\_spinProduct\_eq\_zero}).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[\texttt{walsh\_normalization}]
$\sum_\sigma (\sigma^S)^2 = 2^{|\iota|}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$(\sigma^S)^2 = \sigma^{S \triangle S} = \sigma^\emptyset = 1$.
So $\sum_\sigma 1 = |\mathrm{Config}\;\iota| = 2^{|\iota|}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{walsh\_completeness}]
$\sum_S \sigma^S(\tau) \cdot \sigma^S(\sigma) =
\begin{cases} 2^{|\iota|} & \text{if } \sigma = \tau, \\
0 & \text{if } \sigma \ne \tau. \end{cases}$
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Define $\omega_i = \sigma_i \cdot \tau_i$ (componentwise spin
multiplication). Then $\sigma^S(\tau) \cdot \sigma^S(\sigma)
= \omega^S$ by \texttt{Spin.toSign\_mul}. The sum
$\sum_S \omega^S = \prod_i (1 + \omega_i)$ by
\texttt{Finset.prod\_add\_one}. If $\sigma = \tau$ then each
$\omega_i = +1$ so each factor is $2$; if $\sigma \ne \tau$
then $\exists i$ with $\omega_i = -1$ so the product vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{walsh\_fourier\_inversion}]
Any $f : \mathrm{Config}\;\iota \to \mathbb{R}$ has the expansion
$f(\sigma) = \sum_S \hat{c}_S \sigma^S$ where
$\hat{c}_S = 2^{-|\iota|} \sum_\tau \sigma^S(\tau) f(\tau)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Substitute the expansion and apply Walsh completeness:
\[
  \sum_S \hat{c}_S \sigma^S(\sigma)
  = 2^{-|\iota|} \sum_\tau f(\tau)
    \underbrace{\sum_S \sigma^S(\tau) \sigma^S(\sigma)}_{= \, 2^{|\iota|} [\tau = \sigma]}
  = f(\sigma).
\]
This uses \texttt{Finset.sum\_comm} to swap the order of summation
and \texttt{walsh\_completeness} for the Kronecker delta.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_convergent},
  Theorem 4.2.3, \cite{glimm-jaffe}, p.~59]
For $h \ge 0$ and $\beta > 0$, the sequence
$n \mapsto \langle\sigma^B\rangle_{(G, n, h, \beta)}$ converges.
The limit equals $\sup_n \langle\sigma^B\rangle_{(G, n, h, \beta)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The sequence $n \mapsto \langle\sigma^B\rangle_{(G, n, h, \beta)}$ is:
\begin{itemize}
  \item monotone increasing by Proposition~4.2.1
    (\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_J});
  \item bounded above by $1$ since
    $\langle\sigma^B\rangle \le |\langle\sigma^B\rangle| \le 1$
    (\texttt{correlationJ\_le\_one} via \texttt{abs\_correlation\_le\_one}).
\end{itemize}
By the monotone convergence theorem (\texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciSup}),
the sequence converges to $\sup_n \langle\sigma^B\rangle_{(G, n, h, \beta)}$.
\end{proof}

Auxiliary results:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{correlationJ\_nonneg}: $\langle\sigma^B\rangle \ge 0$
    for $J \ge 0$ (from GKS-I).
  \item \texttt{correlationJ\_le\_one}: $\langle\sigma^B\rangle \le 1$
    (from $|\langle\sigma^B\rangle| \le 1$).
\end{itemize}

$\mathbb{Z}^d$ direct wrappers
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation.lean}):
\texttt{correlationJ\_\{nonneg,le\_one\}\_latticeGraph} and
\texttt{correlation\_convergent\{,\_h,\_beta\}\_latticeGraph}
are thin pass-throughs of the above at the
\texttt{Ambient.inducedGraph (latticeGraph d)\,$\Lambda$}
subgraph on any finite $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$.
Only \texttt{correlation\_convergent\_latticeGraph} is the direct
GJ~\S4.2 Thm.~4.2.3 specialization ($J \to \infty$ along $\mathbb{N}$);
\texttt{correlation\_convergent\_h\_latticeGraph} is its
Prop.~4.2.4 companion ($h \to \infty$), and
\texttt{correlation\_convergent\_beta\_latticeGraph} is a repo-internal
monotone-bounded extension in $\beta \to \infty$ (not in GJ).

Parallel $\mathbb{Z}^d$ wrappers for the derived \S5 quantities
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MagnetizationConvergent.lean},
narrowed out of \texttt{Magnetization.lean} in PR~\#2030):
\texttt{magnetization\_convergent\_\{J,h,beta\}\_latticeGraph},
\texttt{truncated2\_convergent\_\{J,h,beta,subgraph\}\_latticeGraph},
\texttt{susceptibility\_convergent\_subgraph\_latticeGraph}, and
\texttt{magnetization\_total\_convergent\_subgraph\_latticeGraph}
pass through the abstract
\texttt{IsingModel.\{magnetization,truncated2,susceptibility,magnetization\_total\}\_convergent\_*}
(\texttt{IsingModel/PhaseTransition.lean}). The $J,h,\beta$ wrappers
fix the graph to \texttt{Ambient.inducedGraph (latticeGraph d)\,$\Lambda$};
the \texttt{\_subgraph} wrappers only fix $\iota = \operatorname{\uparrow}\Lambda$
(the subgraph parameter $G_n$ on the $\Lambda$-induced type remains
unconstrained and is \emph{not} forced to be $\le$ \texttt{latticeGraph d}).

Susceptibility family (GJ \S5.3, pp.~77–80) at $\mathbb{Z}^d$
(\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/MagnetizationSusceptibility.lean},
narrowed out of \texttt{Magnetization.lean} in PR~\#2004):
\texttt{susceptibility\_\{apply,nonneg,J\_zero,beta\_zero\}\_latticeGraph}
and \texttt{susceptibility\_convergent\_\{J,h,beta\}\_latticeGraph}
are thin pass-throughs of the abstract
\texttt{IsingModel.susceptibility\_*} on
\texttt{Ambient.inducedGraph (latticeGraph d)\,$\Lambda$}. The
$J=0$ closed form reads $\chi_i = t(1-t)$ with $t = \tanh(\beta h)$,
inheriting the Finset-based \texttt{truncated2} diagonal caveat
($\{i,i\}$ collapses to $\{i\}$, so the term is $t - t^2$ rather
than the physical $1 - t^2$). In the same batch,
\texttt{eta\_nonneg\_finite\_vol\_latticeGraph} is the
finite-volume slice of GJ Thm~17.7.1 ($\eta \ge 0$) at
$\mathbb{Z}^d$, derived from GKS-II via
\texttt{truncated2\_nonneg}.

{\raggedright
The concrete $\mathbb{Z}^d$ Lambda-layer susceptibility regularity and
parameter-direction convergence wrappers now live in
\path{IsingModel/Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/SusceptibilityLambda.lean}.
\par}

\begin{remark}
The original Glimm--Jaffe formulation uses lattice growth
$\Lambda \uparrow \mathbb{Z}^d$. In the finite-volume setting,
this reduces to increasing coupling constants from $0$ to $J$.
The lattice-growth version ($\Lambda \uparrow$) is formalized
below via the subgraph order on a fixed ambient lattice.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Lattice-growth version of Theorem 4.2.3}

The Glimm--Jaffe proof of Theorem~4.2.3 reads
``increasing $\Lambda$ amounts to increasing certain $J_A$,
and so $\langle\xi^B\rangle$ is monotone increasing in $\Lambda$''.
We formalize this by taking a fixed ambient \texttt{Fintype} $\iota$
and working with subgraphs $G_1 \le G_2$ of the interaction graph:
new edges $e \in E(G_2) \setminus E(G_1)$ correspond exactly to the
coupling $J_A$ going from $0$ to $\beta J$.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_subgraph},
  Theorem 4.2.3 (lattice version), \cite{glimm-jaffe}, p.~59]
For a ferromagnetic Ising model on the ambient lattice $\iota$
and subgraphs $G_1 \le G_2$,
$\langle \sigma^A\rangle_{G_1} \le \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{G_2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $R(\sigma) := \prod_{e \in E(G_2)\setminus E(G_1)} \exp(\beta J \sigma_i\sigma_j)$.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Factorization.} Since $H_{G_2}(\sigma) - H_{G_1}(\sigma) = -J\sum_{E(G_2)\setminus E(G_1)} \sigma_i\sigma_j$,
    we have $w_{G_2}(\sigma) = R(\sigma)\, w_{G_1}(\sigma)$
    (\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_subgraph\_factor}).
  \item \textbf{HNC.} Each factor decomposes as $\cosh(\beta J) + \sinh(\beta J)\,\sigma_i\sigma_j$
    with both coefficients $\ge 0$; by
    \texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_finset\_prod},
    $R$ has non-negative correlations
    (\texttt{hasNonnegCorrelations\_edge\_prod\_of\_finset}).
  \item \textbf{Covariance.} Apply \texttt{cov\_hnc\_boltzmann\_nonneg}
    with base graph $G_1$ and function $R$:
    \[
      \bigl(\textstyle\sum_\sigma \sigma^A R(\sigma) w_1\bigr)Z_{G_1}
      \ge \bigl(\sum_\sigma \sigma^A w_1\bigr)\bigl(\sum_\sigma R(\sigma) w_1\bigr).
    \]
    Substituting $R w_1 = w_2$ yields $Z_{G_1} N_{G_2}(A) \ge Z_{G_2} N_{G_1}(A)$,
    i.e., $\langle\sigma^A\rangle_{G_1} \le \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{G_2}$.
\end{itemize}
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_convergent\_subgraph}]
For any increasing sequence of subgraphs $G_1 \le G_2 \le \cdots$ of the ambient lattice,
the correlation sequence $n \mapsto \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{G_n}$ converges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotone increasing by \texttt{correlation\_monotone\_subgraph},
bounded above by $1$ via \texttt{correlation\_le\_one}, hence converges by
\texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciSup}.
\end{proof}

Named specializations:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{magnetization\_convergent\_subgraph}: $\langle\sigma_i\rangle_{G_n}$
        converges (case $A = \{i\}$).
  \item \texttt{twoPoint\_convergent\_subgraph}: $\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle_{G_n}$
        converges (case $A = \{i,j\}$).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Free energy infinite volume convergence (Proposition 4.6.1)}

GJ Proposition 4.6.1 (p.~68): for the ferromagnetic pair interaction
$H = -J\sum_{\langle i,j\rangle}\sigma_i\sigma_j - h\sum_i\sigma_i$
(strictly ferromagnetic), the free energy per site
$f_\Lambda = |\Lambda|^{-1}\ln Z_\Lambda$ converges as $\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb{Z}^d$.
The discretized (fixed ambient lattice $\iota$, growing subgraph) form:

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_subgraph}]
For ferromagnetic $p$ and $G_1\le G_2$, $Z_{G_1}\le Z_{G_2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Factor $Z_{G_2} = \sum_\sigma R(\sigma) w_{G_1}(\sigma)$ with
$R(\sigma)=\prod_{e\in E(G_2)\setminus E(G_1)}\exp(\beta J \sigma_i\sigma_j)$.
Use $\exp(x)\ge 1+x$ to get
$R(\sigma)\ge 1 + \beta J \sum_{e\in E(G_2)\setminus E(G_1)}\sigma_i\sigma_j$.
Then $\sum_\sigma R w_{G_1} \ge Z_{G_1} + \beta J \sum_e \sum_\sigma \sigma_i\sigma_j w_{G_1}$,
and each inner sum is $\ge 0$ by GKS-I (via \texttt{boltzmannWeight\_hasNonnegCorrelations})
applied to the pair $\{i,j\}$. Hence $Z_{G_2}\ge Z_{G_1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_subgraph}]
For ferromagnetic $p$ and $G_1\le G_2$, $f_{G_1}\le f_{G_2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$|\iota|$ is fixed; apply $\log$ (monotone) to $Z_{G_1}\le Z_{G_2}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{$\beta$-monotonicity and $\beta \to \infty$ convergence}{beta-monotonicity and beta to infinity convergence}}

Rescale identities:
\[
  \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{(J,h,\beta)} = \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{(\beta J, \beta h, 1)}
  \quad\text{(\texttt{correlation\_rescale\_beta})}
\]
\[
  f(J,h,\beta) = f(\beta J, \beta h, 1)
  \quad\text{(\texttt{freeEnergy\_rescale\_beta})}
\]

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_beta}]
For $J, h \ge 0$, the correlation function is monotone increasing in
$\beta$ on $(0, \infty)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the rescale identity; then $\beta_1 \le \beta_2$ gives
$\beta_1 J \le \beta_2 J$ and $\beta_1 h \le \beta_2 h$ at both
endpoints.  Apply \texttt{correlation\_monotone\_J} and
\texttt{correlation\_monotone\_h}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_convergent\_beta}]
For $J, h \ge 0$ and any finite set $A$, the sequence
$\langle\sigma^A\rangle_{(J,h,n+1)}$ converges as $n \to \infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotone by \texttt{correlation\_monotone\_beta}, bounded above by
$1$ via \texttt{correlation\_le\_one}. Converges by
\texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciSup}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_beta}]
For $J, h \ge 0$, the free energy $f(J,h,\beta)$ is monotone in $\beta$
on $(0,\infty)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply the rescale identity, then \texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_J} and
\texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_h}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The free energy does not converge as $\beta\to\infty$
(it grows linearly in $\beta$, since $\log Z \sim \beta(J|E| + h|\iota|)$
at low temperature).
\end{remark}

Specializations to magnetization:
\texttt{magnetization\_monotone\_beta},
\texttt{magnetization\_convergent\_beta} (both via $A = \{i\}$).

\subsection{Convergence as \texorpdfstring{$h \to \infty$}{h to infinity}}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_convergent\_h}]
For $J \ge 0$, $\beta > 0$, the sequence
$n \mapsto \langle\sigma^A\rangle_{(J,n,\beta)}$ converges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotone by \texttt{correlation\_monotone\_h} (Prop.~4.2.4),
bounded above by $1$ via \texttt{correlation\_le\_one}.
Apply \texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciSup}.
\end{proof}

Specialization: \texttt{magnetization\_convergent\_h} via $A = \{i\}$.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_convergent\_subgraph}, = Prop 4.6.1]
For any increasing subgraph sequence $G_n\uparrow$ on a fixed finite ambient
lattice $\iota$ and ferromagnetic $p$, $n\mapsto f_{G_n}$ converges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Monotone by \texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_subgraph}.
Bounded above by $f_{\top}$ (free energy on the complete graph $\top$)
via \texttt{le\_top}. Converges by \texttt{tendsto\_atTop\_ciSup}.
\end{proof}

\section{Free energy (\texttt{FreeEnergy.lean})}

The free energy and its monotonicity properties.
Reference: \cite[{\S4.6, pp.~67--70}]{glimm-jaffe}.

\begin{definition}[\texttt{freeEnergy}, (4.6.1), p.~67]
The free energy per site: $f = |\iota|^{-1} \ln Z$.
Well-defined since $Z > 0$ (\texttt{partitionFunction\_pos}).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_h};
  cf.\ \cite{glimm-jaffe}, {\S4.6, p.~67}]
For $J \ge 0$, $\beta > 0$, $0 \le h_1 \le h_2$:
$Z(J, h_1, \beta) \le Z(J, h_2, \beta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Rewrite $Z(h_2) = \sum_\sigma R(\sigma) w_1(\sigma)$ where
$R(\sigma) = \prod_i \exp(\beta(h_2-h_1)\,\text{sign}(\sigma_i))$ and
$w_1 = e^{-\beta H_{h_1}}$.
Using $\exp(x) \ge 1 + x$:
\[
  R(\sigma) = \exp\Bigl(\beta(h_2 - h_1)\sum_i \sigma_i\Bigr)
  \ge 1 + \beta(h_2 - h_1)\sum_i \sigma_i.
\]
Multiply by $w_1(\sigma)$ and sum:
$Z(h_2) \ge Z(h_1) + \beta(h_2-h_1)\sum_i Z(h_1)\langle\sigma_i\rangle_{h_1}$.
By GKS-I (\texttt{boltzmannWeight\_hasNonnegCorrelations}):
$\langle\sigma_i\rangle_{h_1} \ge 0$ for each $i$, so
$Z(h_2) \ge Z(h_1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_J};
  cf.\ \cite{glimm-jaffe}, {\S4.6, p.~67}]
For $h \ge 0$, $\beta > 0$, $0 \le J_1 \le J_2$:
$Z(J_1, h, \beta) \le Z(J_2, h, \beta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Same technique as $h$-monotonicity with
$R(\sigma) = \exp(\beta(J_2-J_1)\sum_e \sigma_i\sigma_j)$.
Using $\exp(x) \ge 1+x$ and GKS-I
($\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \ge 0$ for each edge).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_h}, \texttt{freeEnergy\_monotone\_J}]
The free energy $f = |\iota|^{-1}\ln Z$ is monotone increasing
in $h$ on $[0,\infty)$ and in $J$ on $[0,\infty)$.
Immediate from $Z$ monotonicity and $\ln$ monotonicity
(\texttt{Real.log\_le\_log}).
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Free energy analyticity (Theorem 4.6.2)}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunctionH\_analyticAt}]
The partition function $Z(h) = \sum_\sigma \exp(a(\sigma) + b(\sigma) h)$
is real-analytic in $h$ at every point.  Each Boltzmann weight
$\exp(a + bh)$ is real-analytic (exponential of affine),
and a finite sum of real-analytic functions is real-analytic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyH\_analyticOn}; Thm~4.6.2, finite vol.]
The free energy $f(h) = |\iota|^{-1} \ln Z(h)$ is real-analytic on $(0,\infty)$.
Since $Z(h) > 0$ for all $h$ (\texttt{partitionFunction\_pos}), $\ln Z$
is defined and real-analytic (\texttt{AnalyticAt.log}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$Z$ is a finite sum of exponentials of affine functions,
hence real-analytic (\texttt{fun\_prop}).  Since $Z > 0$,
$\ln Z$ is real-analytic.  Multiplication by the constant
$|\iota|^{-1}$ preserves analyticity.
\end{proof}

The same argument gives $Z(J)$ and $f(J)$ real-analytic
(\texttt{partitionFunctionJ\_analyticAt}, \texttt{freeEnergyJ\_analyticOn}).

\subsection{Configuration--subset bijection}

The Lee-Yang polynomial sums over subsets $X \subseteq \iota$
while the partition function sums over configurations
$\sigma : \iota \to \{\pm 1\}$.
The bijection \texttt{configFinsetEquiv} identifies $\sigma$ with
its ``down spin'' set $X = \{i : \sigma_i = -1\}$.

\begin{definition}[\texttt{configToFinset}, \texttt{finsetToConfig}]
$\sigma \mapsto \{i : \sigma_i = \mathrm{down}\}$ and
$X \mapsto (\lambda i.\;\text{if } i \in X \text{ then down else up})$.
These are mutual inverses (\texttt{configFinsetEquiv}).
\end{definition}

The connection identity
(\cite[{(3.63)--(3.65), pp.~122--123}]{friedli-velenik}):
\[
  Z(J, h, \beta) = e^{\beta J|E| + \beta h N} \cdot
  P\bigl(e^{-2\beta h}, \ldots, e^{-2\beta h}\bigr)
\]
where $P = \texttt{isingEdgePoly}$, $z_i = e^{-2\beta h}$,
$t_e = e^{-2\beta J}$.
Combined with Lee-Yang ($P(z) \ne 0$ for $|z_i| < 1$), this gives
$Z(h) \ne 0$ for complex $h$ with $|e^{-2\beta h}| < 1$.

\begin{definition}[\texttt{graphToEdgeList}]
Converts a \texttt{SimpleGraph} with uniform coupling $t$ to the
edge list format used by \texttt{lee\_yang\_circle}:
each edge $e$ is represented as $(\texttt{Quot.out}\;e)$ with coupling $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{isingEdgePoly\_nonvanishing\_of\_graph},
  Theorem 4.6.2 {\cite[pp.~64--70]{glimm-jaffe}},
  {\cite[Theorem~3.43, pp.~122--127]{friedli-velenik}}]
For the Ising model on graph $G$ with coupling $t \in [0,1)$
(i.e., $J > 0$), the partition polynomial does not vanish on the
open unit polydisk: $P(z) \ne 0$ for all $|z_k| < 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Construct the edge list via \texttt{graphToEdgeList}, verify the
conditions (distinct endpoints from \texttt{SimpleGraph.Adj.ne},
coupling bounds from $0 \le t < 1$), and apply
\texttt{lee\_yang\_circle}.
\end{proof}

\section{GHS inequality (\texttt{Inequalities/GHS.lean})}

\par\noindent\textbf{Prerequisites:} \texttt{InfiniteVolume.lean}.

\textbf{Role:} Defines truncated correlation functions ($u_2$, $u_3$,
$u_4$) and proves the GHS inequality $u_3 \le 0$, Cor.~4.3.3
($U_4 \le 0$ for $h=0$), and Cor.~4.3.5 (inductive bound).
Also contains \texttt{correlation\_odd\_vanish} ($h=0$, odd $|A|$).

\textbf{What to look for:} the Lebowitz axiom family is fully discharged
(Issue \#3906): \texttt{lebowitz\_four} and \texttt{lebowitz\_third} were
deleted in PRs \#3909/\#3910 --- both were false as stated (see the
remarks below) --- and \texttt{lebowitz\_inductive} (true as stated) was
replaced by the proven \texttt{Lebowitz.lebowitz\_inductive\_bound} in
PR \#3911. Everything is proved. The spin-flip symmetry proof
(\texttt{correlation\_odd\_vanish}) uses a bijection argument:
pair $\sigma$ with $\mathrm{flip}(\sigma)$ to show $S = -S$.

The Griffiths--Hurst--Sherman inequality for the Ising model.
Reference: Ellis, \emph{Entropy, Large Deviations, and Statistical
Mechanics}, \S V.3, pp.~143--146.

\begin{definition}[\texttt{truncated2}, \texttt{truncated3}]
The truncated 2-point and 3-point functions (Ursell functions):
\begin{align*}
  u_2(i,j) &= \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle - \langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle, \\
  u_3(i,j,k) &= \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
    - \langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
    - \langle\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_i\sigma_k\rangle
    - \langle\sigma_k\rangle\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    + 2\langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\rangle.
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{truncated2\_nonneg}]
$u_2(i,j) \ge 0$ for ferromagnetic parameters. Proved via GKS-II
for $i \ne j$ and GKS-I $+$ $|\langle\sigma_i\rangle| \le 1$ for $i = j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[The former \texttt{lebowitz\_third} axiom was false; deleted
in PR \#3910]
The repository formerly axiomatised, for ferromagnetic $h \ge 0$ and
distinct $i, j, k$:
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle +
\langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle \le
\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\rangle +
\langle\sigma_i\sigma_k\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle$. This is false:
decoupling site $i$ ($J_{i\cdot} = 0$) with $h > 0$, correlations
factorise and the claim forces $\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle \le
\langle\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\rangle$, contradicting strict GKS-II
for a strongly coupled edge $jk$. (Equivalently the axiom asserted
$u_3 + 2\langle\sigma_i\rangle\,u_2(j,k) \le 0$, strictly stronger than
GHS.) It was the second false axiom caught by the formalisation, after
\texttt{lebowitz\_four} (PR \#3909).
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{Lebowitz.cor\_4\_3\_4}; proved, general $h \ge 0$]
For ferromagnetic parameters and distinct $i, j, k$:
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
  - \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\rangle
  - \langle\sigma_i\sigma_k\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle
  + \langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
  \le 2\langle\sigma_i\rangle\bigl(\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
    - \langle\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\rangle\bigr).
\]
Proof: \texttt{cor\_4\_3\_2\_tq} with $A = \{i\}$, $B = \{j,k\}$ ---
GJ's $2^{3/2}\langle t_iq_jq_k\rangle \le
2^{3/2}\langle t_i\rangle\langle q_jq_k\rangle$, p.~61 --- via the powerset
formulas $\langle t_i\rangle_2 = 2c_i$, $\langle q_jq_k\rangle_2 =
2(c_{jk} - c_jc_k)$, $\langle t_iq_jq_k\rangle_2 = 2(c_{ijk} - c_{ij}c_k -
c_{ik}c_j + c_ic_{jk})$. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.3
Corollary 4.3.4, p.~61.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{ghs\_inequality}; proved, axiom-free]
For ferromagnetic parameters with $h \ge 0$ and distinct $i, j, k$:
$u_3(i,j,k) \le 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\texttt{Lebowitz.cor\_4\_3\_4} \emph{is} $u_3 \le 0$ after moving the
right side over; \texttt{linarith} closes the goal. No GKS-I or
\texttt{truncated2\_nonneg} input is needed.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Spin-flip symmetry and odd correlations}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{spinProduct\_flip}]
For any set $A$ and configuration $\sigma$:
$\sigma^A(\mathrm{flip}\;\sigma) = (-1)^{|A|} \cdot \sigma^A(\sigma)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{correlation\_odd\_vanish}]
For $h = 0$ and $|A|$ odd: $\langle\sigma^A\rangle = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Set $S = \sum_\sigma \sigma^A(\sigma) \cdot w(\sigma)$.
Since $H(\mathrm{flip}\;\sigma) = H(\sigma)$ when $h = 0$
(\texttt{hamiltonian\_flip\_eq}), we have $w(\mathrm{flip}\;\sigma) = w(\sigma)$.
The flip involution $\sigma \mapsto \mathrm{flip}\;\sigma$ is a bijection on
configurations, so
$S = \sum_\sigma \sigma^A(\mathrm{flip}\;\sigma) \cdot w(\mathrm{flip}\;\sigma)
   = (-1)^{|A|} S = -S$,
hence $S = 0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Cor.~4.3.3: truncated 4-point function}

\begin{definition}[\texttt{truncated4}]
The truncated (connected) 4-point function:
\[
  U_4(i,j,k,l) = \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_k\sigma_l\rangle
  - \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\sigma_l\rangle
  - \langle\sigma_i\sigma_k\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_l\rangle
  - \langle\sigma_i\sigma_l\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[The former \texttt{lebowitz\_four} axiom was false; deleted
in PR \#3909]
The repository formerly axiomatised, for $h \ge 0$,
$\langle\sigma_{ijkl}\rangle + \langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle\langle\sigma_{kl}\rangle
\le \langle\sigma_{ik}\rangle\langle\sigma_{jl}\rangle
+ \langle\sigma_{il}\rangle\langle\sigma_{jk}\rangle
+ \langle\sigma_{ikl}\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle
+ \langle\sigma_{jkl}\rangle\langle\sigma_i\rangle$. At $h = 0$ the
odd-cardinality correlations vanish, so this asserts
$U_4 \le -2\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle\langle\sigma_{kl}\rangle$, which is
false: for two disjoint strongly coupled edges $ij$ and $kl$ the cross
correlations vanish and $\langle\sigma_{ijkl}\rangle =
\langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle\langle\sigma_{kl}\rangle > 0$. The axiom was
deleted; the corrected zero-field inequality below is proved from the
duplicate-variable machinery (\texttt{lebowitz\_four\_zero\_field}).
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{cor\_4\_3\_3}; proved, axiom-free]
For $h = 0$ and four distinct sites, $U_4(i,j,k,l) \le 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \texttt{lebowitz\_four\_zero\_field} (PR \#3909, proved from Corollary
4.3.2's $tq$ inequality),
$\langle\sigma_{ijkl}\rangle
\le \langle\sigma_{ij}\rangle\langle\sigma_{kl}\rangle
  + \langle\sigma_{ik}\rangle\langle\sigma_{jl}\rangle
  + \langle\sigma_{il}\rangle\langle\sigma_{jk}\rangle$,
which is exactly $U_4 \le 0$ after the $h = 0$ odd-correlation vanishing.
\end{proof}

\subsection[Cor.~4.3.5: n-point inductive bound]{Cor.~4.3.5: $n$-point inductive bound}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{Lebowitz.lebowitz\_inductive\_bound}; proved,
general $h \ge 0$; PR \#3911]
For ferromagnetic $h \ge 0$, a set $S$ of sites, and two sites $j, k \notin S$
with $j \ne k$:
\[
  \langle\sigma_{S \cup \{j,k\}}\rangle \le
  \langle\sigma_S\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle
  + \sum_{T \subseteq S}
    \langle\sigma_{T \cup \{j\}}\rangle\langle\sigma_{(S\setminus T) \cup \{k\}}\rangle.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \texttt{cor\_4\_3\_2\_tq} with $A = S$, $B = \{j,k\}$ and expand by
the powerset formulas (write $X' := S\setminus X$, $c_X :=
\langle\sigma^X\rangle$):
\[
  \sum_{X \subseteq S}\bigl[c_{X}c_{X'\cup\{j,k\}}
    - c_{X\cup\{j\}}c_{X'\cup\{k\}} - c_{X\cup\{k\}}c_{X'\cup\{j\}}
    + c_{X\cup\{j,k\}}c_{X'}\bigr]
  \le \Bigl[\sum_X c_Xc_{X'}\Bigr]\,2(c_{jk} - c_jc_k).
\]
Drop the odd right-hand part $-2c_jc_k\sum_X c_Xc_{X'} \le 0$ (GKS-I);
identify the first and last left-hand sums and the two middle sums by the
reflection $X \mapsto S\setminus X$ (\texttt{sum\_powerset\_reflect});
split off the $X = S$ terms and cancel the remaining even terms pairwise by
per-term GKS-II ($c_Xc_{jk} \le c_{X\cup\{j,k\}}$, multiplied by
$c_{X'} \ge 0$). What remains is exactly the claimed bound. This was the
statement of the former \texttt{lebowitz\_inductive} axiom (true as
stated, unlike \texttt{lebowitz\_four}/\texttt{lebowitz\_third}); the
axiom is deleted and \texttt{cor\_4\_3\_5\_h0} rewired. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.3 Cor.~4.3.5, p.~62.
\end{proof}

Iterating gives Cor.~4.3.5: the $n$-point function
is bounded by $(n-1)!$ times the sum over partial matchings of products
of 2-point and 1-point correlations.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{cor\_4\_3\_3\_scaled}; proven, PR \#3912 ---
GJ Cor 4.3.3 for non-uniform couplings]
For the scaled model (`$K_e = sJ$' on a distinguished edge set
$E_0 \subseteq E$, $K_e = J$ elsewhere) with ferromagnetic parameters,
$h = 0$ and $s \ge 0$, and four distinct sites $r, a, k, l$:
\[
  \langle\sigma_{rakl}\rangle_s \le
  \langle\sigma_{ra}\rangle_s\langle\sigma_{kl}\rangle_s
  + \langle\sigma_{rk}\rangle_s\langle\sigma_{al}\rangle_s
  + \langle\sigma_{rl}\rangle_s\langle\sigma_{ak}\rangle_s .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The duplicate-variable layer is generalised to an abstract positive weight
$w$ (\texttt{WeightedSystem.lean}): the $t/q$ bracket chain depends on the
weight only through the product structure and the non-negativity of the
fourfold u-moments, so the generic $tq$ comparison inequality
(\texttt{wCor\_4\_3\_2\_tq}) and the powerset formulas hold for any such
$w$. The scaled fourfold weight is the exponential of a u-edge sum with
per-edge coefficients $\beta s J/4$ on $E_0$ and $\beta J/4$ elsewhere
(\texttt{wQuadWeight\_scaled\_eq\_exp} --- the $-\beta(1-s)J$ correction
combines with the base coupling and never appears negatively), hence has
non-negative u-moments for $s \ge 0$
(\texttt{hasNonnegUMoments\_wQuadWeight\_scaled}). The zero-field assembly
with \texttt{scaledCorrelation\_odd\_vanish} then proves the former
axiom's statement verbatim, exactly as in the uniform case. This was the
last \S4.3 corollary axiom; the entire Lebowitz corollary family of
GJ \S4.3 is now axiom-free. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.3
Cor.~4.3.3, p.~61.
\end{proof}

\section{\texorpdfstring{$\varphi^4$}{phi4} inequalities (\texttt{ContinuousSpin/Phi4.lean})}

The $\varphi^4$ correlation inequalities
\cite[{\S4.3, pp.~59--62}]{glimm-jaffe}
provide Lebowitz-type bounds for continuous spin models with
single-spin distribution $d\mu = e^{-\lambda\xi^4 - \sigma\xi^2}\,d\xi$.

The formalization includes:
\begin{itemize}
\item The quartic identity for the orthogonal transformation
  $(\xi,\chi,\xi',\chi') \mapsto (\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$
  (\texttt{quartic\_identity}, proved by \texttt{ring}).
\item Sum-of-squares, linear, and inner-product identities
  (orthogonality of the transformation).
\item The positivity lemma $t\cdot\sinh(ct) \ge 0$ for $c \ge 0$
  (\texttt{mul\_sinh\_nonneg}).
\item Odd-function integral vanishing (\texttt{integral\_odd\_eq\_zero}).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Now proven (Issue \#3913 complete, PR \#3917).}
This single-site positivity was formerly an axiom; it is now
\textbf{proven unconditionally} (no integrability hypothesis) by the
four-fold sign symmetrisation, in \texttt{ContinuousSpin/Phi4AllOdd.lean}.
The statement:
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{phi4\_single\_\allowbreak site\_nonneg}: non-negativity of the
  symmetrized 4D integral: for $Q$ even and $c \ge 0$,
  \[
    \int \alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n \,
    e^{-Q + c\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} \ge 0.
  \]
\end{itemize}
The proof strategy: write $e^x = \cosh(x) + \sinh(x)$ with $x = c\alpha\beta\gamma\delta$.
The $\cosh$ term is even in each variable, so odd-power monomials integrate to zero
(\texttt{integral\_odd\_eq\_zero}); for all-even $(k,l,m,n)$ the integrand is
$\ge 0$ (even powers $\times$ $\cosh \ge 0$ $\times$ $e^{-Q} \ge 0$).
The $\sinh$ term is odd in each variable, so even-power monomials integrate to zero;
for all-odd $(k,l,m,n)$ the integrand is
$\alpha^{k-1}\beta^{l-1}\gamma^{m-1}\delta^{n-1} \cdot
(\alpha\beta\gamma\delta \cdot \sinh(c\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)) \cdot e^{-Q} \ge 0$
by \texttt{mul\_sinh\_nonneg}.

\paragraph{Integrability-free symmetrisation core (PR \#3914,
\texttt{ContinuousSpin/Phi4Symmetrization.lean}).}
The reflection $x \mapsto -x$ is measure-preserving on
$(\mathbb{R}, \mathrm{vol})$, so $\int f(-x) = \int f$ unconditionally
(\texttt{integral\_comp\_neg\_real}; both sides take the junk value $0$
together on non-integrable $f$). The four sign flips $T_s$ are products of
such reflections, and since $Q$ is even in each variable the integrand
transforms by the sign character $s_1^k s_2^l s_3^m s_4^n$ and the factor
$e^{c\sigma\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}$ with $\sigma = s_1s_2s_3s_4$.
Averaging over the sixteen patterns
(\texttt{sign\_average\_all\_even}/\texttt{\_all\_odd}/\texttt{\_mixed},
assembled as \texttt{sign\_average\_trichotomy}) collapses the sign sum to
$16\cosh(c\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)$ when all of $k,l,m,n$ are even,
$16\sinh(c\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)$ when all are odd, and $0$ for every
mixed parity (pairwise sign cancellation). The remaining steps --- the
measure-theoretic averaging under an integrability hypothesis and the
pointwise non-negativity of the symmetrised integrand --- follow in later
PRs of Issue \#3913.

\paragraph{Unconditional iterated-integral reflection (PR \#3915,
\texttt{ContinuousSpin/Phi4Reflection.lean}).}
Writing the single-site integrand as
\texttt{phi4Integrand}$\,Q\,c\,k\,l\,m\,n = \alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n
e^{-Q+c\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}$, each multiplier reflection
$x \mapsto \mathrm{boolSign}(b)\cdot x$ preserves the integral
(\texttt{integral\_comp\_boolSign\_mul}), so the four-fold iterated integral
is invariant under every sign pattern, the flip being applied at each
nesting level (\texttt{integral4\_comp\_boolSign\_mul}; no integrability
hypothesis). Since $Q$ is even in each variable, the reflected integrand is
$\mathrm{boolSign}^{k,l,m,n}\cdot \alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n
e^{-Q+c\sigma\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}$ with $\sigma = \prod \mathrm{boolSign}(b_i)$
(\texttt{phi4Integrand\_boolSign\_mul}), giving
\texttt{phi4\_integral4\_eq\_reflected}: the four-fold $\varphi^4$ integral
equals the integral of the sign-transformed integrand for each of the
sixteen patterns. The averaging over patterns (which needs integrability)
and the pointwise non-negativity follow in the next PRs.

\paragraph{Unconditional parity cases (PR \#3916,
\texttt{ContinuousSpin/Phi4Averaging.lean}).}
Two of the three parity cases of the single-site positivity need no
integrability. When $k,l,m,n$ are all even, the integrand
$\alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n e^{-Q+c\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}$ is pointwise
non-negative (even powers and a positive exponential), so the four-fold
integral is non-negative (\texttt{phi4\_integral4\_nonneg\_all\_even}). When
the parities are mixed, reflecting one even-exponent and one odd-exponent
variable (a two-flip sign pattern) fixes the cross term ($\sigma = +1$) but
flips the monomial sign character ($= -1$), so by
\texttt{phi4\_integral4\_eq\_reflected} the integral equals its own negative
and therefore vanishes (\texttt{phi4\_integral4\_eq\_zero\_mixed}, via the
negation-by-reflection helper \texttt{phi4\_integral4\_eq\_zero\_of\_neg\_pattern}).
The all-odd case is handled at the \emph{innermost} $\delta$-integral, where
the integrability dichotomy is local and no Fubini is needed: the
$\delta$-reflection gives $\int_\delta G = -\int_\delta G''$ (with $G''$ the
$c \mapsto -c$ integrand), so on the integrable branch
$2\int_\delta G = \int_\delta (G - G'')
= \int_\delta 2\,(\text{even powers})\,e^{-Q}\,(\alpha\beta\gamma\delta)
\sinh(c\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta) \ge 0$ by \texttt{mul\_sinh\_nonneg}, and
on the non-integrable branch $\int_\delta G = 0$; either way the inner
integral is non-negative, and four iterations of \texttt{integral\_nonneg}
give the all-odd result (\texttt{phi4\_integral4\_nonneg\_all\_odd}).
The headline \texttt{phi4\_single\_site\_nonneg} dispatches the three parity
cases unconditionally, and the axiom is deleted. No interchange of
symmetrization sums with nested Bochner integrals is needed: the only
combining happens inside the single innermost $\delta$-integral.

\section{Two-component spins (\texttt{ContinuousSpin/TwoComponent.lean})}

Glimm--Jaffe, \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1 (p.~70) generalises the correlation
inequalities to two-component (planar rotator) vector spins
$\xi_i = (t_i, q_i) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with the $SO(2)$-invariant single-spin
potential $P(\xi) = A(t^2+q^2)^2 + \sigma(t^2+q^2)$, $A \ge 0 \le \sigma$.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{twoCompPotential\_double\_eq}, PR \#3919]
Doubling the potential across a duplicate spin and writing it in the
(4.3.2) rotation $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ of $(t,q,t',q')$ (with the
$\delta$ slot taken as \texttt{twoCompDelta} $= -\,\texttt{phi4Delta}$, fixing
the sign of the cross term),
\[
  P(t,q) + P(t',q') = \texttt{twoCompEvenPart}(A,\sigma;\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)
    - 4A\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta,
\]
where \texttt{twoCompEvenPart} is even in each rotated variable
(\texttt{twoCompEvenPart\_even\_alpha}/\texttt{\_beta}/\texttt{\_gamma}/\texttt{\_delta}).
\end{theorem}

This is exactly the $Q$ even, $c = 4A \ge 0$ form of
\texttt{phi4\_single\_site\_nonneg}, so the single-site positivity at the core
of Theorem 4.7.1, \texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_nonneg}, follows immediately:
\[
  0 \le \int\!\!\int\!\!\int\!\!\int \alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n\,
    e^{-\texttt{twoCompEvenPart} + 4A\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} .
\]
The $t/q$ vector duplicate framework and the three inequalities (4.7.5)--(4.7.7)
of Theorem 4.7.1, together with Corollary 4.7.2, follow in subsequent PRs.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, pp.~70--71; [Ruelle, 1969].

\paragraph{Multi-site framework (\texttt{ContinuousSpin/TwoComponentSystem.lean}).}
The foundational layer of the two-component multi-site Gibbs system:
vector configurations $\xi : \iota \to \mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}$, the
single-spin potential summed over sites
(\texttt{vectorPotentialSum}), the ferromagnetic Hamiltonian
$H = -J\sum_e \xi_i\cdot\xi_j - h^1\sum t_i - h^2\sum q_i$
(\texttt{vectorHamiltonian}), the positive Gibbs weight
$e^{-\beta H - \sum_i P(\xi_i)}$ (\texttt{vectorWeight}, with
\texttt{vectorWeight\_pos}), the partition function and expectation as
Lebesgue integrals over $(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R})^\iota$
(\texttt{vectorPartition}, \texttt{vectorExpectation}), and the $t/q$
correlations $\langle t^A q^B\rangle$ (\texttt{vectorCorrelation}). The weight
and all building blocks are continuous in the configuration, hence measurable.
The single-spin and multi-site integrability, and the three inequalities of
Theorem 4.7.1, follow in subsequent PRs.

\paragraph{Single-spin integrability (\texttt{ContinuousSpin/TwoComponentIntegrable.lean}).}
For $A > 0$, $\sigma \ge 0$ the $SO(2)$-invariant single-spin density
$e^{-A(t^2+q^2)^2 - \sigma(t^2+q^2)}$ is integrable over $\mathbb{R}^2$
(\texttt{integrable\_singleSpinDensity}). In polar coordinates
(\texttt{lintegral\_comp\_polarCoord\_symm}, with
$|\,\texttt{polarCoord.symm}(r,\theta)|^2 = r^2$) and Tonelli
(\texttt{Measure.prod\_restrict}) the $\mathbb{R}^2$ Lebesgue integral factors
as $\operatorname{vol}(-\pi,\pi)\cdot\int_0^\infty r\,e^{-A r^4 - \sigma r^2}\,dr$,
and the radial integrand is integrable on $(0,\infty)$
(\texttt{integrableOn\_radial\_single\_spin}), dominated by the Mathlib
super-Gaussian $r\,e^{-A r^4}$ since $e^{-\sigma r^2} \le 1$. The quartic term
$A > 0$ is what forces integrability.

\paragraph{Multi-site weight integrability and partition positivity
(\texttt{ContinuousSpin/TwoComponentMultiIntegrable.lean}).}
For $A > 0$ the multi-site Gibbs weight
$\texttt{vectorWeight} = e^{-\beta H - \sum_i P(\xi_i)}$ is integrable over
$(\mathbb{R}^2)^\iota$ (\texttt{integrable\_vectorWeight}), so the partition
function is well defined. The proof is a \emph{uniform arithmetic--geometric-mean
estimate} (\texttt{exists\_vectorWeight\_exponent\_bound}): the exponent is
bounded, with configuration-independent constants $K, b$, by
\[
  -\beta H(\xi) - \sum_i P(\xi_i)
  \;\le\; K + \sum_i \bigl(b\,|\xi_i|^2 - A\,|\xi_i|^4\bigr).
\]
The ferromagnetic interaction is absorbed through
$|\xi_i\cdot\xi_j| \le \tfrac12(|\xi_i|^2 + |\xi_j|^2) \le \sum_k |\xi_k|^2$
(\texttt{abs\_vEdgeDot\_le\_sum\_normSq}), and the external field through
$|t_i| \le \tfrac12(1 + |\xi_i|^2)$ (\texttt{abs\_vSpinT\_le}); summing over the
$\#E$ edges and the $n = |\iota|$ sites gives the per-site quadratic coefficient
$b = |\beta J|\cdot\#E + \tfrac12(|\beta h^1| + |\beta h^2|) - \sigma$ and the
constant $K = \tfrac{n}{2}(|\beta h^1| + |\beta h^2|)$. Hence
$\texttt{vectorWeight} \le e^K \prod_i e^{b|\xi_i|^2 - A|\xi_i|^4}$, a product of
integrable modified single-spin densities (\texttt{integrable\_modSpinDensity};
its radial integrand is integrable on $(0,\infty)$ by completing the square
$b r^2 - A r^4 \le \tfrac{b^2}{2A} - \tfrac{A}{2} r^4$ and dominating by the
super-Gaussian $r\,e^{-(A/2) r^4}$, \texttt{integrableOn\_radial\_quad\_quartic}).
\texttt{Integrable.fintype\_prod} makes the product integrable and
\texttt{Integrable.mono'} transfers integrability to \texttt{vectorWeight}.
Since the weight is continuous, integrable, non-negative and strictly positive,
the partition function is strictly positive
(\texttt{vectorPartition\_pos}, via
\texttt{integral\_pos\_of\_integrable\_nonneg\_nonzero}), so the Gibbs
expectation $\langle\cdot\rangle$ of Theorem 4.7.1 is well defined.

\paragraph{Single-site moment positivity (Griffiths-I core)
(\texttt{ContinuousSpin/TwoComponentGriffiths.lean}).}
The first inequality of Theorem 4.7.1, $\langle t^A q^B\rangle \ge 0$, rests on the
single-site moment positivity
$0 \le \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} t^a q^b\, e^{-A(t^2+q^2)^2 - \sigma(t^2+q^2)}$
(\texttt{singleSpinMoment\_nonneg}, $A>0$). If $a$ (or $b$) is odd the integral
vanishes by the reflection $t\mapsto -t$ (resp. $q\mapsto -q$): the density is even
in each coordinate, so via Fubini (\texttt{integral\_prod}) the inner integral is
the integral of an odd function, $0$ by \texttt{integral\_comp\_neg\_real}. If both
are even the integrand is non-negative (\texttt{integral\_nonneg}). The
monomial-weighted density is integrable
(\texttt{integrable\_pow\_mul\_singleSpinDensity}): in polar coordinates its norm is
$\le r^{a+b+1} e^{-A r^4 - \sigma r^2}$ (as $|\cos\theta|,|\sin\theta|\le1$), whose
radial integral is finite by \texttt{integrableOn\_pow\_quad\_quartic} (complete the
square $b r^2 - A r^4 \le \tfrac{b^2}{2A}-\tfrac{A}{2}r^4$ and dominate by the
super-Gaussian $r^n e^{-(A/2)r^4}$). The continuous-spin Griffiths/Ginibre
development of the three inequalities of Theorem 4.7.1 continues from this
single-site core. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, p.~70.

\paragraph{Single-site moments with an external field (Griffiths-I, $h\ge0$).}
The field-dependent version $0 \le \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} t^a q^b\, e^{c_1 t + c_2 q}\,
e^{-A(t^2+q^2)^2-\sigma(t^2+q^2)}$ ($A>0$, $c_1,c_2\ge0$,
\texttt{singleSpinMoment\_field\_nonneg}) is proved by \emph{truncation and
dominated convergence}, the template reused for the multi-site interaction
expansion. Replacing each field exponential by its partial sum
$\texttt{expTrunc}\,N\,x = \sum_{k<N} x^k/k!$ (\texttt{tendsto\_expTrunc},
$|\texttt{expTrunc}\,N\,x|\le e^{|x|}$), the truncated integral expands
(\texttt{Finset.sum\_mul\_sum}) into a finite sum
$\sum_{m,l<N} \tfrac{c_1^m c_2^l}{m!\,l!}\int t^{a+m}q^{b+l} e^{-P}$ of
non-negative-coefficient single-site moments (each $\ge0$ by
\texttt{singleSpinMoment\_nonneg}), hence $\ge0$. Dominated convergence
(\texttt{tendsto\_integral\_of\_dominated\_convergence}) passes to the limit, the
linear field absorbed into the quadratic via $|t|\le(1+t^2)/2$, so the dominating
function $e^{C}\,\|t^a q^b\,\texttt{singleSpinDensity}\,A\,(\sigma-d)\|$ is
integrable (\texttt{integrable\_pow\_mul\_singleSpinDensity} with shifted
$\sigma$). Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{First Griffiths inequality (\texttt{vectorCorrelation\_nonneg}).}
For $A>0$, ferromagnetic $\beta,J\ge0$ and a non-negative external field
$h^1,h^2\ge0$, every monomial correlation of the two-component Gibbs measure is
non-negative,
\[
0\le\Big\langle \textstyle\prod_{i\in A} t_i\,\prod_{j\in B} q_j\Big\rangle
\qquad(\text{GJ Theorem 4.7.1, first inequality}).
\]
The Gibbs weight factorises as
$\exp(\beta J\sum_e \xi_i\!\cdot\!\xi_j)\cdot\prod_i \texttt{siteWeight}_i$
(\texttt{vectorWeight\_eq\_exp\_mul\_siteWeightProd}), with
$\texttt{siteWeight}\,A\,\sigma\,c_1\,c_2\,\xi
= e^{c_1 t + c_2 q}\,e^{-A|\xi|^4-\sigma|\xi|^2}$ and $c_1=\beta h^1$,
$c_2=\beta h^2$. Replacing the interaction exponential by its truncation
$\texttt{expTrunc}\,N(\beta J\,S)$ turns the integrand into $\texttt{spinEval}\,p$
for a polynomial $p\in\texttt{MvPolynomial}\,(\iota\oplus\iota)\,\mathbb{R}$ with
\emph{non-negative coefficients} (\texttt{NonnegCoeffs}). Ferromagnetism keeps
every coefficient non-negative, and closure under sum/product/power is just
\texttt{coeff\_add}/\texttt{coeff\_mul} non-negativity --- this is what discharges
the otherwise painful multinomial expansion of $(\sum_e \xi_i\!\cdot\!\xi_j)^k$:
the polynomial ring structure does the bookkeeping. The integral of a
non-negative-coefficient polynomial against the product weight factorises
(\texttt{eval\_eq'}, \texttt{Fintype.prod\_sum\_type},
\texttt{integral\_fintype\_prod\_volume\_eq\_prod}) into a non-negative
combination of products of single-site field moments
\texttt{singleSpinMoment\_field\_nonneg}, hence $\ge0$
(\texttt{spinEval\_integral\_nonneg}). Dominated convergence
(\texttt{tendsto\_integral\_of\_dominated\_convergence}) passes to the limit
$N\to\infty$, the uniform dominator (\texttt{norm\_truncIntegrand\_le\_dom})
coming from $|\texttt{expTrunc}\,N(\beta J\,S)|\le \exp(|\beta J|\cdot\#E\cdot
\sum_i|\xi_i|^2)$ (AM-GM on the inner products), which raises the per-site
quadratic coefficient $\sigma\mapsto\sigma-cc$. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd
ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{Integrability foundations for the second/third inequalities.}
The duplicate-variable proof of (4.7.6)--(4.7.8) works in the rotated variables
$(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$, where the doubled single-site density is
$\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,\sigma\,p
= e^{-\texttt{twoCompEvenPart}\,A\,\sigma\,\alpha\beta\gamma\delta
+ 4A\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}$. The required integrability rests on
\texttt{integrable\_pow\_mul\_exp\_quad\_quartic}: $x^a e^{bx^2-Ax^4}$ is
integrable over all of $\mathbb{R}$ for $A>0$ (the quartic dominates; proved by
splitting $\mathbb{R}=(-\infty,0]\cup(0,\infty)$ and reflecting the negative half
onto $(0,\infty)$). The exponent obeys the AM-GM bound
\texttt{rotExponent\_le}:
$-\texttt{twoCompEvenPart}+4A\alpha\beta\gamma\delta
\le \sum_j(-\sigma p_j^2-\tfrac{A}{2}p_j^4)$, the sole positive cross term
$4A\alpha\beta\gamma\delta\le 2A(\alpha^2\beta^2+\gamma^2\delta^2)$ being absorbed
by $-3A(\alpha^2\beta^2+\gamma^2\delta^2)$. Hence the monomial-weighted density is
integrable over $(\,\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{Fin}\,4})$
(\texttt{integrable\_monomial\_mul\_rotSiteDensity}), and likewise with an
external field $e^{c_\alpha\alpha+c_\gamma\gamma}$ absorbed into the quadratic
part (\texttt{integrable\_monomial\_mul\_field\_rotSiteDensity}), by
\texttt{Integrable.fintype\_prod} over the four coordinates. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{Product-form single-site moment.} The iterated single-site positivity
\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_nonneg} ($0\le\int\!\int\!\int\!\int
\alpha^k\beta^l\gamma^m\delta^n e^{-\texttt{twoCompEvenPart}+4A\alpha\beta\gamma
\delta}$) is recast over the product space $(\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})$. A
reusable one-coordinate peeling
$\int_{(\mathrm{Fin}(n{+}1)\to\mathbb{R})} F = \int_x\int_r F(\mathrm{cons}\,x\,r)$
(\texttt{integral\_pi\_cons}, via the measure-preserving head split
$(\mathrm{Fin}(n{+}1)\to\mathbb{R})\simeq\mathbb{R}\times(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to
\mathbb{R})$) together with a.e.\ integrability of the tail
(\texttt{ae\_integrable\_cons}) gives the four-fold expansion
\texttt{integral\_fin4} (the innermost $\mathrm{Fin}\,0$ integral collapsing
against the probability measure). Hence
$0\le\int_{(\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})}(\prod_j p_j^{e_j})\,
\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,\sigma\,p$
(\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_prod\_nonneg}), and with extra $0/2$-powers
(\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_prod\_extra\_nonneg}, via the exponent-raising
identity \texttt{prod\_pow\_raise}). These are the per-site moments consumed by
the four-variable multi-site cone of the second/third inequalities. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{Single-site moment with field.} The field-dependent version
$0\le\int_{(\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})}(\prod_j p_j^{e_j})\,
e^{c_\alpha p_0+c_\gamma p_2}\,\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,\sigma\,p$ for
$c_\alpha,c_\gamma\ge0$ (\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_field\_prod\_nonneg}) is
proved exactly as the two-component field moment: truncate the field exponentials,
expand each truncation into a finite non-negative combination of
\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_prod\_extra\_nonneg} moments, and pass to the limit
by dominated convergence. The linear field is absorbed into the quadratic part via
$|t|\le(1+t^2)/2$, so the dominator raises $\sigma\mapsto\sigma-d$
(\texttt{rotSiteDensity\_shift}:
$\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,(\sigma-d)\,p
= e^{d\sum_j p_j^2}\,\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,\sigma\,p$). This is the per-site
engine (with field) for the second/third inequalities. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe,
2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{The doubled-rotated cone.} The multi-site analogue of the first
inequality's cone, for the \emph{doubled rotated} measure: a configuration
$\mathrm{cfg}:\iota\to(\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})$ assigns the four rotated
coordinates per site, with per-site weight
$\texttt{siteWeight4}\,A\,\sigma\,c_\alpha\,c_\gamma\,q
= e^{c_\alpha q_0+c_\gamma q_2}\,\texttt{rotSiteDensity}\,A\,\sigma\,q$, and
polynomials over $\iota\times\mathrm{Fin}\,4$ with non-negative coefficients
(\texttt{NNCoeffs}). The integral of a non-negative-coefficient polynomial against
the product weight factorises (\texttt{eval\_eq'},
\texttt{Fintype.prod\_prod\_type},
\texttt{integral\_fintype\_prod\_volume\_eq\_prod}) into single-site field moments
\texttt{twoComp\_single\_site\_field\_prod\_nonneg}, hence
$0\le\int_{(\iota\to\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})}\texttt{dSpinEval}\,p\cdot
\prod_i\texttt{siteWeight4}\,(\mathrm{cfg}\,i)$
(\texttt{dSpinEval\_integral\_nonneg}). This is the cone consumed (after
interaction truncation and the duplicate-variable rotation) by the second/third
inequalities. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{Interaction truncation.} The ferromagnetic interaction
$\sum_e(\alpha_i\alpha_j+\beta_i\beta_j+\gamma_i\gamma_j+\delta_i\delta_j)$ is a
polynomial \texttt{interactionPoly4} over $\iota\times\mathrm{Fin}\,4$ with
non-negative coefficients. The truncating polynomial
$\texttt{truncPoly4}=\texttt{obs}\cdot\sum_{k<N}C((\beta J)^k/k!)\,
\texttt{interactionPoly4}^k$ has $\texttt{dSpinEval}=\texttt{dSpinEval}\,
\texttt{obs}\cdot\texttt{expTrunc}\,N(\beta J\sum_e\texttt{edgeDot4})$ and keeps
non-negative coefficients for $\beta,J\ge0$ and a non-negative observable
(\texttt{truncPoly4\_nncoeffs}). The AM-GM bound \texttt{abs\_edgeDot4\_le\_sum}
($|\texttt{edgeDot4}\,\mathrm{cfg}\,e|\le\sum_i\texttt{normSq4}\,(\mathrm{cfg}\,i)$)
and the density shift \texttt{siteWeight4\_shift}
($\texttt{siteWeight4}\,A\,(\sigma-cc)=e^{cc\cdot\texttt{normSq4}}\,
\texttt{siteWeight4}\,A\,\sigma$) prepare the dominated-convergence dominator.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{The interaction expectation.} For a non-negative-coefficient
observable $\texttt{obs}$, ferromagnetic $\beta J\ge0$ and non-negative field
$c_\alpha,c_\gamma\ge0$,
\[
0\le\int_{(\iota\to\mathrm{Fin}\,4\to\mathbb{R})}\texttt{dSpinEval}\,\texttt{obs}\,
\mathrm{cfg}\cdot e^{\beta J\sum_e\texttt{edgeDot4}\,\mathrm{cfg}\,e}\cdot
\prod_i\texttt{siteWeight4}\,A\,\sigma\,c_\alpha\,c_\gamma\,(\mathrm{cfg}\,i)
\quad(\texttt{dRotInteraction\_nonneg}).
\]
The interaction exponential is truncated to the non-negative-coefficient
\texttt{truncPoly4}, whose integral is $\ge0$ by
\texttt{dSpinEval\_integral\_nonneg}; dominated convergence with the uniform
dominator $\texttt{dSpinEval}\,\texttt{obs}\,|\mathrm{cfg}|\cdot\prod_i
\texttt{siteWeight4}\,A\,(\sigma-cc)$ (using
$|\texttt{dSpinEval}\,\texttt{obs}\,\mathrm{cfg}|\le
\texttt{dSpinEval}\,\texttt{obs}\,|\mathrm{cfg}|$ for non-negative coefficients and
the AM-GM/shift bounds) passes to the limit. This is the doubled-rotated
non-negativity consumed by the duplicate-variable argument. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{General monomial integrability.} The GKS-II doubling identity needs the
integrability of a general monomial $\texttt{genMonomial}\,a\,b\,\xi=\prod_i
t_i^{a_i}q_i^{b_i}$ against the two-component Gibbs weight
(\texttt{integrable\_genMonomial\_mul\_vectorWeight}). The proof mirrors
\texttt{integrable\_vectorWeight}: the uniform AM-GM bound dominates
\texttt{vectorWeight} by $e^K\prod_i\texttt{modSpinDensity}\,c\,A\,(\xi_i)$, and
the extra monomial is absorbed into a product of integrable monomial-weighted
modified single-spin densities (\texttt{integrable\_abs\_pow\_mul\_modSpinDensity},
via $\texttt{modSpinDensity}\,c\,A=\texttt{singleSpinDensity}\,A\,(-c)$). Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., \S4.7, Theorem 4.7.1, pp.~70--71.

\paragraph{The GKS-II doubling identity.} The Ginibre duplicate-variable
reduction (\texttt{doubling\_identity}): for a weight $W$ and observables $F,G$,
\[
\Big(\!\int W\Big)\Big(\!\int FGW\Big)-\Big(\!\int FW\Big)\Big(\!\int GW\Big)
= \tfrac12\!\int\!\!\int (F(\xi)-F(\xi'))(G(\xi)-G(\xi'))\,W(\xi)\,W(\xi'),
\]
