\end{Verbatim}
The hypothesis is the conjunction produced by
\path{cubicTanhProfileBound_cubic_corr_mem_Ioo_and_profile}: anchored cubic
active-range membership and the cubic profile lower bound.  This gives
downstream proofs a stable way to pass that pair into the capstone bundle
without placing \path{cubicTanhProfileBound} itself in the heavy comparison
statement.

The totalized comparison
\path{pseudoMassExt_twoPointFunction_le_high_temp_rate_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
packages the same tanh-power input without forcing the upper endpoint into the
proof.  It proves
\[
  \mathrm{pseudoMassExt}\bigl(
    \mathrm{twoPointFunction}\,d\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,z\bigr)
    \le -\log(\beta J\,2d).
\]
If the two-point function lies in $(0,2)$, this is the ordinary pseudo-mass
comparison via the implicit characterization of $\mathrm{pseudoMass}$.  If it
does not lie in $(0,2)$, the totalized function is zero, and the comparison
follows from $0\le -\log(\beta J\,2d)$ for Lean's total real logarithm.  The
concrete $\mathrm{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair}$ wrapper remains a separate
lightweight composition step.

\paragraph{Active two-point pseudo-mass comparison from tanh profile bounds
(PR~\#1817).}
The follow-up
\path{twoPointFunction_mem_Ioo_zero_two_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
records that the same tanh-power profile hypothesis places the anchored
two-point function itself in the active interval $(0,2)$.  The lower endpoint
is obtained by the positivity of $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}$ at the nonnegative
Lean real-log rate and the tanh-distance lower bound, while the upper endpoint
uses the universal estimate
\(\mathrm{twoPointFunction}\le 1 < 2\).
Consequently
\path{pseudoMass_twoPointFunction_le_high_temp_rate_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
removes the totalisation and proves the ordinary pseudo-mass comparison
\[
  \mathrm{pseudoMass}\bigl(
    \mathrm{twoPointFunction}\,d\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,z\bigr)
    \le -\log(\beta J\,2d),
\]
with the required active-interval proof supplied as the implicit argument to
\(\mathrm{pseudoMass}\).  The equality
\path{pseudoMassExt_twoPointFunction_eq_pseudoMass_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
then states that the totalised comparison of PR~\#1816 agrees with the ordinary
pseudo-mass comparison under this profile hypothesis.  This stays on the
anchored two-point API and deliberately does not claim the concrete
\(\mathrm{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair}\) wrapper.

\paragraph{Positive active two-point pseudo-mass consequences (PR~\#1818).}
The positivity follow-up keeps the same anchored two-point scope.  The theorem
\path{pseudoMass_twoPointFunction_pos_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
applies \(\mathrm{pseudoMass\_pos}\) to the active-interval proof from
PR~\#1817.  The totalized form
\path{pseudoMassExt_twoPointFunction_pos_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
uses \(\mathrm{pseudoMassExt\_pos\_of\_mem}\) with the same active proof, and
\path{pseudoMassExt_twoPointFunction_ne_zero_of_pseudoMassG_le_tanh_pow_dist}
records the corresponding non-vanishing corollary.  These are bookkeeping
consequences for later Step~117l compositions and still do not assert the
concrete \(\mathrm{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair}\) comparison.

\paragraph{\S5.1 cluster property bundled formalisation (PR~\#792).}
The Glimm--Jaffe \S5.1 cluster property is formalised as a single
predicate
\[
  \mathrm{clusterProperty}\,G\,\Lambda\,p \;:=\;
    \forall\, i \in V,\
    \mathrm{Tendsto}\bigl(j \mapsto U_2(i, j)\bigr)\,
    \mathrm{Filter.cofinite}\,(\mathrm{nhds}\,0)
\]
($\mathrm{IsingModel.Ambient.clusterProperty}$, in
\texttt{AmbientLattice.lean}). The PR bundles the
sufficient condition $\mathrm{clusterProperty\_of\_summable}$
(per-site application of
$\mathrm{truncated2Infinite\_tendsto\_cofinite\_zero\_of\_summable}$),
together with the two trivial-slice proofs
$\mathrm{clusterProperty\_J\_zero}$ (for ferromagnetic
$\langle 0, h, \beta \rangle$, using $U_2 = 0$ off-diagonally and
$\mathrm{Filter.eventuallyEq}$ on $\{i\}^{\mathrm c}$) and
$\mathrm{clusterProperty\_beta\_zero}$ (for any
$\langle J, h, 0 \rangle$, using $U_2 \equiv 0$ at $\beta = 0$).
$\mathbb Z^d$ wrappers
$\mathrm{clusterProperty\_latticeGraph\_\{of\_summable, J\_zero, beta\_zero\}}$
specialise these to the integer lattice graph. The general
(non-trivial) case requires the Simon--Lieb inequality (FV Prop~9.31)
or random-current representation; both are research-level and
remain open (Issue~\#780).

\paragraph{Outer-side companion of PR~\#787's edge bound (PR~\#791).}
The symmetric outer-side bound
\[
  |\partial^e S| \;\le\; \sum_{y \in \partial^v_o S} \deg_G(y)
\]
($\mathrm{edgeBoundary\_card\_le\_sum\_degrees\_outerVertexBoundary}$)
follows from PR~\#789's outer-side equality plus the
$|\mathrm{filter}| \le |\mathrm{neighborFinset}| = \deg$
estimate, mirroring PR~\#787 with $\partial^v_o$ in place of
$\partial^v_i$. On $\mathbb Z^d$ this gives
$|\partial^e S| \le 2 d \cdot |\partial^v_o S|$, and combining
with PR~\#787's inner-side wrapper yields the strictly stronger
combined bound
$|\partial^e S| \le 2 d \cdot \min(|\partial^v_i S|, |\partial^v_o S|)$.

\paragraph{Vertex-by-edge bounds (PR~\#790).}
Two simple-but-useful bounds tying the vertex boundaries to the
edge boundary:
\[
  |\partial^v_i S| \;\le\; |\partial^e S|, \quad
  |\partial^v_o S| \;\le\; |\partial^e S|
\]
($\mathrm{innerVertexBoundary\_card\_le\_edgeBoundary\_card}$,
$\mathrm{outerVertexBoundary\_card\_le\_edgeBoundary\_card}$).
Each follow from the equalities of PRs~\#788 / \#789 by observing
that the very witness making a vertex a boundary vertex is an
element of the corresponding filter, so each summand is $\ge 1$;
sum monotonicity finishes. Together with the existing
edge-boundary bounds these give the linear chain
\[
  |\partial^v_i S|,\, |\partial^v_o S|
  \;\le\; |\partial^e S|
  \;\le\; \deg_{\max} \cdot |\partial^v_i S|,
\]
which on $\mathrm{latticeGraph}(d)$ becomes the chain with
$\deg_{\max} = 2d$.

\subsection{Lattice-growth convergence of \S5 quantities}

Named corollaries of \texttt{correlation\_convergent\_subgraph} (PR~\#64):

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{truncated2\_convergent\_subgraph}]
$\langle\sigma_i;\sigma_j\rangle_{G_n}$ converges for any increasing subgraph
sequence $G_n$ with ferromagnetic parameters.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Each of $\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle_{G_n}$, $\langle\sigma_i\rangle_{G_n}$,
$\langle\sigma_j\rangle_{G_n}$ converges; apply \texttt{Tendsto.sub} and
\texttt{Tendsto.mul}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{susceptibility\_convergent\_subgraph}]
$\chi_i(G_n) = \sum_j \langle\sigma_i;\sigma_j\rangle_{G_n}$ converges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{magnetization\_total\_convergent\_subgraph}]
$\sum_i \langle\sigma_i\rangle_{G_n}$ converges.
\end{theorem}

Both follow from \texttt{tendsto\_finset\_sum} applied to the componentwise
convergence.

\section{Conditioning inequalities (\texttt{Conditioning.lean})}

Lattice analogues of Glimm--Jaffe, \S10.1--10.2 (pp.~193--194).

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_beta\_rescale}]
$Z(J, h, \beta) = Z(\beta J, \beta h, 1)$: the partition function
depends on $(J, h, \beta)$ only through $(\beta J, \beta h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_beta}; Cor.~10.2.3]
For $J \ge 0$, $h \ge 0$, and $0 < \beta_1 \le \beta_2$:
$Z(J, h, \beta_1) \le Z(J, h, \beta_2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By the rescaling identity, $Z(J,h,\beta) = Z(\beta J, \beta h, 1)$.
Since $\beta J$ and $\beta h$ are monotone in $\beta$ for $J, h \ge 0$,
the result follows from \texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_J} and
\texttt{partitionFunction\_monotone\_h}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Partition function bounds (Cor.~10.3.2)}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{hamiltonian\_abs\_le}]
$|H(\sigma)| \le |J| \cdot |E| + |h| \cdot |\iota|$, since
$|\text{edgeSpin}| \le 1$ and $|\text{sign}(\sigma_i)| \le 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_upper}]
$Z \le 2^{|\iota|} \cdot \exp(|\beta|(|J| \cdot |E| + |h| \cdot |\iota|))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_lower}]
$\exp(-|\beta|(|J| \cdot |E| + |h| \cdot |\iota|)) \le Z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_upper\_bound}]
For $|\iota| > 0$,
\[
\texttt{freeEnergy}\,G\,p \;\le\; \log 2
  + \frac{|\beta|(|J| \cdot |E| + |h| \cdot |\iota|)}{|\iota|}.
\]
Take $\log$ of \texttt{partitionFunction\_upper} and use
$|\text{Config}| = 2^{|\iota|}$, then divide by $|\iota|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion\_upper\_bound}]
For nonempty $\Lambda.\text{volume}\,n$,
\[
\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,p\,n \;\le\; \log 2
  + \frac{|\beta|(|J| \cdot |E_n| + |h| \cdot |\Lambda_n|)}{|\Lambda_n|},
\]
specialization of \texttt{freeEnergy\_upper\_bound} at each stage.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Free-spin / one-body limit \texorpdfstring{$(G = \bot)$}{(G = bottom)}}

Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, opening of \S 4 (free spin).
Regardless of $J$, if the ambient graph is $\bot$ (no edges), the
interaction term disappears.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{hamiltonian\_bot}]
$H_{\bot, p}(\sigma) = -h \sum_{i \in \iota} \operatorname{sign}(\sigma_i)$.
\texttt{edgeFinset\_bot}: $(\bot).\text{edgeFinset} = \emptyset$, so the
$J$-term is an empty sum and is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{sum\_exp\_spin\_sign}]
$\sum_{s \in \{\pm 1\}} \exp(\beta h \cdot s) = 2 \cosh(\beta h)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_bot}]
$Z_{\bot, p} = (2 \cosh(\beta h))^{|\iota|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\texttt{hamiltonian\_bot} + $\exp(-\beta H) = \prod_i \exp(\beta h \cdot \operatorname{sign}(\sigma_i))$.
The finite product-sum rule \texttt{Finset.sum\_prod\_piFinset} gives
$\sum_\sigma \prod_i f(\sigma_i) = \prod_i \sum_s f(s)$.
The one-site sum is closed by \texttt{sum\_exp\_spin\_sign}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_bot}]
For $|\iota| > 0$,
\[
  f(\bot, p) = \log(2 \cosh(\beta h)).
\]
Apply \texttt{Real.log\_pow} to \texttt{partitionFunction\_bot} and divide
by $|\iota|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_bot\_h\_zero}]
For $|\iota| > 0$ and arbitrary $J, \beta \in \mathbb R$,
\[
  f(\bot, \langle J, 0, \beta \rangle) = \log 2.
\]
This follows immediately from \texttt{freeEnergy\_bot} and $\cosh 0 = 1$.
The parameter $J$ is arbitrary because the $J$-term is empty on $\bot$.
It extends PR \#120 \texttt{freeEnergy\_zero\_params} ($J = h = 0$) to
arbitrary $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunction\_beta\_zero}]
$Z_G(\langle J, h, 0 \rangle) = |\text{Config}\,\iota|$.
When $-\beta = 0$, the Boltzmann weight is $\exp 0 = 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_beta\_zero}]
For $|\iota| > 0$ and arbitrary $J, h, G$,
\[
  f(G, \langle J, h, 0 \rangle) = \log 2.
\]
This is the $\beta$-direction analogue of PR \#120
\texttt{freeEnergy\_zero\_params}.
\texttt{partitionFunction\_beta\_zero} + \texttt{Real.log\_pow} + $|\iota|^{-1}$ cancel.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion\_beta\_zero}; PR \#132]
For nonempty $\Lambda.\text{volume}\,n$,
$\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle J, h, 0 \rangle\,n = \log 2$.
Specialize by \texttt{change} and definitional unfolding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite\_beta\_zero}; PR \#133]
Assume $\Lambda.\text{volume}\,n$ is nonempty for every $n$:
$\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle J, h, 0 \rangle = \log 2$.
Rewrite to a constant sequence and close with \texttt{Filter.limsup\_const}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion\_zero\_params}; PR \#162]
For nonempty $\Lambda.\text{volume}\,n$,
$\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle 0, 0, \beta \rangle\,n = \log 2$.
Use \texttt{change} and definitional unfolding to specialize
\texttt{IsingModel.freeEnergy\_zero\_params}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite\_zero\_params}; PR \#162]
Assume $\Lambda.\text{volume}\,n$ is nonempty for every $n$:
$\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle 0, 0, \beta \rangle = \log 2$.
Reuse the structure of \texttt{freeEnergyInfinite\_beta\_zero} through
\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion\_zero\_params}. This gives the maximal
entropy value from the $J = h = 0$ pair, where the Hamiltonian is
identically zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion\_zero\_params}; PR \#163]
For every $n$,
\[
  \texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle 0, 0, \beta \rangle\,n
    = 2^{|\Lambda_n|}.
\]
\texttt{IsingModel.partitionFunction\_zero\_params} is specialized directly,
then combined with
\texttt{card\_config\_eq\_two\_pow} + \texttt{Fintype.card\_coe}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{log\_partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion\_zero\_params}; PR \#163]
For every $n$,
\[
  \log \texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle 0, 0, \beta \rangle\,n
    = |\Lambda_n| \cdot \log 2.
\]
This is the composition of the preceding theorem with \texttt{Real.log\_pow}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion\_beta\_zero}; PR \#164]
For every $n$ and arbitrary $J, h \in \mathbb R$,
\[
  \texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle J, h, 0 \rangle\,n
    = 2^{|\Lambda_n|}.
\]
Specialize \texttt{IsingModel.partitionFunction\_beta\_zero}. At
$\beta = 0$, the Boltzmann weight satisfies $\exp(-\beta H) = 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{log\_partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion\_beta\_zero}; PR \#164]
Under the same assumptions,
\[
  \log \texttt{partitionFunctionAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,\langle J, h, 0 \rangle\,n
    = |\Lambda_n| \cdot \log 2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergy\_ge\_log\_two\_of\_ferromagnetic}; PR \#168]
For $0 < |\iota|$ and ferromagnetic $p$,
\[
  \log 2 \;\le\; f_G(p).
\]
\texttt{freeEnergy\_ge\_log\_two\_cosh}, \texttt{Real.one\_le\_cosh}, and
monotonicity of logarithm. The existing $\Lambda$ version
\texttt{freeEnergy\LeanLambda\_ge\_log\_two} (PR \#125) is refactored here into a
thin wrapper around the base identity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite\_eq\_of\_tendsto}; PR \#170]
Assuming
$\texttt{Tendsto}\,(\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,p)\,
\texttt{atTop}\,(\mathcal N (L))$,
\[
  \texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p \;=\; L.
\]
Combine the definition \texttt{freeEnergyInfinite := Filter.limsup} with
\texttt{Filter.Tendsto.limsup\_eq}. This infrastructure identifies the value
of \texttt{freeEnergyInfinite} once Fekete convergence is available.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Glimm--Jaffe \S 4.6 Prop 4.6.1 (Fekete convergence);
PR \#192]
Under the following bundled assumptions, expressing a disjoint-tower
exhaustion condition, the free-energy density converges:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\forall m, n, |\Lambda_{m+n}| = |\Lambda_m| + |\Lambda_n|$
        (cardinality additivity)
  \item $\forall m, n, \log Z_{\Lambda_m} + \log Z_{\Lambda_n}
          \le \log Z_{\Lambda_{m+n}}$ (super-additivity)
  \item $\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,p$ is bounded above
  \item $|\Lambda_1| \neq 0$
\end{itemize}
Under these assumptions,
\[
  \texttt{Tendsto}\,(\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,p)\,
    \texttt{atTop}\,
    (\mathcal N (\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p)).
\]
Proof: $u_n := -\log Z_{\Lambda_n}$ is \texttt{Subadditive} by sign reversal
of super-additivity. Cardinality additivity gives
$|\Lambda_n| = n \cdot |\Lambda_1|$ by induction. Apply mathlib
\texttt{Subadditive.tendsto\_lim} (Fekete) to obtain $u_n / n \to \ell$.
The ratio is
\[
  \texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,p\,n
    = -(u_n / n) / |\Lambda_1|
\]
for $n \ge 1$, so the \texttt{Tendsto} result transfers.
\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite\_eq\_of\_tendsto} identifies the limit value.

This completes the Fekete stage of Proposition 4.6.1; together with the
existing disjoint-union super-additivity, upper bound, and divergence
infrastructure, the targeted exhaustion class is covered.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Glimm--Jaffe \S 4.6 Prop 4.6.1, \emph{unconditional} on the
cubic exhaustion of $\mathbb Z^d$; PR \#3898,
\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion\_latticeGraph\_cubicExhaustion\_tendsto}]
For ferromagnetic parameters $p$ and every $d$, the free-energy density along
the cubic boxes $B_n = [-n,n]^d \cap \mathbb Z^d$ converges, with no
super-additivity, cardinality-additivity, or translation-tower hypotheses:
\[
  \texttt{Tendsto}\,
    (\texttt{freeEnergyAlongExhaustion}\,(\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d)\,
      (\texttt{cubicExhaustion}\,d)\,p)\, \texttt{atTop}\,
    (\mathcal N(\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite})).
\]
Proof (tiling--liminf; \texttt{Concrete/CubicTiling.lean},
\texttt{Concrete/CubicFreeEnergy.lean}). Fix a radius $r$ and set
$s = 2r+1$. The translates of $B_r$ centred at $s k$, $k \in B_M$, are
pairwise disjoint (\texttt{cubicTile\_disjoint}; the spacing exceeds the
diameter) and tile $B_{sM+r}$ exactly (\texttt{biUnion\_cubicTile};
Euclidean division of $x_i + r$ by $s$). Family super-additivity of
$\log Z$ over disjoint families
(\texttt{log\_partitionFunction\(\Lambda\)\_latticeGraph\_biUnion\_super\_additive},
Finset induction over the binary disjoint-union estimate) and translation
invariance give $(2M+1)^d \log Z_{B_r} \le \log Z_{B_{sM+r}}$
(\texttt{log\_partitionFunction\(\Lambda\)\_cubicBox\_tiling\_le}). With the
inner radius $R_N = s\lfloor (N-r)/s\rfloor + r \le N$ (within $2r$ of $N$)
and the monotonicity of $\log Z$ along nested cubes, the exact cardinality
factorisation $(2M+1)^d (2r+1)^d = (2R_N+1)^d$ yields
$\frac{|B_{R_N}|}{|B_N|}\, f_r \le f_N$
(\texttt{ratio\_mul\_freeEnergy\(\Lambda\)\_cubicBox\_le}). The volume
ratio tends to $1$
(\texttt{tendsto\_cubicBox\_innerRadius\_card\_ratio}; the side ratio is
squeezed between $1 - 4r/(2N+1)$ and $1$), so every stage value satisfies
$f_r \le \liminf_N f_N$
(\texttt{freeEnergy\(\Lambda\)\_cubicBox\_le\_liminf}). Taking the
$\limsup$ over $r$ gives $\limsup \le \liminf$; with the uniform upper
bound (bounded edge density) and ferromagnetic non-negativity,
\texttt{tendsto\_of\_le\_liminf\_of\_limsup\_le} concludes, the limit
being $\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite} = \limsup$ by definition. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Proposition 4.6.1,
p.~68.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.3: the zero-field four-point Lebowitz inequality and
the deletion of the \texttt{lebowitz\_four} axiom; PR \#3909]
For ferromagnetic parameters at $h = 0$ and four distinct sites,
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_k\sigma_l\rangle \le
\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\sigma_l\rangle +
\langle\sigma_i\sigma_k\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_l\rangle +
\langle\sigma_i\sigma_l\rangle\langle\sigma_j\sigma_k\rangle$
(equivalently $U_4 \le 0$;
\texttt{lebowitz\_four\_zero\_field}). Proof: the binomial expansions of
the doubled $t/q$ products give the powerset formulas
$\langle t^A\rangle_2 = \sum_{S \subseteq A} c_S c_{A\setminus S}$,
$\langle q^B\rangle_2 = \sum_T (-1)^{|B\setminus T|} c_T c_{B\setminus T}$,
and $\langle t^A q^B\rangle_2 = \sum_S \sum_T (-1)^{|B\setminus T|}
c_{S\cup T}\, c_{(A\setminus S)\cup(B\setminus T)}$ (disjoint merges);
applying \texttt{cor\_4\_3\_2\_tq} with $A = \{i,j\}$, $B = \{k,l\}$,
evaluating over the two pairs, and killing the odd correlations by the
zero-field spin-flip symmetry yields the inequality. \textbf{The
formalisation exposed that the former \texttt{lebowitz\_four} axiom was
false as stated}: its $h = 0$ specialisation asserts $U_4 \le
-2\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle\langle\sigma_k\sigma_l\rangle$, refuted by
two disjoint strongly coupled edges with vanishing cross-correlations. The
axiom is deleted; its only consumer (\texttt{cor\_4\_3\_3}) follows from
the corrected inequality directly. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum
Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.3, Corollaries 4.3.2--4.3.3, pp.~60--61; J.~L.
Lebowitz, Comm.\ Math.\ Phys.\ 35 (1974).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.3 Corollary 4.3.2: the Lebowitz $t/q$ inequalities;
PR \#3908]
For ferromagnetic Ising parameters, with the unnormalised doubled variables
$t_i = \xi_i + \chi_i$, $q_i = \xi_i - \chi_i$ (GJ's $\sqrt2$ factors are
positive scalars), the three once-subtracted inequalities hold:
$0 \le \langle t^A t^B\rangle - \langle t^A\rangle\langle t^B\rangle$,
$0 \le \langle q^A q^B\rangle - \langle q^A\rangle\langle q^B\rangle$,
$0 \le \langle t^A\rangle\langle q^B\rangle - \langle t^A q^B\rangle$
(\texttt{cor\_4\_3\_2\_tt}/\texttt{\_qq}/\texttt{\_tq}). Each difference
lifts through the pair factorisation $\langle F(\xi,\chi)G(\xi',\chi')
\rangle_4 = \langle F\rangle_2\langle G\rangle_2$ to a fourfold expectation
of an all-plus factor times a once-subtracted bracket; the inverse rotation
$t = (u_1+u_2)/2$, $q = (u_3-u_4)/2$, $q' = (u_3+u_4)/2$ (matching the
even-subgroup $u_4$ orientation) and the \texttt{Finset.prod\_add} subset
expansions give the double sum with coefficients $2^{-|A|-|B|}(1 -
(-1)^{|B\setminus T|}) \ge 0$ — GJ's ferromagnicity of the brackets — and
the exponent-level Theorem 4.3.1 makes every term non-negative. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.3, Corollary 4.3.2,
p.~60.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.3 Theorem 4.3.1: fourfold duplicate-variable
infrastructure; PR \#3907]
On the sixteen-point fourfold single-site Ising space
$(\xi, \chi, \xi', \chi') \in \{\pm1\}^4$, the Hadamard variables
$u_1 = \xi{+}\chi{+}\xi'{+}\chi'$, $u_2 = \xi{+}\chi{-}\xi'{-}\chi'$,
$u_3 = \xi{-}\chi{+}\xi'{-}\chi'$, $u_4 = -\xi{+}\chi{+}\xi'{-}\chi'$
($u_4$ is the \emph{negative} of GJ's $2\delta$ from (4.3.2); the sign is
flipped so that the generic sign patterns form the even subgroup — with the
original sign the all-odd moment is negative for the discrete Ising
single-site measure, and the theorem is stated for the sign-flipped
variables; the downstream corollaries use the brackets $q' \pm q$, which
match this orientation) have non-negative joint moments
(\texttt{siteMoment\_nonneg}) — the Ising replacement of Glimm--Jaffe's
$\varphi^4$ single-site computation (4.3.6): the sixteen points split into
eight aligned points $u = \pm 4 e_r$, contributing $(1 + (-1)^e)$ pair sums
against non-negative bases, and eight generic points $u = 2s$ with
$s_1s_2s_3s_4 = +1$, whose character sum factorises as
$\tfrac12\bigl(\prod_i (1 + (-1)^{e_i}) + \prod_i (1 - (-1)^{e_i})\bigr)$ —
manifestly non-negative with no parity case analysis. The fourfold system
(four independent copies with product weight) has $Z_4 = Z^4$ and the
factorisation $\langle F(\xi)G(\chi)H(\xi')K(\chi')\rangle_4 = \langle
F\rangle\langle G\rangle\langle H\rangle\langle K\rangle$
(\texttt{quadExpectation\_factor}); the site-indexed Hadamard variables and
their \texttt{Finset} products are the objects of Theorem 4.3.1, toward
discharging the \texttt{lebowitz\_four}/\texttt{lebowitz\_third}/%
\texttt{lebowitz\_inductive} axioms (Issue \#3906). \textbf{Theorem 4.3.1
(Ising form) is proven} (\texttt{theorem\_4\_3\_1}): per edge the Hadamard
orthogonality (4.3.5) gives $\xi_i\xi_j + \chi_i\chi_j + \xi'_i\xi'_j +
\chi'_i\chi'_j = \tfrac14\sum_r u_r(i)u_r(j)$ and the field term is
$h\,u_1(i)$, so the fourfold weight is $\exp$ of a ferromagnetic sum of
joint $u$-monomials (\texttt{quadWeight\_eq\_exp}); the exponential-of-sum
closure (\texttt{hasNonnegUMoments\_exp\_sum\_mul}, built on the series
closure \texttt{HasNonnegUMoments.mul\_exp} — the $\cosh/\sinh$ closed form
of the GKS route does not apply to the multi-valued Hadamard variables)
reduces all joint moments to the single-site positivity, and dividing by
$Z^4 > 0$ yields $0 \le \langle u_1^A u_2^B u_3^C u_4^D\rangle_4$ for
ferromagnetic parameters. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.3, Theorem 4.3.1,
pp.~59--61; J.~L. Lebowitz, Comm.\ Math.\ Phys.\ 35 (1974).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Theorem 4.6.2: analyticity of the infinite-volume
free energy; PR \#3905]
For positive real ferromagnetic parameters ($0 < \beta$, $0 < J$) with bounded
edge density and a field-uniform real-axis convergence input (supplied either
by the disjoint-tower Fekete theorem or, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with the cubic
exhaustion, by the tiling--liminf Proposition 4.6.1), there is a single
function $g$ analytic on the Lee--Yang cone $\{|\mathrm{Im}\,h| <
\mathrm{Re}\,h\}$ with $g(x) = f_\infty(\beta, J, x)$ for every real $x > 0$
(\texttt{freeEnergyComplex\_infiniteVolume\_analyticOnNhd\_leeYangDomain},
fully instantiated $\mathbb Z^d$ form
\texttt{\_latticeGraph\_cubic} assuming only $0 < \beta$, $0 < J$).
Proof structure: (i) \emph{exact real-axis agreement}
(\texttt{globalBranchStage\_real\_eq}): along the real segment from the
anchor, $\operatorname{Im} g_m$ is continuous, $(2\pi/N_m)\mathbb Z$-valued
(the exponential identity with positive real $Z$ forces $\sin = 0$,
$\cos > 0$), and vanishes at the anchor, hence vanishes identically by the
intermediate value theorem against the half-multiple
(\texttt{eq\_zero\_of\_continuousOn\_int\_multiples}); injectivity of the
real exponential then gives $g_m(x) = F_m(x)$. (ii) The subsequential
compact-target patch is identified with $f_\infty$ at every positive real
field of its open neighbourhood (real Fekete convergence along the
subsequence; the disjoint-tower input of the patch chain is generalised to a
bare convergence hypothesis). (iii) \emph{Globalisation}
(\texttt{exists\_convex\_tube\_patch}): the patch over the segment from the
anchor restricts to a convex open thickening tube around the segment; any
two tubes meet in a convex open set containing a real interval accumulating
at the anchor, where both patches equal $f_\infty$, so the identity theorem
for analytic functions glues all patches into one global $g$. Reference:
Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2,
pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: the unconditional subsequential
compact-target patch; PR \#3904]
For positive real ferromagnetic parameters ($0 < \beta$, $0 < J$) with bounded
edge density and the disjoint-tower hypotheses, and any compact
$K \subseteq \{|\mathrm{Im}\,h| < \mathrm{Re}\,h\}$ containing the physical
field $h$, there exist an open $U$ with $K \subseteq U$ inside the cone, a
strictly monotone stage subsequence $\sigma$, and $g$ holomorphic on $U$ which
is the pointwise limit on $U$ of the subsequenced global branch logarithms
$g_{\sigma(m)}$ (locally uniformly on each cover ball) with
$g(h) = f_\infty(\beta, J, h)$ — \emph{no analytic side hypotheses remain}
(\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_posReal\_globalBranch\_holomorphicExtension\_of\_isCompact},
with the $\mathbb Z^d$ wrapper \texttt{\_isCompact\_latticeGraph}).
Construction: (i) any branch with the exponential identity has derivative
$Z'/(NZ)$ (\texttt{deriv\_eq\_globalLogDerivStage\_of\_exp\_eq}; the
non-vanishing of $Z$ is automatic from the identity); (ii) $Z'/(NZ)$ is
bounded stage-uniformly on compacts by quarter-ball Schwarz estimates over
the existing half-ball Borel--Carath\'eodory branch bounds with a finite
subcover
(\texttt{exists\_uniform\_norm\_globalLogDerivStage\_on\_isCompact}); (iii)
hence the global branch is bounded stage-uniformly on compacts via the
segment-integral estimate over the compact segment tube
(\texttt{exists\_uniform\_norm\_globalBranchStage\_on\_isCompact}); (iv) the
all-centre principal normalisation threaded through the existing
compact-open diagonal extraction is never consumed by the extraction itself,
so unnormalised twins (\texttt{compactOpen\_vitali\_fin\_ball\_unnormalised},
\texttt{\_overlap}, \texttt{\_patch} — fully generic in the analytic family)
drop it; (v) covering $K$ by the halved global-branch balls (one centred at
$h$), the closure-carrier compactness and derived equicontinuity supply the
compact-open carriers, overlap is trivial (every centre selects the same
global function), and the diagonal extraction patches to a holomorphic $g$
on $K$; (vi) the identification $g(h) = f_\infty$ follows at the real centre
from the anchored normalisation $g_m(h) = F_m(h)$ and the established
real-centre subsequence identification. Remaining toward the full GJ
statement: identification along the real axis (not only at the single
physical field), globalisation to one function on the whole Lee--Yang
domain, and the full-sequence upgrade (a consequence of the previous two by
uniqueness of limits). Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6,
Theorem 4.6.2, pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: the global branch on the convex
Lee--Yang cone; PR \#3903]
The eventual-overlap input of the overlap-only endpoint is satisfiable by a
\emph{global} per-stage branch. First, a segment-primitive lemma with no
Goursat-type input: on a convex open $U \subseteq \mathbb C$ with $b \in U$,
for $f$ differentiable on $U$ with continuous derivative, the primitive
$g(z) = \int_0^1 (z-b) f(b + t(z-b))\,dt$ (\texttt{segmentPrimitive})
satisfies $g' = f$ on $U$ (\texttt{hasDerivAt\_segmentPrimitive}): the
$z$-derivative of the integrand equals
$\frac{d}{dt}[t\,f(b+t(z-b))]$, so differentiation under the integral sign
(dominated on a compact tube around the segment, mathlib's
\texttt{hasDerivAt\_integral\_of\_dominated\_loc\_of\_deriv\_le}) followed by
the fundamental theorem of calculus yields $f(z)$; mathlib lacks
triangle-Goursat/simply-connected primitives, and this route avoids them.
Applied to the Lee--Yang cone $\{|\mathrm{Im}\,h| < \mathrm{Re}\,h\}$
(convex) with $f = Z_m'/(N_m Z_m)$ (holomorphic there by Lee--Yang
non-vanishing, \texttt{globalLogDerivStage}), the anchored primitive
$g_m = F_m(b) + \int$ (\texttt{globalBranchStage}) is holomorphic on the
whole cone with $g_m(b) = F_m(b)$ and $\exp(N_m g_m) = Z_m$
(\texttt{exp\_card\_mul\_globalBranchStage}: the ratio $\exp(N_m g_m)/Z_m$
has zero derivative, is constant on the convex domain, and equals $1$ at $b$
by the principal-logarithm identity). Choosing this single function as the
selected branch at every Lee--Yang centre produces all-stage branch data
satisfying the eventual-overlap predicate trivially
(\texttt{exists\_globalLeeYangAllStageBranchData}). Reference: Glimm--Jaffe,
\emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2, pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: the overlap-only positive-real
endpoint; PR \#3902]
Composing the supplied Ascoli inputs reduces the conditional Vitali pipeline for
GJ Theorem 4.6.2 to a single analytic hypothesis. Define \emph{eventual branch
overlap} (\texttt{LeeYangAllStageBranchData.OverlapEventually}): for every pair
of Lee--Yang centres $h_0, h_1$ the selected stage branches eventually agree on
$B(h_0, r(h_0)) \cap B(h_1, r(h_1))$. Halving the radii preserves the predicate
(\texttt{OverlapEventually.half}; the halved intersection is contained in the
original one). For positive real ferromagnetic parameters and a compact target
$K$ inside the Lee--Yang domain containing the physical field: construct the
closed-ball all-stage branch data, pass to its half-radius restriction (the
exposed witness), and extract the finite cover geometry by compactness. The
stage-uniform Borel--Carath\'eodory bound of PR \#3900 lands exactly on the full
selected balls of the halved data (the halved radius is definitionally $r/2$
with unchanged branch family), so the closedness-free closure-carrier
constructor of PR \#3901 (equicontinuity derived per PR \#3899) produces the
relative-compactness data from the bound and the (halved) overlap alone
(\texttt{RangeRelCompactCOpenData.ofHalfUniformBoundOverlap}). The established
relative-compactness patch then yields the cover limit family and a function
$g$ holomorphic on $K$ with $g(h) = f_\infty$
(\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_closedBallUniformBoundOverlap\_patch},
\texttt{\_of\_isCompact}). Headline:
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_posRealUniformBoundOverlap\_patch\_of\_isCompact}
exposes $\exists\, \text{data}, \exists\, \text{geometry}$ such that
\emph{eventual overlap alone} implies the patch conclusion, and the consumer
corollary
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_posRealOverlap\_holomorphicExtension\_of\_isCompact}
returns the holomorphic extension with the infinite-volume free-energy value at
the physical field. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed.,
\S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2, pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: closure-carrier Arzel\`a--Ascoli
handoffs; PR \#3901]
The range-image closedness input of the Ascoli data is unnecessary on the closure-carrier
route: for $S \subseteq C(X, \mathbb C)$ with pointwise norm bounds, the closure
$\overline{\iota(S)}$ of the pointwise image is closed by definition and lies in the compact
product of closed balls (\texttt{closure\_minimal} against the compact-hence-closed product),
hence is compact
(\texttt{isCompact\_closure\_toFun\_image\_complex\_of\_norm\_le}). If $S$ is
equicontinuous, so is the closure (\texttt{Set.Equicontinuous.closure}), and its members are
continuous; therefore the carrier $\iota^{-1}(\overline{\iota(S)})$ projects exactly onto the
closure and is compact in the compact-open topology
(\texttt{isCompact\_closureCarrier\_compactOpen\_complex\_of\_norm\_le\_equicontinuous},
via mathlib's Arzel\`a--Ascoli). The relative-compactness data of the Vitali pipeline is then
built without the closedness field
(\texttt{RangeRelCompactCOpenData.ofClosureCarrier}, with the closed-ball branch-deviation
wrapper consuming the PR \#3899 fields except closedness). Reference: Glimm--Jaffe,
\emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2, pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: stage-uniform branch and deviation
bounds on half-radius balls via Borel--Carath\'eodory; PR \#3900]
Let $f_m$ be the centre-normalised stage branches on a selected Lee--Yang ball $B(c,r)$ with
$\overline B(c,r)$ inside the Lee--Yang domain, and let $A$ be the unconditional compact
free-energy bound on $\overline B(c,r)$
(\texttt{exists\_norm\_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_le\_leeYang\_of\_isCompact}).
The exponential identity gives $\operatorname{Re} f_m = \log\|Z_m\|/N_m
= \operatorname{Re} F_m$ (\texttt{re\_eq\_log\_norm\_div\_of\_exp\_eq},
\texttt{re\_freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_eq}), hence
$\operatorname{Re} f_m \le A$ on $B(c,r)$. The centred Borel--Carath\'eodory estimate
(\texttt{norm\_le\_of\_re\_le\_on\_half}, from mathlib's
\texttt{Complex.borelCaratheodory}) yields, on $\overline B(c, r/2)$,
$\|f_m\| \le 2(A+1) + 3A =: C$ stage-uniformly (the centre value is $F_m(c)$, of norm
$\le A$), and the triangle inequality bounds the deviation
$\|f_m - F_m\| \le C + A \le 2C$. Halving the selected radii
(\texttt{LeeYangAllStageBranchData.half} and variants) exposes these bounds on the *full*
selected balls of the halved data, so for positive real ferromagnetic parameters
\texttt{exists\_uniform\_branchFamily\_bound\_half} supplies, unconditionally, the
\texttt{hbound}/\texttt{hdev} inputs of the PR \#3899 Ascoli constructor.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2,
pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: Ascoli side conditions for the
closed-ball branch-deviation data from a stage-uniform bound; PR \#3899]
Let the stage branches $f_m$ of a Lee--Yang all-stage branch family be analytic on a selected
ball $B(c,R)$ (\texttt{branch\_spec}) with a stage-uniform bound $\|f_m\| \le C$ there. Then:
(i) the Schwarz lemma applied on interior discs gives
$\|f_m'(\xi)\| \le 2C/\rho$ whenever $B(\xi,\rho) \subseteq B(c,R)$
(\texttt{norm\_deriv\_le\_of\_analyticOnNhd\_of\_bounded});
(ii) the mean-value inequality upgrades this to a uniform local Lipschitz estimate on
half-balls (\texttt{norm\_sub\_le\_of\_analyticOnNhd\_of\_bounded});
(iii) hence the family is pointwise equicontinuous on the subtype ball
(\texttt{equicontinuous\_restrict\_of\_analyticOnNhd\_of\_bounded}), and equicontinuity
transfers to range carriers by re-indexing along representatives
(\texttt{equicontinuous\_range\_coe}).
Consequently the six fields of the closed-ball branch-deviation Ascoli data of the latest
positive-real direct-range Vitali endpoint reduce to four inputs — range-image closedness, the
stage-uniform bound, the branch-deviation bound, and eventual overlap coherence — via the
constructor
\texttt{LeeYangPointwiseNormAllStageCompactRealClosedBallBranchDeviationAscoliData.ofUniformBound},
with a norm-bounded companion. The continuous restrictions and the restriction identity come
from \texttt{branchRestricted} (analytic $\Rightarrow$ continuous, subtype restriction).
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics}, 2nd ed., \S 4.6, Theorem 4.6.2,
pp.~68--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Support toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2: finite-volume complex $Z$ analyticity; PR \#193]
Preliminary support for GJ Theorem 4.6.2: after extending the finite-volume
partition function $Z_G(J, h, \beta)$ to $(J, h, \beta) \in \mathbb C^3$, it
is entire in each parameter separately:
\[
  Z_G^{\mathbb C}(J, h, \beta) = \sum_\sigma \exp(-\beta \cdot H^{\mathbb C}_G(J, h; \sigma)),
\]
$H^{\mathbb C}_G$ is affine in $(J, h)$. Hence each Boltzmann weight is
$\exp \circ$(affine) and entire, and the finite sum $Z$ is entire.
\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_analyticAt\_\{h,J,beta\}}.
This PR only covers separate-parameter analyticity of $Z$. The body of GJ
Theorem 4.6.2, namely complex analyticity of free energy on
$|\mathrm{Im}\,h| < \mathrm{Re}\,h$, joint analyticity, $\log Z$ via the
slit plane, and the infinite-volume Vitali step, is left to later PRs. Note
that in mathlib, \texttt{Complex.log} is analytic only on \texttt{slitPlane}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2 continuation: $Z \in$ slitPlane on real slice; PR \#198]
\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_mem\_slitPlane\_of\_real}:
For real $p$, $Z^{\mathbb C}_G(p.J, p.h, p.\beta) \in \texttt{Complex.slitPlane}$.
Proof: PR \#196 real-complex compatibility and \texttt{partitionFunction\_pos}
($Z > 0$) give positive real part and zero imaginary part. This is the
\texttt{Or.inl} branch of the slit-plane condition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2 continuation: \texttt{freeEnergy} real-complex compat; PR \#197]
\texttt{freeEnergy\_ofReal\_eq\_freeEnergyComplex}:
For real parameters $p$,
$((\texttt{freeEnergy}\,G\,p : \mathbb R) : \mathbb C) = \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}\,G\,(J:\mathbb C)\,(h:\mathbb C)\,(\beta:\mathbb C)$.
Proof: use the $Z$ compatibility from PR \#196 and
\texttt{partitionFunction\_pos} ($Z > 0$), then apply
\texttt{Complex.ofReal\_log}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2 continuation: real-complex compatibility; PR \#196]
\texttt{partitionFunction\_ofReal\_eq\_partitionFunctionComplex}:
For real parameters $p = \langle J, h, \beta\rangle$, coercing
$(\texttt{partitionFunction}\,G\,p : \mathbb R)$ to $\mathbb C$ gives
$\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex}\,G\,(J:\mathbb C)\,(h:\mathbb C)\,(\beta:\mathbb C)$.
Proof: \texttt{Complex.ofReal} is a ring homomorphism, so it commutes with
finite sums, exponentials, and each site's spin sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2 continuation: joint analyticity in $(J,h,\beta)$; PR \#195]
\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_analyticAt\_joint}:
The map $(J, h, \beta) \in \mathbb C^3 \mapsto Z_G^{\mathbb C}$ is entire.
\texttt{freeEnergyComplex\_analyticAt\_joint}: $Z \in$ \texttt{slitPlane}
at a point where $f_G^{\mathbb C}$ is also jointly analytic.
Proof: by the definitions $H_J = -J \cdot \text{edgeSum}$ and
$H_h = -h \cdot \text{siteSum}$, the exponent
$-\beta(H_J + H_h) = \beta \cdot (J \cdot \text{edgeSum} + h \cdot \text{siteSum})$
is polynomial in $(J, h, \beta)$. Use
\texttt{analyticAt\_fst}/\texttt{analyticAt\_snd} for projections and compose
with \texttt{add}/\texttt{mul}/\texttt{neg}. Then
\texttt{AnalyticAt.cexp'} plus \texttt{Finset.analyticAt\_fun\_sum} gives
entireness of $Z$, and \texttt{AnalyticAt.clog} plus
\texttt{analyticAt\_const.mul} gives analyticity of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2 continuation: \texttt{freeEnergyComplex} analyticity via slitPlane; PR \#194]
Following PR \#193, where $Z$ is entire in each parameter separately, at a
point with $Z(J, h_0, \beta) \in \texttt{Complex.slitPlane}$,
\[
  \texttt{AnalyticAt}\,\mathbb C\,
    (h \mapsto \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}\,G\,J\,h\,\beta)\,h_0
\]
with analogous statements for the other two parameters. Proof: compose
mathlib \texttt{AnalyticAt.clog}
(\texttt{Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Analytic}) with
multiplication by a constant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lee-Yang domain infrastructure (support toward GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2); PR \#199]
Support lemmas toward the eventual completion of GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2
(pp.~67--70). The following are independent auxiliary results, not
statements of GJ itself:
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{leeYangDomain} $= \{h \in \mathbb C : |\mathrm{Im}\,h| < \mathrm{Re}\,h\}$
 is open, is a subset of \texttt{slitPlane}, and contains the positive
 real axis.
\item \texttt{leeYangFugacity}$(\beta, h) := e^{-2\beta h}$ is entire
 on $\beta, h \in \mathbb C$, and on the Lee-Yang domain with
 $\beta > 0$ it satisfies $\|\cdot\| < 1$ (i.e. maps into the open
 unit disk).
\item \texttt{leeYangNormalization}$(\beta, J, h, |E|, |\iota|)
 := \exp(\beta J |E| + \beta h |\iota|)$ is entire, non-vanishing, and
 has positive real part at real parameters.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Friedli--Velenik factorisation; PR \#199]
\label{thm:friedli-velenik}
For real $\beta, J$ and complex uniform field $h \in \mathbb C$,
with finite graph $G$, $|\iota| = \texttt{Fintype.card}\,\iota$,
$|E| = G.\texttt{edgeFinset.card}$:
\[
  Z(J, h, \beta)
    = \exp(\beta J |E| + \beta h |\iota|) \cdot P_E(z),
\]
where $z_k = e^{-2\beta h}$ (uniform fugacity vector) and $P_E$ is the
Ising partition polynomial \texttt{isingEdgePoly}
(from \texttt{LeeYang.lean}, with
\texttt{graphToEdgeList}\,$G$\,$(e^{-2\beta J})$ as coefficients).
Proof: transport through the bijection
$\sigma \mapsto X := \{i : \sigma_i = \mathrm{down}\}$
(\texttt{configFinsetEquiv}) and, for each $\sigma$, expand
$\exp(-\beta H(\sigma))$ per-site and per-edge and identify
coefficients.
Lean name: \texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_eq\_normalization\_mul\_isingEdgePoly}.
Reference: Friedli--Velenik (3.63)--(3.65), pp.~122--123.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ Thm 4.6.2 non-vanishing half on Lee-Yang domain; PR \#199]
For real ferromagnetic $J > 0$, $\beta > 0$, and
$h \in \texttt{leeYangDomain}$,
$\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex}\,G\,(J:\mathbb C)\,h\,(\beta:\mathbb C)
\ne 0$.
The Friedli--Velenik identity (\ref{thm:friedli-velenik}) expresses
$Z$ as a non-vanishing normalisation times $P_E(z)$; the Lee-Yang
circle theorem
(\texttt{lee\_yang\_circle} / \texttt{isingEdgePoly\_nonvanishing\_of\_graph})
gives non-vanishing of the $P_E$ factor.
Lean name: \texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_ne\_zero\_on\_leeYangDomain}.

Note: non-vanishing does not directly give $Z \in \texttt{slitPlane}$.
Establishing slit-plane membership via continuous branch selection, and
hence completing the analyticity of \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}, is
handled in a later session.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real-slice slitPlane corollary (preliminary to GJ Thm 4.6.2); PR \#199]
For arbitrary real $J, h_0, \beta$,
$\texttt{AnalyticAt}\,\mathbb C\,
  (h \mapsto \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}\,G\,(J:\mathbb C)\,h\,(\beta:\mathbb C))\,
  (h_0:\mathbb C)$.
This is not the statement of GJ Thm 4.6.2 proper, but a simple
composition of
\texttt{partitionFunctionComplex\_mem\_slitPlane\_of\_real}
(at real parameters $Z > 0$ is real, hence in slit-plane) with
\texttt{freeEnergyComplex\_analyticAt\_h}. No assumption $J > 0$,
$\beta > 0$, or Lee-Yang-domain is required.
Lean name: \texttt{freeEnergyComplex\_analyticAt\_h\_ofReal}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[GJ Thm 4.6.2 finite-volume local branch on Lee-Yang domain; PR \#200]
For real ferromagnetic $\beta > 0$, $J > 0$, with
\texttt{[Nonempty }$\iota$\texttt{]}, at any
$h_0 \in \texttt{leeYangDomain}$ there exists an analytic function
$f : \mathbb C \to \mathbb C$ such that
$\texttt{AnalyticAt}\,\mathbb C\,f\,h_0$,
$\exp(|\iota| f(h_0)) = Z(h_0)$, and
$f(h_0) = \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}\,G\,(J:\mathbb C)\,h_0\,(\beta:\mathbb C)$.
Proof chain:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Z'/Z$ analytic on Lee-Yang (\texttt{logDeriv\_...\_analyticOnNhd\_leeYangDomain}).
\item Morera gives a primitive on each ball contained in the domain
  (\texttt{DifferentiableOn.isExactOn\_ball}, mathlib), producing $g$
  with $g' = Z'/Z$ (\texttt{exists\_logZ\_branch\_on\_ball\_of\_leeYangDomain}).
\item Normalise at the basepoint: $g(h_0) = \log Z(h_0)$
  (\texttt{\_normalised\_}).
\item Show $F(z) := \exp(g(z))/Z(z)$ has zero derivative on the ball
  (chain + quotient rules); the ball is connected, hence $F$ is
  constant. At the centre, $F(h_0) = \exp(\log Z(h_0))/Z(h_0) = 1$,
  so $\exp g = Z$ pointwise on the ball.
\item $g$ is \texttt{DifferentiableOn} an open set $\Rightarrow$
  \texttt{AnalyticOnNhd}.
\item Take a ball around each $h_0$ to obtain a pointwise statement.
\item Set $f = g / |\iota|$ for the local branch of
  \texttt{freeEnergyComplex}.
\end{enumerate}
Lean names: \texttt{exists\_freeEnergyComplex\_analyticAt\_branch\_of\_leeYangDomain},
\texttt{analyticBranch\_freeEnergyComplex\_leeYangDomain}.

Note: the principal branch \texttt{Complex.log}($Z$) is discontinuous
where $Z$ crosses the negative real axis; the local branch $f$ is
continuous across such crossings. The statement
``log $Z$ is analytic'' intended by GJ Thm 4.6.2 is interpreted in the
local-branch sense.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$\infty$-vol Vitali lift preparation --- ingredients; PR \#200]
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{vitali\_bridge}: a direct wrapper of mathlib's
  \texttt{TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.differentiableOn}. A locally
  uniform limit of holomorphic functions on an open set is holomorphic.
\item \texttt{norm\_partitionFunctionComplex\_le\_partitionFunction}:
  $|Z(J, h, \beta)| \le Z(J, \mathrm{Re}\,h, \beta)$ (real Ising
  partition function).
\item \texttt{norm\_partitionFunctionComplex\_le\_trivial\_bound}:
  combining with the existing \texttt{partitionFunction\_upper},
  $|Z| \le 2^{|\iota|} \exp(|\beta|(|J||E| + |\mathrm{Re}\,h| \cdot |\iota|))$.
\item \texttt{norm\_complex\_log\_le}:
  $\|{\rm log}\,z\| \le |\log\|z\|| + \pi$.
\item \texttt{norm\_freeEnergyComplex\_le\_trivial\_bound}:
  $\|f_{\rm complex}\| \le (|\log\|Z\|| + \pi)/|\iota|$.
\end{itemize}
These are the ingredients for a Montel-style argument (locally uniform
boundedness + real-axis Fekete convergence) yielding locally uniform
convergence. Next step: formalise locally uniform convergence and
apply \texttt{vitali\_bridge\_leeYangDomain} to obtain analyticity of
the infinite-volume limit $f_\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional $\infty$-volume Vitali assembly for GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2; PR \#2673]
Let $G$ be an ambient graph with exhaustion $\Lambda_n$, and let
\[
  F_n(h)=\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,J\,h\,\beta\,n .
\]
The Lean theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_vitali\_bridge} states that,
on any open set $U\subseteq\mathbb C$, if every $F_n$ is holomorphic on
$U$ and $F_n\to f$ locally uniformly on $U$, then $f$ is holomorphic on
$U$. The specialization
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_vitali\_bridge\_leeYangDomain}
sets $U=\texttt{leeYangDomain}$.

The companion theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_limit\_eq\_freeEnergyInfinite\_at\_real}
adds the real-axis identification. If
\[
  F_n(h)\to f(h)
\]
locally uniformly on the Lee-Yang domain, and the real parameters satisfy
the existing \texttt{DisjointTowerHypotheses} and
\texttt{BoundedEdgeDensity} assumptions, then at a real point
$p.h\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}$,
\[
  f(p.h)=
  \bigl(\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p:\mathbb R\bigr):\mathbb C .
\]
The proof uses mathlib's pointwise consequence
\texttt{TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.tendsto\_at}, the previously
formalised real-axis convergence of
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}, and uniqueness of limits in
the Hausdorff space $\mathbb C$.
The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) non-real wrappers now live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/VitaliBridge/Bridge/OpenSet.lean
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/VitaliBridge/Bridge/LeeYangDomain.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and the real-axis wrappers live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/VitaliBridge/Real/Limit.lean
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/VitaliBridge/Real/Identified.lean
\end{Verbatim}
with the old Vitali bridge and branches import paths kept as re-exports.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Per-stage Lee-Yang local branches for the Vitali input; PR \#2674]
Let $G$ be an ambient graph with exhaustion $\Lambda_n$, and assume
that the induced edge set at each finite stage is finite.  For real
ferromagnetic parameters $\beta>0$ and $J>0$, the Lean theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_exists\_analyticAt\_branch\_leeYangDomain\_stage}
states that every nonempty stage $\Lambda_n$ inherits the finite-volume
Lee-Yang local branch theorem from PR \#200.  More explicitly, for each
$h_0\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ there is a function
$f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ such that
\[
  f \text{ is analytic at } h_0,\qquad
  \exp(|\Lambda_n|\,f(h_0)) = Z_{\Lambda_n}(h_0),
\]
and
\[
  f(h_0)=
  \texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,J\,h_0\,\beta\,n .
\]
The wrapper
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_analyticBranch\_leeYangDomain\_stage}
packages this in pointwise
$\forall h_0\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ form, and
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_analyticBranch\_leeYangDomain\_all\_stages}
packages the same statement for all stages under
$\forall n,\ \Lambda_n\ne\emptyset$.

The stronger ball-level wrapper
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_exists\_analyticOnNhd\_branch\_ball\_stage}
is the usable local-branch input for Vitali.  If
$B(h_0,r)\subseteq\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ and $r>0$, it gives
$f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ such that $f$ is analytic on a neighbourhood
of the ball and
\[
  \forall z\in B(h_0,r),\qquad
  \exp(|\Lambda_n|\,f(z))=Z_{\Lambda_n}(z).
\]
The all-stages form
\begin{Verbatim}
freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_analyticOnNhd_branch_ball_all_stages
\end{Verbatim}
packages this for every nonempty stage.  The concrete $\mathbb Z^d$
specializations are recorded in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/StageLeeYang/Stage/Ball/Basic.lean
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/StageLeeYang/AllStages/Ball.lean
\end{Verbatim}
with the old ball, all-stage, stage-Lee--Yang, and branches import paths
kept as re-exports.

These are local branch inputs for the normal-family/Vitali part of
GJ \S 4.6 Thm 4.6.2; they do not by themselves choose a coherent
global branch family or prove local uniform convergence of the chosen
branches.  The pointwise branch agrees with the principal
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion} value at the basepoint $h_0$,
while the local analytic representative may differ from the principal
\texttt{Complex.log} branch away from $h_0$.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalised Lee-Yang branch-ball witnesses for the Vitali input; PR \#2675]
The finite-volume theorem
\texttt{exists\_freeEnergyComplex\_analyticOnNhd\_branch\_ball\_strong}
strengthens the ball-level branch statement by keeping the centre
normalisation in the same witness.  For real ferromagnetic parameters
$\beta>0$, $J>0$, and nonempty finite volume, if
$B(h_0,r)\subseteq\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ and $r>0$, then there is
$f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ such that
\[
  f \text{ is analytic on a neighbourhood of } B(h_0,r),
\]
\[
  \forall z\in B(h_0,r),\qquad
  \exp(|\iota|\,f(z))=Z(z),
\]
and
\[
  f(h_0)=\texttt{freeEnergyComplex}\,G\,J\,h_0\,\beta .
\]
The proof applies the Morera-built log branch
\texttt{exists\_logZ\_analytic\_branch\_on\_ball} and sets
$f(z)=g(z)/|\iota|$; the nonempty-volume hypothesis gives
$|\iota|\ne 0$, while the basepoint equality follows from the stored
normalisation $g(h_0)=\log Z(h_0)$.

The along-exhaustion wrappers
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_exists\_analyticOnNhd\_branch\_ball\_stage\_strong}
and
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_analyticOnNhd\_branch\_ball\_all\_stages\_strong}
apply this theorem to the induced graph on $\Lambda_n$ for the same real
ferromagnetic parameter range.  Thus, at every nonempty stage, the same
local witness carries analyticity on the ball,
the ball-wide exponential identity for $Z_{\Lambda_n}$, and agreement
with the principal \texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion} value at
the centre.  This still does not prove coherent branch selection or
locally uniform convergence; it fixes the normalised local input that a
future normal-family/Vitali argument can consume.
The concrete $\mathbb Z^d$ stage wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/StageLeeYang/Stage/Ball/Strong.lean
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  Branches/StageLeeYang/AllStages/Strong.lean
\end{Verbatim}
with the old ball, all-stage, stage-Lee--Yang, and branches import paths
kept as re-exports.

Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local branch-family Vitali assembly on Lee--Yang balls; PR \#2676]
The theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_branchFamily\_vitali\_bridge\_ball}
packages the local Vitali handoff for a chosen branch family.  Let
$F_n:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be functions on a ball $B(h_0,r)$ such that each
$F_n$ is analytic on a neighbourhood of the ball, satisfies the ball-wide
branch identity
\[
  \forall z\in B(h_0,r),\qquad
  \exp(|\Lambda_n|\,F_n(z))=Z_{\Lambda_n}(z),
\]
and is normalised at the centre by
\[
  F_n(h_0)=
  \texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,J\,h_0\,\beta\,n .
\]
If $F_n$ converges locally uniformly on $B(h_0,r)$ to $f$, then $f$ is
holomorphic on $B(h_0,r)$.  The proof is the existing
\texttt{vitali\_bridge} applied to the analytic part of the branch witness.

The centre-identification theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_branchFamily\_vitali\_ball\_identified\_at\_center}
specialises the centre to a real parameter $h_0=p.h$.  Local uniform
convergence gives $F_n(p.h)\to f(p.h)$, while the normalisation above rewrites
this sequence to the principal stage free energies.  The real-axis Fekete
theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_tendsto\_at\_real\_of\_disjointTowerHypotheses}
then gives convergence to
\[
  \texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p .
\]
Uniqueness of limits identifies
\[
  f(p.h)=\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p .
\]
The concrete $\mathbb Z^d$ wrappers live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali/Ball/Bridge.lean
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali/Ball/Real.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and are re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali/Ball.lean
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali.lean
Branches/LocalCoverPatch.lean
\end{Verbatim}
paths.

This result does not construct the coherent branch family or prove its local
uniform convergence.  It records the exact local theorem that can consume that
future normal-family/Montel output.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local-cover branch-family Vitali handoff on Lee--Yang; PR \#2677]
The theorem
\texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion\_branchFamily\_vitali\_localCover}
packages the passage from local balls to the full Lee--Yang domain.  Suppose
that for every $h_0\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ there is a radius $r>0$ with
$B(h_0,r)\subseteq\texttt{leeYangDomain}$ and a branch family $F_n$ on that
ball satisfying the PR \#2676 hypotheses:
\[
  F_n\text{ analytic on }B(h_0,r),\qquad
  \exp(|\Lambda_n|F_n(z))=Z_{\Lambda_n}(z),
\]
\[
  F_n(h_0)=
  \texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,J\,h_0\,\beta\,n,
\]
and $F_n\to f$ locally uniformly on $B(h_0,r)$, with the same limiting
function $f$ for all centres.  Then $f$ is holomorphic on
\texttt{leeYangDomain}.  The proof applies the ball-level theorem at each
point and converts holomorphicity on the containing ball into
within-domain differentiability.

The real-centre theorem
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true,breakanywhere=true]
freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_vitali_localCover_real
\end{Verbatim}
adds the Fekete identification at a real Lee--Yang point $p.h$, assuming
\texttt{BoundedEdgeDensity} for $(G,\Lambda)$,
\texttt{DisjointTowerHypotheses} for $(G,\Lambda,p)$, and
$(p.h:\mathbb C)\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}$:
\[
  f(p.h)=\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p .
\]
It selects the local ball supplied by the cover at $p.h$ and reuses the
PR \#2676 centre-identification theorem.  The non-real concrete $\mathbb Z^d$
wrapper lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true,breakanywhere=true]
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali/LocalCover.lean
\end{Verbatim}
It is re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true,breakanywhere=true]
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/Vitali.lean
Branches/LocalCoverPatch.lean
\end{Verbatim}
paths.  The real wrapper lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true,breakanywhere=true]
Branches/RealCompact/Vitali.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and is re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true,breakanywhere=true]
Branches/RealCompact.lean
\end{Verbatim}
path.

This result still does not construct the coherent local cover or prove local
uniform convergence; it records the global conditional handoff that such a
future normal-family/Montel argument must satisfy.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subsequence local-cover branch-family Vitali handoff; PR \#2693]
The PR \#2676 and PR \#2677 handoffs are also recorded in the form produced by
a Montel-style subsequence extraction.  Let
\(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) be a strictly increasing stage map.  On a
Lee--Yang ball \(B(h_0,r)\), suppose a branch family \(F_m\) satisfies
\[
  F_m\text{ analytic on }B(h_0,r),\qquad
  \exp(|\Lambda_{\sigma(m)}|F_m(z))=Z_{\Lambda_{\sigma(m)}}(z),
\]
\[
  F_m(h_0)=
  \texttt{freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion}\,G\,\Lambda\,J\,h_0\,\beta\,
    \sigma(m),
\]
and \(F_m\to f\) locally uniformly on the ball.  Then the theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_subseq_branchFamily_vitali_bridge_ball
\end{Verbatim}
gives holomorphicity of \(f\) on the ball.

At a real centre \(h_0=p.h\), the corresponding centre-identification theorem
(the same name ending in \texttt{\_ball\_identified\_at\_center}) also identifies
the centre value:
\[
  f(p.h)=\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p .
\]
The proof is the same uniqueness-of-limits argument as PR \#2676, with one
additional step: the real-axis convergence
\[
  f_{\Lambda_n}(p.h)\to f_\infty(p)
\]
is composed with \(\sigma\).  Since \(\sigma\) is strictly increasing,
\(\sigma(m)\to\infty\), so the subsequence has the same real-axis limit.

The local-cover theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_subseq_branchFamily_vitali_localCover_real
\end{Verbatim}
globalises this post-extraction handoff on \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).  If each
Lee--Yang point has such a local subsequence branch family and all local
families converge to the same \(f\), then \(f\) is holomorphic on the
Lee--Yang domain and agrees with the real infinite-volume free energy at real
Lee--Yang centres.  The corresponding \(\mathbb Z^d\) ball wrappers now live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/SubseqVitali/Ball.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and the local-cover wrappers now live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/SubseqVitali/LocalCover.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex
\end{Verbatim}
and are re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/SubseqVitali.lean
\end{Verbatim}
path.

This theorem does not prove Montel extraction.  It records the exact
post-extraction target consumed by the remaining normal-family construction.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compact-open ball extraction handoff; PR \#2694]
The compact-open topology supplies the next formal handoff after local
compactness of a branch family has been established.  The generic theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
exists_subseq_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_isCompact_compactOpen
\end{Verbatim}
states the following.  Let \(s\subset\mathbb C\) be open, let
\(\widehat F_n\in C(s,\mathbb C)\), and suppose \(\widehat F_n\in A\) for all
\(n\), where \(A\subset C(s,\mathbb C)\) is compact.  If total functions
\(F_n:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\) agree with \(\widehat F_n\) on \(s\), then there
are a strictly increasing \(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\), a compact-open
limit \(\widehat f\in A\), and a total \(f:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\) agreeing
with \(\widehat f\) on \(s\), such that
\[
  F_{\sigma(m)}\longrightarrow f
  \quad\hbox{locally uniformly on }s .
\]
The proof combines \texttt{IsCompact.tendsto\_subseq} in the compact-open
function space with mathlib's equivalence between compact-open convergence and
locally uniform convergence for continuous maps on weakly locally compact
domains.

For a Lee--Yang ball, the ambient theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_compactOpen_vitali_bridge_ball
\end{Verbatim}
uses this extraction on the continuous restrictions of the branch witnesses and
then applies the PR \#2693 subsequence Vitali bridge.  Thus compactness of the
local branch family in \(C(B(h_0,r),\mathbb C)\) yields a subsequence whose
limit is holomorphic on \(B(h_0,r)\).

At a real centre, the theorem ending in \texttt{\_ball\_real} additionally
identifies the centre value with the real infinite-volume free energy:
\[
  f(p.h)=\texttt{freeEnergyInfinite}\,G\,\Lambda\,p .
\]
The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrappers now live in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/Ball/Bridge.lean
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/Ball/Real.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex}, and are
re-exported by the old paths
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/Ball.lean
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali.lean
\end{Verbatim}

This result still does not prove Montel compactness of the branch family, nor
does it perform the diagonal extraction needed for a coherent local cover of
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).  It isolates the compactness-to-subsequence step
that the remaining normal-family argument must feed.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-ball compact-open diagonal handoff; PR \#2695]
The first finite-diagonal step is formalised by
\begin{Verbatim}
exists_subseq_two_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_isCompact_compactOpen
\end{Verbatim}
and its Lee--Yang wrapper
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_compactOpen_vitali_two_ball
\end{Verbatim}
Given two open sets \(s_1,s_2\subset\mathbb C\), two compact subsets of
\(C(s_i,\mathbb C)\), and two branch families whose continuous restrictions
lie in those compact subsets, one first extracts a subsequence on \(s_1\), then
extracts a further subsequence on \(s_2\).  The auxiliary lemma
\begin{Verbatim}
tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_subseq_of_strictMono
\end{Verbatim}
shows that locally uniform convergence on \(s_1\) is preserved by the second
strictly increasing reindexing.  Thus a single strictly increasing
\(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) works on both balls.

For two Lee--Yang balls the ambient theorem applies the PR \#2693 subsequence
Vitali bridge on each ball, producing holomorphic local limits on both balls.
The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/FiniteDiagonal/TwoBall.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex
\end{Verbatim}
and is re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/FiniteDiagonal.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali.lean
\end{Verbatim}
paths.

This is the two-ball base case for the finite diagonal extraction theorem.  By
itself it does not prove Montel compactness, compatibility of the two limits on
overlaps, or global patching on \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite compact-open diagonal handoff; PR \#2696]
The arbitrary finite extraction step is formalised by
\begin{Verbatim}
exists_subseq_fin_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_isCompact_compactOpen
\end{Verbatim}
and its Lee--Yang wrapper
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_compactOpen_vitali_fin_ball
\end{Verbatim}
For a finite family \(i:\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) of open sets \(s_i\subset\mathbb C\),
compact subsets of \(C(s_i,\mathbb C)\), and total branch families whose
continuous restrictions lie in those compact subsets, the theorem produces one
strictly increasing \(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) such that every
\(F_{i,\sigma(m)}\) converges locally uniformly on \(s_i\).

The proof is induction over \(n\).  At the successor step one extracts on the
head open set, applies the induction hypothesis to the tail families already
restricted to that head subsequence, and uses
\begin{Verbatim}
tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_subseq_of_strictMono
\end{Verbatim}
to preserve the head convergence under the final tail refinement.  For finitely
many Lee--Yang balls the ambient theorem then applies the PR \#2693 subsequence
Vitali bridge on every ball, producing holomorphic local limits for the whole
finite family.  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/FiniteDiagonal/FinBall.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex}, and is
re-exported by the old
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/FiniteDiagonal.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali.lean
\end{Verbatim}
paths.

This result still assumes compact-open compactness for each branch family.  It
does not prove Montel compactness, compatibility of arbitrary branch choices on
overlaps, coherent local-cover extraction, or global patching on
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite overlap-compatibility handoff; PR \#2697]
The generic overlap uniqueness step is formalised by
\begin{Verbatim}
eqOn_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_eventuallyEqOn
pairwise_eqOn_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_of_eventuallyEqOn
\end{Verbatim}
and its Lee--Yang finite-ball wrapper
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_compactOpen_vitali_fin_ball_overlap
\end{Verbatim}
If two stage families converge locally uniformly on open sets \(s\) and \(t\),
and the stage functions are eventually equal on \(s\cap t\), then Hausdorff
uniqueness of pointwise limits gives equality of the two limiting functions on
the overlap.  The finite-family theorem applies this argument pairwise over
\(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\).

For finitely many Lee--Yang balls, the ambient theorem combines this overlap
lemma with the PR \#2696 compact-open finite diagonal extraction.  It returns a
single strictly increasing subsequence \(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\), a
family of holomorphic local limits \(f_i\), and pairwise equalities
\[
  f_i = f_j \quad\text{on}\quad
  B(h_i,r_i)\cap B(h_j,r_j)
\]
whenever the selected stage branches are eventually equal on the same
overlaps.  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali/Overlap.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex}, and is
re-exported by the old
\texttt{SubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpenVitali.lean} path.

This is an explicit-hypothesis compatibility handoff.  It does not construct
coherent branch choices, prove that arbitrary local logarithm branches agree on
overlaps, prove Montel compactness, or patch the resulting local limits to a
global function on \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Packaged finite subsequence branch-limit family; PR \#2705]
The structure
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.LeeYangFiniteSubseqBranchLimitFamily
\end{Verbatim}
packages the finite compact-open diagonal and overlap output.  For a finite
family of balls \(B(h_i,r_i)\), it contains:
\begin{itemize}
\item a strictly increasing stage map
  \(\sigma:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\);
\item per-ball branch families \(F_{i,m}\) indexed by the selected stages;
\item local limits \(f_i\);
\item the stage-\(\sigma(m)\) exponential partition-function identity on each
  ball;
\item centre normalisation
  \(F_{i,m}(h_i)=f_{\Lambda_{\sigma(m)}}(J,h_i,\beta)\);
\item locally uniform convergence \(F_{i,m}\to f_i\), differentiability of
  \(f_i\), and pairwise compatibility on ball overlaps.
\end{itemize}

The theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_finiteSubseqBranchLimitFamily_compactOpen
\end{Verbatim}
constructs such a package from the PR \#2697 finite compact-open/overlap
handoff.  The theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_finiteSubseqBranchLimitFamily_patch
\end{Verbatim}
then consumes the packaged compatibility and patches the local limits to a
single function differentiable on the finite union of balls.  The concrete
\(\mathbb Z^d\) wrappers are
\begin{Verbatim}
freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_finiteSubseqBranchLimitFamily_compactOpen_latticeGraph
freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_finiteSubseqBranchLimitFamily_patch_latticeGraph
\end{Verbatim}
The compact-open package wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpen/FiniteFamily.lean
\end{Verbatim}
The patch wrapper now lives in
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen/Patch/Family.lean
\end{Verbatim}
under \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex}; both are
re-exported by the old paths
\begin{Verbatim}[fontsize=\footnotesize]
SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen/CompactOpen.lean
SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen/Patch.lean
SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen.lean
\end{Verbatim}

This is still a finite, explicit-hypothesis handoff.  It does not prove Montel
compactness or construct a coherent \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\)-cover; it only
records the finite post-extraction output in the same structured style as the
later local-cover packages.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Packaged finite subsequence branch-limit real-centre

Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_finiteSubseqBranchLimitFamily_patch_real
\end{Verbatim}
adds the real-centre conclusion to the PR \#2705 finite package.  Its input is

SubseqCompactOpen/FiniteSubseqCompactOpen.lean

\begin{theorem}[Finite local-patching handoff; PR \#2698]
The finite differentiable patching step is formalised by
\begin{Verbatim}
exists_differentiableOn_iUnion_of_finite_eqOn
\end{Verbatim}
and its Lee--Yang finite-ball wrapper
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_compactOpen_vitali_fin_ball_patch
\end{Verbatim}
Suppose \(s_i\subset\mathbb C\) is a finite family of open sets and
\(f_i\) is differentiable on \(s_i\).  If the local functions are pairwise
compatible,
\[
  f_i=f_j \quad\text{on}\quad s_i\cap s_j ,
\]
then there is a single function \(g\) on \(\mathbb C\) such that
\[
  g=f_i \quad\text{on}\quad s_i
\]
for every \(i\), and \(g\) is differentiable on the finite union
\(\bigcup_i s_i\).

The proof is induction over the finite index.  At the successor step, patch the
tail by the induction hypothesis, define the new function by
\texttt{Set.piecewise} using the head open set, and use pairwise compatibility
to show that this piecewise function agrees with the head branch on the head
and with the tail patch on the tail union.  Differentiability on the final
union follows from \texttt{DifferentiableOn.union\_of\_isOpen}.

For finitely many Lee--Yang balls, the ambient theorem composes this patching
lemma with the PR \#2697 overlap handoff.  It produces the extracted local
limits \(f_i\), a patched function \(g\) on the finite union of balls, local
agreement \(g=f_i\) on each ball, and differentiability of \(g\) on that finite
union.  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper is in
\begin{Verbatim}
Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/PerStageComplex/
  BranchAscoliCompactOpen/EventualPatches/FiniteBallPatch.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and is re-exported through the legacy eventual-patches path.

This is still a finite, explicit-hypothesis handoff.  It does not construct the
coherent stage branches that supply overlap equality, prove Montel compactness,
perform diagonal coherent local-cover extraction, or patch a full
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\)-cover.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Open-cover local-patching handoff; PR \#2699]
The open-cover differentiable patching step is formalised by
\begin{Verbatim}
exists_differentiableOn_iUnion_of_eqOn
\end{Verbatim}
and its Lee--Yang open-cover wrapper
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_openCover_patch
\end{Verbatim}
Let \(s_i\subset\mathbb C\) be an arbitrary family of open sets and let
\(f_i\) be differentiable on \(s_i\).  If the local functions are pairwise
compatible,
\[
  f_i=f_j \quad\text{on}\quad s_i\cap s_j ,
\]
then there is a single function \(g\) on \(\mathbb C\) such that \(g=f_i\) on
each \(s_i\), and \(g\) is differentiable on \(\bigcup_i s_i\).

The proof defines \(g(z)\) by choosing one index \(i\) with \(z\in s_i\) when
\(z\) lies in the union, and using \(0\) outside the union.  Pairwise
compatibility proves that this choice agrees with every local function on its
own open set.  For differentiability, if \(z\in s_i\), then \(s_i\) is a
neighbourhood of \(z\); on that neighbourhood the patched function is
eventually equal to \(f_i\), so differentiability transfers from \(f_i\) to
\(g\).

For a Lee--Yang open cover, the ambient theorem first applies the Vitali
handoff on each cover member to obtain differentiable local limits, then
applies the open-cover patching theorem.  If the cover contains
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\), the resulting patched function is differentiable on
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper is in the
\texttt{OpenPatch/OpenCover.lean} child, re-exported by the legacy
\texttt{OpenPatch.lean} and \texttt{LocalCoverPatch.lean} paths.

This is still a conditional handoff.  It assumes the compatible local-cover
limits explicitly, and does not prove coherent branch selection, Montel
compactness, or diagonal coherent local-cover extraction.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pointed Lee--Yang local-cover patching assembly; PR \#2700]
The theorem
\begin{Verbatim}
Ambient.freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_localCover_patch
\end{Verbatim}
specialises the open-cover patching handoff to the canonical cover of
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\) by balls centred at its own points.  For each
point \(h_0\in\texttt{leeYangDomain}\), assume a positive radius \(r(h_0)\)
whose ball is contained in \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\), a branch family
\(F_{h_0,n}\), and a local limit \(f_{h_0}\).  If \(F_{h_0,n}\) is
holomorphic on the ball, satisfies the finite-stage exponential partition
function identity there, and converges locally uniformly to \(f_{h_0}\), then
the PR \#2699 open-cover theorem supplies differentiability of each local
limit.

The remaining hypothesis is pairwise compatibility:
\[
  f_{h_0}=f_{h_1}
  \quad\text{on}\quad
  B(h_0,r(h_0))\cap B(h_1,r(h_1)).
\]
Under this condition the local limits patch to a single function \(g\) on
\(\mathbb C\), agreeing with each \(f_{h_0}\) on its ball, and \(g\) is
differentiable on \(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).  The proof uses the subtype of
Lee--Yang points as the open-cover index and covers a point \(z\) by the ball
centred at \(z\) itself.  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper is
\begin{Verbatim}
freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchFamily_localCover_patch_latticeGraph
\end{Verbatim}
in
\begin{Verbatim}
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/OpenPatch/LocalCover.lean
\end{Verbatim}
and is re-exported by the legacy paths
\begin{Verbatim}
Branches/LocalCoverPatch/OpenPatch.lean
Branches/LocalCoverPatch.lean
\end{Verbatim}
.

This is still a conditional post-extraction handoff.  It packages the pointed
Lee--Yang ball cover, but it does not prove coherent branch selection, Montel
compactness, or diagonal coherent local-cover extraction.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe \cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S 4.6, pp.~67--70.
\end{theorem}

The structure

Ambient.LeeYangLocalBranchLimit
\end{Verbatim}
packages the data attached to one point of the Lee--Yang domain: a positive

single function \(g\) on \(\mathbb C\), agreeing with every packaged local
limit on its own ball, and \(g\) is differentiable on
\(\texttt{leeYangDomain}\).  The concrete \(\mathbb Z^d\) wrapper is

freeEnergyComplexAlongExhaustion_branchLimitData_localCover_patch_latticeGraph
\end{Verbatim}
in the patch child

\end{Verbatim}
and re-exported by the legacy chain
