\subsection*{Lemma~17.5.2 Part B -- system pseudo-mass and transfer-matrix
all-rate reduction (Partial)}

\subsubsection*{Mathematical content}

Glimm--Jaffe \S17.5 (2nd ed., pp.~311--312) prove the two-sided estimate
\[
  m^-(\sigma) \le m(\sigma) \le \mathrm{const}\cdot m^-(\sigma),
\]
where $m(\sigma)$ is the lattice mass (inverse correlation length) and
$m^-(\sigma)$ is the \emph{system pseudo-mass}, defined as the lower envelope of
the per-pair pseudo-masses $m^-(x,y,\sigma)$: the book chooses a minimizing pair
$x_0\neq y_0$ with $m^-(x_0,y_0,\sigma)=m^-(\sigma)$.

The upper bound $m(\sigma)\le\mathrm{const}\cdot m^-(\sigma)$ (\emph{Part B}) is
derived from the \emph{transfer matrix}, which gives exponential decay of all
correlations at a rate $e^{-m\cdot\mathrm{dist}}$ with
$\mathrm{dist}\ge|x-y|/a_0$; thus
$\langle\phi(x)\phi(y)\rangle\le A\,e^{-(m/a_0)|x-y|}$, and comparison with the
defining identity of $m^-$ yields the bound.  This transfer-matrix step is
\emph{distinct} from the Lipschitz-continuity argument used in the proof of
Theorem~17.5.1 (continuity of $(m^-)^{2\alpha+1}$ in $\sigma$); the Lipschitz
estimate alone does not bound the admissible exponential decay rates.

\subsubsection*{Lean 4 formalization}

This step introduces the system pseudo-mass and isolates the transfer-matrix
content as a single named hypothesis.  The per-pair pseudo-mass
$\mathtt{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair}$ returns $0$ on inactive pairs (correlation
outside $\mathrm{Ioo}\,0\,2$), so the lower envelope is taken over \emph{active}
pairs only, preventing a trivial collapse of the infimum.

\begin{definition}[\texttt{globalPseudoMass}]
For active-pair value set
$\mathtt{globalPseudoMassSet}=\{\,m^-(x,z,\sigma)\mid x\neq z,\
\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle^\infty\in(0,2)\,\}$,
\[
  m^-(\sigma) \;=\; \mathtt{globalPseudoMass}
  \;=\; \operatorname{sInf}\bigl(\mathtt{globalPseudoMassSet}\bigr),
\]
with the real-infimum convention $\operatorname{sInf}\emptyset=0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{globalPseudoMass\_le\_pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair\_of\_active}]
For any active distinct pair $(x,z)$,
$\mathtt{globalPseudoMass}\le\mathtt{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair}\ \dots\ x\ z$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof sketch}:
The value set is bounded below by $0$
(\texttt{globalPseudoMassSet\_bddBelow}, via per-pair nonnegativity), and the
active pair contributes its own pseudo-mass to the set, so $\operatorname{sInf}$
is $\le$ that element by \texttt{csInf\_le}.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_upper\_bound\_of\_global\_all\_rate\_comparison}]
Let $\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_GlobalAllRateComparison}$ be the predicate
\[
  \forall a:\mathbb{R}_{\ge0},\
  \mathrm{HasExponentialDecay}\,(\langle J,0,\beta\rangle)\,a
  \;\Rightarrow\;
  (a:\overline{\mathbb{R}}_{\ge0})\le C\cdot\mathrm{ofReal}\,(\mathtt{globalPseudoMass}).
\]
Then for any active pair $(x,z)$ this predicate implies the named
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}$ at coefficient $C$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof sketch}:
The lower-envelope inequality and monotonicity of
$\mathrm{ENNReal.ofReal}$ and of $C\cdot(-)$ (\texttt{gcongr}) transfer the
global all-rate bound to the pair, and the existing $\operatorname{sSup}$
assembly $\mathtt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_upper\_bound\_of\_all\_decay\_rates\_le}$ closes
the $\mathtt{latticeMass}$ upper-bound predicate.

\noindent\textit{Status}: System pseudo-mass and the order-theoretic reduction
are fully formalized (no \texttt{sorry}); the transfer-matrix comparison
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_GlobalAllRateComparison}$ remains an explicit
hypothesis (Part B analytic core, tracked by issue~\#3378).
File: \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/Lemma\_17\_5\_2/GlobalPseudoMass.lean}.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics} 2nd~ed. (1987),
\S17.5 Lemma~17.5.2, pp.~311--312.

\subsubsection*{All-rate comparison from per-active-pair bounds}

The system pseudo-mass $m^-(\sigma)=\operatorname{sInf}$ over an infinite active
pair set, so a single pair only gives $m^-(\sigma)\le m^-(x,z,\sigma)$.  The
reverse direction needed for the all-rate comparison requires the per-pair
estimate to hold uniformly.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_global\_all\_rate\_comparison\_of\_per\_active\_pair\_rate\_pseudoMass\_lower\_bound}]
Let $\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_PerActivePairRatePseudoMassLowerBound}$ be
\[
  0<K \ \wedge\ \forall a,\
  \mathrm{HasExponentialDecay}\,(\langle J,0,\beta\rangle)\,a
  \Rightarrow
  \forall\,(x,z)\ \text{active},\ (a:\mathbb{R})/K\le m^-(x,z,\sigma).
\]
Given an active-pair witness, this implies
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_GlobalAllRateComparison}$ at coefficient
$\mathrm{ofReal}\,K$, hence (at that pair) the named
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof sketch}:
The uniform per-pair bound and $\mathtt{le\_csInf}$ (with the active-pair witness
supplying nonemptiness) give $(a:\mathbb{R})/K\le m^-(\sigma)$; an
$\mathrm{ENNReal}$ transfer using only $0<K$ then yields
$(a:\overline{\mathbb{R}}_{\ge0})\le\mathrm{ofReal}\,K\cdot\mathrm{ofReal}\,m^-(\sigma)$.
The active-pair witness is essential: the empty-active degenerate slice
($\beta=0$, every rate admissible, $m^-(\sigma)=0$) would otherwise falsify the
statement.

\noindent\textit{Status}: Order-theoretic reduction fully formalized (no
\texttt{sorry}); the per-active-pair rate bound
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_PerActivePairRatePseudoMassLowerBound}$ (the
transfer-matrix exponential-decay step, not reducible to the Simon--Lieb
selected-rate layer alone) remains the explicit analytic input (issue~\#3378).
File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/Lemma\_17\_5\_2/GlobalAllRateComparisonFromPairs.lean}.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics} 2nd~ed. (1987),
\S17.5 Lemma~17.5.2, pp.~311--312.

\subsubsection*{Per-pair rate bound from a uniform $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}$ transfer
bound}

The pseudo-mass calculus already converts a profile-shaped correlation upper
bound into a pseudo-mass lower bound: on the active window
$\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\in(0,2)$,
\[
  \langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le \mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,t
  \quad(t\ge0)
  \ \Longrightarrow\
  t\le m^-(x,z,\sigma)
\]
($\mathtt{pseudoMassFromParamsAtPair\_ge\_of\_corr\_le\_pseudoMassG}$).  Taking
$t=(a:\mathbb{R})/K$ gives the per-pair rate bound, hence (uniformly over active
pairs, with a witness) the named upper bound.

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_upper\_bound\_of\_uniform\_transfer\_pseudoMassG}]
Let $\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UniformTransferPseudoMassGBound}$ be
\[
  0<K\ \wedge\ \forall a,\
  \mathrm{HasExponentialDecay}\,(\langle J,0,\beta\rangle)\,a
  \Rightarrow
  \forall\,(x,z)\ \text{active},\
  \langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,((a:\mathbb{R})/K).
\]
At an active pair $(x,z)$ this implies the named
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}$ at coefficient $\mathrm{ofReal}\,K$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof sketch}:
For each admissible rate the uniform $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}$ bound yields
$(a:\mathbb{R})/K\le m^-(x,z)$ at every active pair, which is exactly the
per-active-pair rate bound; the reductions of the preceding subsections then
close $\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}$.

\noindent\textit{Status}: Reduction fully formalized (no \texttt{sorry}).  At

\subsection*{Lemma~17.5.2 Part B -- closing the upper bound via large-$K$ uniform
transfer (Done)}

\subsubsection*{Mathematical content}

The uniform $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}$ transfer bound, and hence the upper-bound side
$m(\sigma)\le\mathrm{const}\cdot m^-(\sigma)$ of Lemma~17.5.2, is now closed for
ferromagnetic positive-temperature pairs ($0<d$, $0<J$, $0<\beta$, $1\le\alpha$,
$0<r$).  Two uniform facts suffice, with a single constant $K$ depending only on
$\alpha,r,d,J,\beta$:
\begin{itemize}
\item every infinite-volume correlation satisfies
  $\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le 1$, a uniform gap below
  $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,0=2$; and
\item every admissible decay rate $a$ satisfies $a\le -\log(\tanh(\beta J))$
  (the all-rate cap $-\log(\tanh(\beta J))$, transferred to an arbitrary exhaustion).
\end{itemize}
Since $\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r$ is continuous with value $2$ at $0$ and
antitone, it stays $\ge 1$ on a neighbourhood $[0,\delta]$ of $0$; choosing $K$
large enough that $(a:\mathbb{R})/K\le\delta$ for every admissible $a$ gives
$\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le 1\le\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,((a:\mathbb{R})/K)$.

\subsubsection*{Lean 4 formalization}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_upper\_bound\_uniform\_transfer}]
For $1\le\alpha$, $0<r$, $0<d$, $0<J$, $0<\beta$ and a ferromagnetic
positive-temperature active pair $(x,z)$,
\[
  \exists K,\ \mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}\ \dots\ x\ z\ (\mathrm{ofReal}\,K),
  \quad\text{i.e.}\quad
  \mathrm{latticeMass}\le\mathrm{ofReal}\,K\cdot\mathrm{ofReal}\,m^-(x,z).
\]
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Proof sketch}:
$\mathtt{exists\_pos\_forall\_pseudoMassG\_ge\_one\_near\_zero}$ gives $\delta$ with
$\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,t\ge 1$ on $[0,\delta]$ (continuity at $0$,
value $2$);
$\mathtt{exists\_K\_forall\_pseudoMassG\_ge\_one\_of\_rate\_bound}$ picks
$K=\max(1,A/\delta)$ for the rate cap $A$;
$\mathtt{exists\_uniform\_transfer\_pseudoMassG\_of\_rate\_bound}$ uses
$\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le 1$ to validate the uniform transfer bound;
$\mathtt{admissible\_rate\_le\_neg\_log\_tanh}$ supplies $A=-\log(\tanh(\beta J))$
on an arbitrary exhaustion; and the PR~\#3381 chain closes
$\mathtt{Lemma\_17\_5\_2\_UpperBound}$.

\noindent\textit{Status}: Complete formalization (no \texttt{sorry}).  The constant
is uniform in the pair but \emph{not sharp}: this proves the qualitative
Glimm--Jaffe statement $m\le\mathrm{const}\cdot m^-$ via the uniform pseudo-mass
lower bound $m^-(x,z)\ge\mathrm{pseudoMassG}^{-1}(1)$ that
$\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle\le 1$ yields, rather than the sharp transfer-matrix
correlation length.
File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/Lemma\_17\_5\_2/UniformTransferLargeK.lean}.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, \emph{Quantum Physics} 2nd~ed. (1987),
\S17.5 Lemma~17.5.2, pp.~311--312.

\subsection*{Lemma~17.5.2 -- full sandwich with a uniform upper constant (Done)}

\subsubsection*{Mathematical content}

Combining the lower side $m^-\le m$ (the pseudo-mass rate validates exponential
decay, from the profile lower bound
$\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,(-\log(\beta J\,2d))\le

Glimm--Jaffe Lemma~17.5.2 sandwich, for ferromagnetic pairs at
$0<\beta J\,2d<1$:
\[
  \mathrm{ofReal}\,m^-(x,z)\ \le\ \mathrm{latticeMass}\ \le\
  \mathrm{ofReal}\,K\cdot\mathrm{ofReal}\,m^-(x,z).
\]

\subsubsection*{Lean 4 formalization}

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{lemma\_17\_5\_2\_high\_temp\_sandwich\_uniform\_transfer\_forall}]
For $1\le\alpha$, $0<r$, $0<d$, $0<J$, $0<\beta$, $\beta J\,2d<1$ there is a single
$K$ such that every active pair $(x,z)$ with
$\mathrm{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,(-\log(\beta J\,2d))\le\langle\sigma_x\sigma_z\rangle$
satisfies
$\mathrm{ofReal}\,m^-(x,z)\le\mathrm{latticeMass}\le\mathrm{ofReal}\,K\cdot

\end{theorem}

For a distinct pair $(x,z)$, set \(w=z-x\).  The named condition

\subsection*{Step 526 -- all-displacement cubic tanh-profile no-go}

The previous wrapper intentionally treats
\[
  \forall\,w\ne0,\quad
  \mathtt{cubicTanhProfileBound}\,\alpha\,d\,r\,\beta\,J\,w
\]
as a conditional input.  In fact this family cannot be discharged in positive
dimension from only \(0<r\), \(0<\beta J\), and \(\beta J\,2d<1\).  The
predicate requires
\[
  \mathtt{pseudoMassG}\,\alpha\,r\,(-\log(\beta J\,2d))
  \le \tanh(\beta J)^{\operatorname{dist}(0,w)}
\]
at every nonzero displacement.  If \(0<\tanh(\beta J)<1\), the right-hand side
tends to zero along any coordinate axis, while \(\mathtt{pseudoMassG}\) at a
nonnegative rate and \(r>0\) is strictly positive.

\begin{theorem}[All-displacement tanh-profile no-go]
The Lean theorems are
\begin{Verbatim}[breaklines=true]
not_forall_cubicTanhProfileBound_of_tanh_pos_lt_one
not_forall_cubicTanhProfileBound_of_betaJ_pos_high_temp
\end{Verbatim}
In positive dimension and \(0<r\), the all-nonzero
\(\mathtt{cubicTanhProfileBound}\) family is impossible when
\(0<\tanh(\beta J)<1\) and \(-\log(\beta J\,2d)\ge0\).  In particular it is
impossible under \(0<\beta J\) and \(\beta J\,2d<1\).
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textit{Status}: Complete formalization (no \texttt{sorry}).  This
clarifies that the all-pairs tanh-profile sandwich theorem is a conditional
interface, not an input-free high-temperature capstone.

\section{Random-walk representation (FFS Ch 12 / GJ \S18)}

\paragraph{Neighbour-vertex Simon-Lieb transfer kernel (Issue~\#3543 PR~1).}
The Simon-Lieb edge-peeling inequality
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \beta J \sum_{e \ni i}
  \langle\sigma^{\{i,j\}\,\triangle\,\partial e}\rangle$ is recast as a one-step
transfer over \emph{neighbour vertices}, the foundation of the random-walk
representation of the two-point function. Define the kernel
\[
  K(j,u) = \begin{cases} 1 & u = j \\ \langle\sigma_u\sigma_j\rangle & u \ne j
  \end{cases}
  \qquad (\texttt{simonLiebKernel}),
\]
where the $u=j$ value $1 = \langle\sigma_\emptyset\rangle$ collects the
diagonal-edge contribution $\{i,j\}\triangle\{i,j\} = \emptyset$. Its basic
properties (\texttt{simonLiebKernel\_\{self,of\_ne,nonneg,le\_one\}}) follow from
GKS-I and $|\langle\sigma_A\rangle| \le 1$. For an edge $e$ incident to $i$ with
other endpoint $u = \texttt{Sym2.Mem.other}$, the per-edge identity
$\langle\sigma^{\{i,j\}\triangle\,\mathrm{toFinset}\,e}\rangle = K(j,u)$
(\texttt{correlation\_symmDiff\_eq\_simonLiebKernel}) uses
$\{i,j\}\triangle\{i,u\} = \{u,j\}$ for $u \ne j$. Reindexing the incident-edge
sum to a neighbour sum via \texttt{Finset.sum\_bij'} and \texttt{Sym2.other\_spec}
gives the headline one-step inequality
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le \beta J \sum_{u \in \mathcal N(i)} K(j,u)
  \qquad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_simon\_lieb\_neighbor}),
\]
for ferromagnetic $\langle J,0,\beta\rangle$ and $i \ne j$. Iterating this
transfer kernel (later PRs) yields the random-walk bound
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \sum_{\text{walks } i \to j}(\beta J)^{\text{length}}$.
File: \texttt{Inequalities/SimonLiebKernel.lean}. Issue~\#3543 PR~1.

\paragraph{Walk-weight and fixed-length walk-sum framework (Issue~\#3543 PR~2).}
The walk-side companion of the transfer kernel. Define the geometric weight
$\texttt{walkWeight}\,z\,w = z^{w.\mathrm{length}}$ and the walk sum
\[
  \texttt{walkSum}\,G\,z\,i\,j\,n
    = \sum_{w : \text{length-}n\text{ walk } i \to j} z^{w.\mathrm{length}}
  \qquad (z = \beta J).
\]
Every length-$n$ walk has weight $z^n$, so
$\texttt{walkSum} = z^n \cdot \#\{\text{length-}n\text{ walks}\}
  = z^n \cdot (A^n)_{ij}$ (\texttt{walkSum\_eq\_pow\_mul\_card},
\texttt{walkSum\_eq\_pow\_mul\_adjMatrix\_pow}, via
\texttt{adjMatrix\_pow\_apply\_eq\_card\_walk}), nonnegative for $z \ge 0$, and
$\texttt{walkSum}\,z\,i\,j\,0 = [i = j]$ (\texttt{walkSum\_zero}). The headline is
the \emph{neighbour recurrence}
\[
  \texttt{walkSum}\,z\,i\,j\,(n+1)
    = z \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathcal N(i)} \texttt{walkSum}\,z\,u\,j\,n
  \qquad (\texttt{walkSum\_succ}),
\]
from the adjacency-matrix step $(A \cdot A^n)_{ij} = \sum_{u \sim i}(A^n)_{uj}$
(\texttt{adjMatrix\_mul\_apply}). This mirrors the one-step Simon-Lieb transfer
kernel; iterating the kernel against this recurrence (next PR) yields the
random-walk bound. File: \texttt{Inequalities/WalkSum.lean}. Issue~\#3543 PR~2.

\paragraph{Iterated Simon-Lieb transfer kernel (Issue~\#3543 PR~3).}
Iterating the one-step neighbour-vertex kernel $n$ times produces
\[
  \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,p\,j\,0\,i = K(j,i), \qquad
  \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,p\,j\,(n{+}1)\,i =
    \begin{cases} 1 & i = j \\
      \beta J \sum_{u \sim i} \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,p\,j\,n\,u & i \ne j,
    \end{cases}
\]
the $n$-step transfer applied to the kernel, with the diagonal value $K(j,j)=1$
absorbed at the target $j$ (a walk reaching $j$ stops, contributing the
$\langle\sigma_\emptyset\rangle = 1$ factor). The key estimate is the uniform upper bound
\[
  K(j,i) \le \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,j\,n\,i
  \qquad \forall\, n, i
  \quad (\texttt{simonLiebKernel\_le\_simonLiebIterate}),
\]
by induction on $n$ (generalising $i$): base reflexivity; for $i=j$ both sides are
$1$; for $i \ne j$ the one-step kernel $\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \beta J
\sum_{u \sim i} K(j,u)$ combines with the induction hypothesis via $\beta J \ge 0$
and \texttt{Finset.sum\_le\_sum}. For distinct $i \ne j$ this reads
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,\langle
J,0,\beta\rangle\,j\,n\,i$
(\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_simonLiebIterate}). This is the iteration
mechanism of the random-walk representation; a later PR connects the iterated
bound to the walk sum and the high-temperature exponential decay. File:
\texttt{Inequalities/SimonLiebIterate.lean}. Issue~\#3543 PR~3.

\paragraph{High-temperature uniform bound on the iterate (Issue~\#3543 PR~4).}
In the high-temperature regime $\beta J \cdot D \le 1$ ($D$ a vertex-degree
bound) the iterated Simon-Lieb kernel stays uniformly bounded:
\[
  \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,j\,n\,i \le 1
  \qquad \forall\, n, i
  \quad (\texttt{simonLiebIterate\_le\_one}),
\]
by induction on $n$: the base is $K(j,i) \le 1$; for $i=j$ the value is $1$; for
$i \ne j$ the one-step transfer is $\beta J \sum_{u \sim i}(\cdots) \le \beta J
\cdot D \cdot 1 \le 1$ using the induction hypothesis, $\beta J \ge 0$, the degree
bound, and $\beta J \cdot D \le 1$. This is the boundedness input for the
random-walk representation: the iterated upper bound for
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle$ does not blow up as the number of transfer steps
grows (the prerequisite for the first-passage walk-sum limit). The corollary
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le 1$ for $i \ne j$
(\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_one\_of\_high\_temp}) follows by composing
with \texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_simonLiebIterate}. File:
\texttt{Inequalities/SimonLiebIterateHighTemp.lean}. Issue~\#3543 PR~4.

\paragraph{Exponential decay via Simon-Lieb iteration (Issue~\#3543 PR~5).}
The iterated kernel yields exponential decay in the graph distance. If the target
$j$ is more than $n$ steps from $i$ ($n < \mathrm{dist}(i,j)$), the $n$-step
transfer never reaches the absorbing diagonal $K(j,j)=1$, so
\[
  \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,j\,n\,i
    \le (\beta J \cdot D)^n
  \quad (\texttt{simonLiebIterate\_le\_pow\_of\_lt\_dist}),
\]
by induction on $n$: base $0 < \mathrm{dist}(i,j)$ (kernel $K(j,i)\le 1$); step
$\mathrm{dist}(i,j) > n+1$ forces $i \ne j$, and every neighbour $u \sim i$ still
has $\mathrm{dist}(u,j) > n$ (the edge moves the distance by at most one,
\texttt{Adj.diff\_dist\_adj}), so the induction hypothesis bounds each branch by
$(\beta J D)^n$; summing over $\le D$ neighbours times $\beta J$ gives $(\beta J
D)^{n+1}$. Specialising $n = \mathrm{dist}(i,j)-1$ for reachable distinct $i,j$
gives the exponential decay
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le (\beta J \cdot D)^{\mathrm{dist}(i,j)-1}
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_pow\_dist}),
\]
which tends to $0$ with the distance in the high-temperature regime $\beta J
\cdot D < 1$ --- the random-walk (Simon-Lieb) derivation of high-temperature
correlation decay. File: \texttt{Inequalities/SimonLiebIterateDecay.lean}.
Issue~\#3543 PR~5.

\paragraph{$\mathbb Z^d$ wrapper of the Simon-Lieb decay (Issue~\#3543 PR~6).}
On the cubic lattice $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$ every induced-subgraph vertex has
degree $\le 2d$ (\texttt{inducedLatticeGraph\_degree\_le}), so the
high-temperature parameter is $\beta J \cdot 2d$ and
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le (\beta J \cdot 2d)^{\mathrm{dist}(i,j)-1}
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedLatticeGraph\_le\_pow\_dist}),
\]
for reachable distinct sites $i,j$ of the induced subgraph on $\Lambda$
($0 < \mathrm{dist}(i,j)$), decaying exponentially in the induced-graph distance
in the high-temperature regime $\beta J \cdot 2d < 1$. The $\mathbb Z^d$ concrete
reading of the random-walk (Simon-Lieb) high-temperature correlation decay.
File: \texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/SimonLiebDecayLatticeGraph.lean}.
Issue~\#3543 PR~6.

\paragraph{$\ell^1$ lattice-distance form of the decay (Issue~\#3543 PR~7).}
The induced-graph-distance decay refines to the physical $\ell^1$ lattice
distance. A minimal induced-graph walk maps (via the inclusion
$\uparrow\!\Lambda \hookrightarrow \mathbb Z^d$,
\texttt{SimpleGraph.Embedding.induce}) to a $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$ walk of the
same length, so $\mathrm{latticeDistance}\,i\,j \le \mathrm{dist}\,i\,j$
(\texttt{latticeDistance\_le\_inducedGraph\_dist}), the ambient lattice-graph
distance being the $\ell^1$ distance (\texttt{latticeGraph\_dist\_eq\_latticeDistance}).
In the high-temperature regime $\beta J \cdot 2d \le 1$ the base $\le 1$ makes the
geometric bound monotone (\texttt{pow\_le\_pow\_of\_le\_one}), giving
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le (\beta J \cdot 2d)^{\mathrm{latticeDistance}(i,j)-1}
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedLatticeGraph\_le\_pow\_latticeDistance}),
\]
for reachable distinct sites, exponential decay in the $\ell^1$ lattice distance
--- the physically natural reading of the random-walk (Simon-Lieb) high-temperature
correlation decay. File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/SimonLiebDecayLatticeDistance.lean}.
Issue~\#3543 PR~7.

\paragraph{Walk-sum representation of the two-point function (Issue~\#3543 PR~8).}
The genuine FFS Ch~12 walk-sum bound, finally using the walk-sum framework. The
diagonal $K(j,j)=1$ is exactly the length-$0$ walk $\texttt{walkSum}\,0\,j\,j = 1$
($\texttt{simonLiebIterate\_self}$), and the one-step transfer matches
$\texttt{walkSum\_succ}$, so by induction (uniform in $i$)
\[
  \texttt{simonLiebIterate}\,\langle J,0,\beta\rangle\,j\,n\,i
    \le \sum_{k=0}^{n} \texttt{walkSum}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,k + (\beta J\cdot D)^n
  \quad (\texttt{simonLiebIterate\_le\_sum\_walkSum\_add\_pow}),
\]
swapping and folding the neighbour double sum into the shifted walk sum via
\texttt{Finset.sum\_comm} and \texttt{Finset.sum\_range\_succ'}, the not-yet-absorbed
branches giving the geometric remainder $(\beta J D)^n$. For distinct $i \ne j$ the
length-$0$ walk vanishes, giving the finite-horizon walk-sum bound
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le \sum_{k=1}^{n} \texttt{walkSum}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,k + (\beta J\cdot D)^n
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_sum\_walkSum\_add\_pow}),
\]
the finite-horizon form of the random-walk representation
$\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \sum_{k\ge 1}\texttt{walkSum}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,k$.
This is the actual walk-sum representation of the correlation, distinct from the
bare exponential decay. File: \texttt{Inequalities/WalkSumRepresentation.lean}.
Issue~\#3543 PR~8.

\paragraph{Infinite walk-sum (random-walk) upper representation (Issue~\#3543 PR~9).}
In the high-temperature regime $\beta J \cdot D < 1$ the finite-horizon bound
passes to the limit. The number of length-$n$ walks is $\le D^n$, so
$\texttt{walkSum}\,z\,i\,j\,n \le (z\cdot D)^n$
(\texttt{walkSum\_le\_pow\_degree\_bound}), whence the positive-length walk sum is
summable for $z \cdot D < 1$ (\texttt{summable\_walkSum\_of\_lt\_one}, geometric
domination). Passing $\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle \le \sum_{k=1}^{n}
\texttt{walkSum}\,k + (\beta J\cdot D)^n$ to the limit (\texttt{ge\_of\_tendsto'};
the geometric remainder $\to 0$, the partial sums $\to$ the tsum) gives
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le \sum_{k\ge 1}^{\infty} \texttt{walkSum}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,k
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedGraph\_le\_tsum\_walkSum}),
\]
the discrete random-walk (FFS Ch~12) upper bound on the Ising two-point function.
This completes the random-walk representation arc (kernel $\to$ walk-sum $\to$
iterate $\to$ decay $\to$ walk-sum representation $\to$ infinite sum). File:
\texttt{Inequalities/WalkSumTsum.lean}. Issue~\#3543 PR~9.

\paragraph{$\mathbb Z^d$ infinite walk-sum representation (Issue~\#3543 PR~10).}
On the cubic lattice $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$ (induced degree $\le 2d$) the
abstract infinite walk-sum bound specialises: in the high-temperature regime
$\beta J \cdot 2d < 1$, for distinct sites $i \ne j$,
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle
    \le \sum_{k\ge 1}^{\infty} \texttt{walkSum}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,k
  \quad (\texttt{correlation\_inducedLatticeGraph\_le\_tsum\_walkSum}),
\]
the $\mathbb Z^d$ concrete form of the discrete random-walk (FFS Ch~12) upper
bound on the Ising two-point function. File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/WalkSumTsumLatticeGraph.lean}.
Issue~\#3543 PR~10.

\paragraph{Cubic box induced-graph connectivity (infinite-volume infrastructure).}
The induced subgraph of $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$ on a centred box
$\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,n = [-n,n]^d$ is connected: a single distance-reducing
lattice step that moves one differing coordinate one unit towards the target stays
between the endpoints, hence inside the box
(\texttt{cubicBox\_exists\_adj\_step}), and induction on the $\ell^1$ distance
gives reachability of any two box sites
(\texttt{inducedGraph\_cubicBox\_reachable}); distinct sites are therefore at
positive induced-graph distance (\texttt{inducedGraph\_cubicBox\_dist\_pos}). This
is a reusable abstraction that discharges the reachability ($0 < \mathrm{dist}$)
hypotheses of the finite-volume correlation-decay bounds at every cubic-exhaustion
stage, so infinite-volume lifts need not re-prove per-stage reachability. File:
\texttt{Concrete/CubicBoxConnectivity.lean}.

\paragraph{Infinite-volume Simon-Lieb exponential decay on $\mathbb Z^d$ (random-walk route).}
The finite-volume random-walk decay bound is \emph{uniform in the volume}: the
rate and exponent depend only on $i,j$, not on the exhaustion stage. Hence the
thermodynamic limit inherits it:
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle_\infty
    \le (\beta J \cdot 2d)^{\mathrm{latticeDistance}(i,j)-1}
  \quad (\texttt{correlationInfinite\_latticeGraph\_le\_pow\_latticeDistance}),
\]
for distinct $i \ne j$ in the high-temperature regime $\beta J \cdot 2d < 1$. Each
stage $\texttt{correlationAlongExhaustion}\ldots n$ is bounded by the same
constant --- stages containing $\{i,j\}$ via the finite bound (reachability from
the cubic box connectivity \texttt{inducedGraph\_cubicBox\_dist\_pos}), stages not
containing $\{i,j\}$ contributing $0$ --- so $\texttt{correlationInfinite} =
\bigsqcup_n \texttt{correlationAlongExhaustion}$ is bounded by
\texttt{ciSup\_le}. This is the random-walk (FFS Ch~12) derivation of
infinite-volume high-temperature correlation decay (explicit $\beta J\cdot 2d$
rate), a contribution to the project's central long-term goal, the infinite-volume
limit. File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/SimonLiebDecayInfiniteVolume.lean}.

\paragraph{Infinite-volume random-walk (walk-sum) upper representation on $\mathbb Z^d$.}
Beyond the \emph{decay} bound above, the random-walk \emph{structure} itself
survives the thermodynamic limit. Let $\texttt{walkTsumAlongCubic}\,d\,z\,i\,j\,n$
denote the box-confined positive-length walk sum $\sum_{k\ge 1}\texttt{walkSum}\,z\,i\,j\,k$
over walks inside the exhaustion box $(\texttt{cubicExhaustion}\,d).\mathrm{volume}\,n$
(and $0$ before the box contains $\{i,j\}$). Each stage walk sum is dominated,
uniformly in $n$, by the geometric series $\sum_{k\ge 1}(\beta J\cdot 2d)^k$: the
number of length-$k$ walks from $i$ is at most $(2d)^k$
(\texttt{walkSum\_le\_pow\_degree\_bound}, degree $\le 2d$), both series are
summable, and \texttt{Summable.tsum\_le\_tsum} gives
$\texttt{walkTsumAlongCubic\_le\_tsum\_geom}$. Consequently the family
$\{\texttt{walkTsumAlongCubic}\,d\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,n\}_n$ is bounded above, and
since each $\texttt{correlationAlongExhaustion}\,n$ is bounded by its own
box-confined walk sum
($\texttt{correlation\_inducedLatticeGraph\_le\_tsum\_walkSum}$ when the box
contains the pair, $0$ otherwise),
\[
  \langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle_\infty
    \le \bigsqcup_n \texttt{walkTsumAlongCubic}\,(\beta J)\,i\,j\,n
  \quad (\texttt{correlationInfinite\_latticeGraph\_le\_iSup\_tsum\_walkSum}),
\]
for distinct $i \ne j$ in the high-temperature regime $\beta J\cdot 2d < 1$, via
\texttt{le\_ciSup} and \texttt{ciSup\_le}. The two-point function in the infinite
volume is thus exhibited as a supremum of box-confined random-walk sums. File:
\texttt{Concrete/LatticeGraphCorrelation/WalkSumTsumInfiniteVolume.lean}.

\section{Infinite-volume tight ball-boundary inequality (GJ \S17.8)}

The §17.8 polynomial-to-exponential decay layer rested on three declared axioms.
The first, \texttt{ball\_boundary\_tight\_infinite}, is now a \emph{theorem}
(\texttt{TheoremEtaLe1/BallBoundaryInfinite.lean}), obtained as the
infinite-volume limit of the finite-stage tight ball-boundary Simon--Lieb
inequality \texttt{ball\_boundary\_simon\_lieb\_tight} (itself axiom-free since
\texttt{cor\_4\_3\_3\_scaled} was proved). For a ferromagnetic Ising model at
$h=0$ on $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$, with $1\le r$ and a point $x$ satisfying
$r+1 < \texttt{latticeDistance}\,d\,0\,x$,
\[
  \langle\sigma_0\sigma_x\rangle_\infty
  \le \beta J \sum_{(k,l)\in\partial B_r}
    \bigl[\langle\sigma_0\sigma_k\rangle_\infty\langle\sigma_l\sigma_x\rangle_\infty
      + \langle\sigma_0\sigma_l\rangle_\infty\langle\sigma_k\sigma_x\rangle_\infty\bigr].
\]

\paragraph{Correctness finding (hypothesis correction).}
The originally declared axiom asserted this for \emph{every} $r$ and every $x$
with $r < \texttt{latticeDistance}\,d\,0\,x$. The formalization shows this is
false. For $r=0$ the boundary edges run from the origin to its nearest
neighbours, so the origin lies on \emph{every} boundary edge; moreover the
right-hand lift hits the Finset $\{0,0\}$, which collapses to the singleton
$\{0\}$, giving $\langle\sigma_0\rangle = 0$ at $h=0$ instead of the intended
$\langle\sigma_0^2\rangle = 1$, and the bound then fails at high temperature.
For $\texttt{latticeDistance}\,d\,0\,x = r+1$ the sink $x$ sits on the outer
boundary shell, hence on a boundary edge, again breaking the finite-stage
separation hypothesis $0,x\notin e$. The proved theorem therefore carries the
corrected hypotheses $1\le r$ and $r+1 < \texttt{latticeDistance}\,d\,0\,x$. The
distance condition is supplied downstream by \texttt{shellSup\_contraction}
(whose shell point has distance $\ge r+2$); the radius condition $1\le r$ is
genuinely new and must be threaded into \texttt{shellSup\_contraction} when it is
itself discharged (its $r=0$ instance is false for the same Finset-collapse
reason).
This mirrors the false \texttt{lebowitz\_four}/\texttt{lebowitz\_third} axioms
detected earlier in the §4.3 layer.

\paragraph{Proof.}
\texttt{ciSup\_le} reduces to a per-stage bound. At each exhaustion stage $n$
with $\{0,x\}\subseteq\Lambda_n$, apply \texttt{ball\_boundary\_simon\_lieb\_tight}
to the induced graph with $E_0$ the straddling cut edges of the inside ball
$C=\{v : \texttt{latticeDistance}\,d\,0\,v\le r\}$; the disconnection
$\texttt{scaledCorrelation}\;0 = 0$ comes from
\texttt{scaledCorrelation\_at\_zero\_of\_sep} (every cut edge of the stage lies
in $E_0$, so no edge crosses $C$ outside $E_0$), and the separation
$0,x\notin e$ holds because $1\le r$ keeps $0$ off the cut and
$r+1<\texttt{dist}\,x$ keeps $x$ off it (adjacency forces a boundary endpoint to
distance $\le r+1$). Each finite-volume correlation is bounded by its
infinite-volume value via
\texttt{correlationAlongExhaustion\_le\_correlationInfinite}, and the subtype
cut-edge sum reindexes into the ambient $\texttt{latticeBallBoundaryEdges}\,d\,r$
sum: the map $\texttt{Sym2.map Subtype.val}$ is injective, and the image of the
stage-$n$ cut edges is contained in $\texttt{latticeBallBoundaryEdges}$ because
every straddling adjacent pair is confined to $\texttt{cubicBox}\,d\,(r+1)$
(\texttt{latticeBallBoundary\_confine}, \texttt{mem\_latticeBallBoundaryEdges}).
With the ambient summand non-negative, \texttt{Finset.sum\_le\_sum\_of\_subset\_of\_nonneg}
closes the inclusion. Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.8,
(17.8.4)--(17.8.5), pp.~316--318.

\section{Shell supremum contraction (GJ \S17.8)}

The second of the three §17.8 axioms, \texttt{shellSup\_contraction}, is now a
\emph{theorem} (\texttt{TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean}), built directly on the
discharged \texttt{ball\_boundary\_tight\_infinite}. For a ferromagnetic Ising
model at $h=0$ on $\texttt{latticeGraph}\,d$, with $1\le r$ and $r+1<n$,
\[
  \sup_{|y|\ge n} \langle\sigma_0\sigma_y\rangle_\infty
  \;\le\; \texttt{contractionFactor}\,d\,\Lambda\,p\,r \cdot
    \sup_{|y|\ge n-r-1} \langle\sigma_0\sigma_y\rangle_\infty ,
\]
where $\texttt{contractionFactor}\,d\,\Lambda\,p\,r = \beta J\sum_{(k,l)\in\partial B_r}
(\langle\sigma_0\sigma_k\rangle_\infty + \langle\sigma_0\sigma_l\rangle_\infty)$.

\paragraph{Proof.}
\texttt{ciSup\_le} reduces to a per-shell-point bound. For each $y$ with
$|y|\ge n$ (hence $r+1<|y|$, so \texttt{ball\_boundary\_tight\_infinite} applies),
\[
  \langle\sigma_0\sigma_y\rangle_\infty \le \beta J\sum_{(k,l)\in\partial B_r}
    \bigl[\langle\sigma_0\sigma_k\rangle_\infty\langle\sigma_l\sigma_y\rangle_\infty
      + \langle\sigma_0\sigma_l\rangle_\infty\langle\sigma_k\sigma_y\rangle_\infty\bigr].
\]
Translation invariance
(\texttt{correlationInfinite\_latticeGraph\_vaddFinset\_of\_translationInvariant},
shift $t=-w$) gives $\langle\sigma_w\sigma_y\rangle_\infty =
\langle\sigma_0\sigma_{y-w}\rangle_\infty$, and the triangle inequality with the
boundary-endpoint bound $|w|\le r+1$ (\texttt{latticeBallBoundaryEdges\_dist\_le})
yields $|y-w| \ge |y|-(r+1)\ge n-r-1$, so each far factor is at most the
$(n-r-1)$-shell supremum $S$. Summing, $\langle\sigma_0\sigma_y\rangle_\infty \le
\bigl(\beta J\sum (\langle\sigma_0\sigma_k\rangle_\infty +
\langle\sigma_0\sigma_l\rangle_\infty)\bigr)\,S = \texttt{contractionFactor}\cdot S$
(\texttt{shell\_nonempty} supplies the nonempty index for the suprema).

The corrected hypothesis $1\le r$ (inherited from
\texttt{ball\_boundary\_tight\_infinite}, false at $r=0$) is threaded through the
downstream consumers: \texttt{shellSup\_iterated\_bound}, the spatial-decay bounds
\texttt{$\cdots$\_le\_contractionFactor\_pow\_dist(\_pair)}, the
high-temperature mass-gap family (\texttt{HighTempMassGap.lean}), the η≤1 theorem
(\texttt{MainTheorem.lean}, which now picks the contraction radius
$R := \max(R_0,1)$), and the cubic-shell decay-sum chain
(\texttt{CubicShellDecaySum}, \texttt{CubicUrsellShellSum},
\texttt{ShellCovarianceShellSum}). After this, only
\texttt{polynomialDecay\_contraction\_factor\_tendsto} remained, discharged next.
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.8, proof of Theorem 17.8.1, p.~317.

\section{Contraction factor tends to zero (GJ \S17.8) --- last axiom discharged}

The third and final §17.8 axiom, \texttt{polynomialDecay\_contraction\_factor\_tendsto},
is now a \emph{theorem} (\texttt{TheoremEtaLe1/Contraction.lean}). Under
\texttt{HasPolynomialDecay}\,$d\,\Lambda\,p$ (i.e.
$\langle\sigma_0\sigma_x\rangle_\infty\cdot|x|^{d-1}\to 0$ along the cofinite
filter), the contraction factor tends to zero,
$\texttt{contractionFactor}\,d\,\Lambda\,p\,r \to 0$ as $r\to\infty$. With this,
\textbf{GJ §17.8 Theorem 17.8.1 ($\eta \le 1$) is unconditional}, and the entire
project is free of declared axioms (modulo Mathlib).

\paragraph{Surface cardinality.}
The crux is that the boundary has only $O(r^{d-1})$ edges, a \emph{surface} count.
The ℓ¹-sphere bound \texttt{latticeSphere\_card\_le} (\texttt{LatticeSphereCard.lean})
gives $|\{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d : \sum_i|x_i| = r\}| \le 2\,(2r+1)^{d-1}$ via the
two-to-one projection $x \mapsto (\operatorname{sign} x_d,\ \texttt{Fin.init}\,x)$
into $\texttt{Bool}\times\texttt{cubicBox}\,(d{-}1)\,r$ (the last coordinate is
determined up to sign by the first $d-1$, whose ℓ¹ norm is $\le r$). Then
\texttt{latticeBallBoundaryEdges\_card\_le\_sphere} gives
$|\partial B_r| \le 2d\cdot|\texttt{latticeSphere}\,d\,r|$, mapping each boundary
edge to its inside (distance-$r$) endpoint, with at most $2d$ edges per vertex
(\texttt{latticeGraph\_degree\_le}).

\paragraph{Proof.}
Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and set $C := \beta J\cdot 8d\cdot 3^{d-1} + 1$,
$\delta := \varepsilon/C$. Polynomial decay (read through
\texttt{Metric.tendsto\_nhds} and \texttt{Filter.eventually\_cofinite}) makes the
bad set $\{x : \delta \le \langle\sigma_0\sigma_x\rangle_\infty\cdot|x|^{d-1}\}$
\emph{finite}, hence of bounded distance $\le D$; so for every vertex $v$ with
$|v| > D$, $\langle\sigma_0\sigma_v\rangle_\infty\cdot|v|^{d-1} \le \delta$. Each
boundary edge of $\partial B_r$ (for $r \ge D+1$) has both endpoints at distance
in $\{r, r+1\}\subseteq(D,\infty)$, so each summand is
$\le 2\delta/r^{d-1}$. Summing over the $\le 4d\,(2r+1)^{d-1}$ edges and using
$(2r+1)^{d-1} \le 3^{d-1} r^{d-1}$ (for $r\ge1$),
\[
  \texttt{contractionFactor}\,d\,\Lambda\,p\,r
  \;\le\; \beta J\cdot 4d\,(2r+1)^{d-1}\cdot \frac{2\delta}{r^{d-1}}
  \;\le\; \beta J\cdot 8d\cdot 3^{d-1}\cdot \delta
  \;=\; (C-1)\,\delta \;<\; \varepsilon .
\]
Reference: Glimm--Jaffe, 2nd ed., §17.8, pp.~316--318.

\section{Penrose tree-graph inequality (GJ \S18.4--18.5, Issue \#3954)}

A key remaining combinatorial input for general interacting cluster-expansion
convergence (Glimm--Jaffe~\cite{glimm-jaffe}, \S18.4--18.5, pp.~332--340;
Friedli--Velenik~\cite{friedli-velenik}, \S5.7), feeding the majorant summability
already in place, is the \emph{Penrose tree-graph (Ursell) inequality}
\[
  \bigl|\,\texttt{alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum}\,G\,\bigr|
    \;\le\; \texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,G ,
\]
where the left side is $\sum_{S\ \text{connected spanning}} (-1)^{|S|}$ and the
right side counts the spanning trees of $G$. The earlier development reduced this
to an unproven hypothesis structure \texttt{PenrosePartitionScheme} and was deleted;
the present route commits \emph{only unconditionally-true} statements.

\paragraph{Boolean-interval cancellation
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/BooleanInterval.lean}).}
Penrose's argument partitions the connected spanning edge-subsets of $G$ into
Boolean intervals $[\mathit{lo},\mathit{hi}] = \{S \mid \mathit{lo}\subseteq S\subseteq \mathit{hi}\}$,
one per spanning tree $\mathit{lo}$ with \emph{addable} part $\mathit{hi}\setminus\mathit{lo}$.
Parametrising $S = \mathit{lo}\cup U$ with $U\subseteq \mathit{hi}\setminus\mathit{lo}$
(\texttt{booleanInterval\_eq\_image\_powerset\_sdiff}, injective since $\mathit{lo}$ and
$U$ are disjoint) and splitting $|\mathit{lo}\cup U| = |\mathit{lo}| + |U|$ gives the
factorisation
\[
  \sum_{\mathit{lo}\subseteq S\subseteq \mathit{hi}} (-1)^{|S|}
    \;=\; (-1)^{|\mathit{lo}|}\sum_{U\subseteq \mathit{hi}\setminus\mathit{lo}} (-1)^{|U|}
\]
(\texttt{sum\_booleanInterval\_neg\_one\_pow\_card\_int}/\texttt{\_real}). By
$\sum_{U\subseteq X}(-1)^{|U|} = \mathbf 1[X=\varnothing]$
(\texttt{Finset.sum\_powerset\_neg\_one\_pow\_card}) the interval sum
\emph{vanishes} when $\mathit{hi}\setminus\mathit{lo}\ne\varnothing$
(\texttt{\_of\_sdiff\_nonempty}) and equals the survivor $(-1)^{|\mathit{lo}|}$ when
$\mathit{hi}=\mathit{lo}$ (\texttt{\_of\_eq}), in both $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb R$.
This is the sign-cancellation at the heart of the Penrose collapse: only the
trees with no addable edge survive, each contributing $\pm1$.

\paragraph{Spanning-tree edge-subsets
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/SpanningTree.lean}).}
$\texttt{spanningTreeEdgeSubsets}\,G$ records the spanning trees of $G$ as the
connected spanning edge-subsets with exactly $|V|-1$ edges, counted by
$\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,G$. The unit supplies the membership characterisation,
the inclusion into the connected spanning subsets and into the edge powerset,
the crude bounds $\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,G \le |\texttt{connectedSpanningEdgeSubsets}\,G|
\le 2^{|E(G)|}$, and monotonicity of $\texttt{numSpanningTrees}$ in the graph order
(\texttt{numSpanningTrees\_mono}). The remaining steps (a from-scratch partition
scheme assigning each connected spanning subgraph its spanning tree with the
addable-edge interval property, then the Kotecký--Preiss tree-sum induction) build
on this foundation.

\paragraph{The partition scheme: \texttt{treeOf} and \texttt{addable}
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/PartitionScheme.lean}).}
The genuine combinatorial core is constructed by the edge-order Kruskal /
reachability rule, with no hypothesis structures. Edges are totally ordered by an
explicit key $\texttt{edgeKey}\,e := \texttt{toLex}\,(\texttt{Sym2.sortEquiv}\,e)$
into the lexicographic pairs $V \times_\ell V$ (injective, $\texttt{edgeKey\_injective}$):
edges $f$ are compared by $\texttt{edgeKey}\,f < \texttt{edgeKey}\,e$. An explicit key
is necessary because mathlib's ambient \texttt{SetLike} order on $\mathtt{Sym2}\,V$ is
only \emph{partial} (distinct non-diagonal graph edges are never comparable, which would make
the Kruskal ``strictly smaller'' test vacuous). For an edge-subset $X$ and edge $e$,
$\texttt{reachableLT}\,X\,e$ tests whether the endpoints of $e$ are already joined
inside $\texttt{fromEdgeSet}$ of the edges $f$ of $X$ with
$\texttt{edgeKey}\,f < \texttt{edgeKey}\,e$ (a symmetric vertex relation descended to
$\mathtt{Sym2}\,V$ by $\texttt{liftSym2Prop}$).
Then
\[
  \texttt{treeOf}\,S := S.\texttt{filter}\,(\lnot\,\texttt{reachableLT}\,S\,\cdot)
\]
is the Kruskal minimum spanning forest of $S$ --- keep an edge iff its endpoints are
not yet joined by the strictly-smaller edges of $S$ --- and
\[
  \texttt{addable}\,G\,T := G.\texttt{edgeFinset}.\texttt{filter}\,
    (\cdot\notin T \wedge \texttt{reachableLT}\,T\,\cdot)
\]
collects the non-$T$ edges of $G$ that are the maximum edge of the fundamental cycle
they form with $T$, i.e.\ the edges freely addable to a spanning tree $T$ inside its
Boolean interval. This PR proves the structural lemmas $\texttt{treeOf}\,S\subseteq S$
($\texttt{treeOf\_subset}$), $\texttt{treeOf}\,S\subseteq G.\texttt{edgeFinset}$,
$\texttt{addable}\,G\,T\subseteq G.\texttt{edgeFinset}$, and
$\texttt{Disjoint}\,T\,(\texttt{addable}\,G\,T)$, together with the membership
characterisations. The Kruskal correctness ($\texttt{treeOf}\,S$ is a spanning tree)
and the interval-partition property
$\texttt{treeOf}\,S = T \leftrightarrow T\subseteq S\subseteq T\cup\texttt{addable}\,G\,T$
follow in later PRs.

\paragraph{Kruskal connectivity
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/KruskalConnected.lean}).}
The Kruskal forest preserves reachability. Write $\texttt{edgesLT}\,X\,e$ for the edges
$f$ of $X$ with $\texttt{edgeKey}\,f < \texttt{edgeKey}\,e$, so $\texttt{reachableLT}\,X\,s(a,b)$
unfolds to reachability of $a,b$ inside $\texttt{fromEdgeSet}\,(\texttt{edgesLT}\,X\,s(a,b))$
($\texttt{reachableLT\_iff\_edgesLT}$). A transport lemma
$\texttt{reachable\_mono\_of\_edges\_reachable}$ (if every edge of $S$ has
$T$-reachable endpoints then $S$-reachability descends to $T$, by
$\texttt{reachable\_iff\_reflTransGen}$ and $\texttt{ReflTransGen}$ induction) feeds
the Kruskal key lemma $\texttt{reachable\_endpoints\_of\_mem\_treeOf}$: every edge
of $S$ has $\texttt{treeOf}\,S$-reachable endpoints, by strong induction over the
$\texttt{edgeKey}$-pullback well-founded edge order ($\texttt{WellFounded.induction}$)
--- a kept edge yields an adjacency, a dropped edge $e$ has its endpoints joined by
strictly-smaller $S$-edges, each $\texttt{treeOf}$-reachable by the induction
hypothesis. Hence the global reachability equivalence
($\texttt{reachable\_treeOf\_iff\_reachable}$), the connectivity
$\texttt{connected\_treeOf\_of\_connected}$, and the bookkeeping helper
$(\texttt{fromEdgeSet}\,(\texttt{treeOf}\,S)).\texttt{edgeFinset} = \texttt{treeOf}\,S$
($\texttt{edgeFinset\_fromEdgeSet\_treeOf}$).

\paragraph{Kruskal acyclicity and the spanning-tree headline
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/KruskalAcyclic.lean}).}
$\texttt{treeOf}\,S$ is acyclic by the \emph{cycle-max argument}. Any cycle $c$ in
$\texttt{fromEdgeSet}\,(\texttt{treeOf}\,S)$ has a nonempty edge finset
($\texttt{cycle\_edgeFinset\_nonempty}$); localising $c$ to
$\texttt{fromEdgeSet}\,c.\texttt{edges.toFinset}$ and applying
$\texttt{adj\_and\_reachable\_delete\_edges\_iff\_exists\_cycle}$ shows the endpoints of
any cycle edge are reachable via the remaining cycle edges
($\texttt{reachable\_from\_cycle\_edgeFinset\_erase}$). For a maximum-$\texttt{edgeKey}$
cycle edge $M$, the remaining edges all have smaller key, hence lie in
$\texttt{edgesLT}\,S\,M$ ($\texttt{cycle\_edge\_erase\_subset\_edgesLT}$), giving
$\texttt{reachableLT}\,S\,M$ --- contradicting $M \in \texttt{treeOf}\,S$
($\texttt{isAcyclic\_fromEdgeSet\_treeOf}$). Being connected and acyclic,
$\texttt{treeOf}\,S$ is a tree, so
$|\texttt{treeOf}\,S| = |V|-1$ ($\texttt{treeOf\_card\_eq\_card\_vertices\_sub\_one}$ via
$\texttt{IsTree.card\_edgeFinset}$) and the headline follows:
$S \in \texttt{connectedSpanningEdgeSubsets}\,G \Rightarrow
\texttt{treeOf}\,S \in \texttt{spanningTreeEdgeSubsets}\,G$
($\texttt{treeOf\_mem\_spanningTreeEdgeSubsets}$).

\paragraph{Interval-partition property
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/IntervalPartition.lean}).}
The $\texttt{treeOf}$ retraction partitions the connected spanning edge-subsets into
Boolean intervals. The new ingredient is a \emph{prefix} reachability equivalence
$\texttt{reachableLT}\,(\texttt{treeOf}\,S)\,e \leftrightarrow \texttt{reachableLT}\,S\,e$
--- the $< e$ edges of $S$ and of $\texttt{treeOf}\,S$ span the same components, by strong
induction over the $\texttt{edgeKey}$ order
($\texttt{reachable\_edgesLT\_treeOf\_of\_mem\_edgesLT}$,
$\texttt{reachable\_edgesLT\_treeOf\_iff}$, $\texttt{reachableLT\_treeOf\_iff}$), refining the
global equivalence. With $\texttt{isTree\_fromEdgeSet\_of\_mem\_spanningTreeEdgeSubsets}$ and
$\texttt{not\_reachableLT\_of\_mem\_spanningTreeEdgeSubsets}$ (a tree edge is a bridge, hence
not $\texttt{reachableLT}$ via its smaller edges) one proves both directions: forward
$\texttt{subset\_union\_addable\_of\_treeOf\_eq}$ (a dropped edge is addable, through the prefix
equivalence) and converse $\texttt{treeOf\_eq\_of\_subset\_union\_addable}$ (addable edges are
dropped, tree edges kept via $\texttt{not\_reachableLT\_of\_interval\_tree\_edge}$). Hence the
interval property
$\texttt{treeOf}\,S = T \leftrightarrow T \subseteq S \wedge S \subseteq T \cup \texttt{addable}\,G\,T$
($\texttt{treeOf\_eq\_iff\_subset\_union\_addable}$) and the fiber identity
$\{S \in \texttt{connectedSpanningEdgeSubsets}\,G \mid \texttt{treeOf}\,S = T\}
= \texttt{booleanInterval}\,T\,(T \cup \texttt{addable}\,G\,T)$
($\texttt{treeOf\_fiber\_eq\_booleanInterval}$).

\paragraph{The Penrose tree-graph inequality
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/TreeGraphBound.lean}).}
Summing the alternating connected-subgraph sum fiberwise over $\texttt{treeOf}$
($\texttt{Finset.sum\_fiberwise\_of\_maps\_to}$, with $\texttt{treeOf}$ mapping connected
spanning edge-subsets into spanning trees) and rewriting each fiber as a Boolean interval,
each interval contributes $0$ when its addable part is nonempty
($(T \cup \texttt{addable}\,G\,T) \setminus T = \texttt{addable}\,G\,T$ via
$\texttt{addable\_disjoint}$) and $\pm 1$ when it is empty
($\texttt{abs\_sum\_booleanInterval\_addable\_le\_one}$). Hence the unconditional
\emph{Penrose tree-graph inequality}
\[
  |\texttt{alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum}\,G| \;\le\; \texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,G
\]
($\texttt{abs\_alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum\_le\_numSpanningTrees}$), completing the
from-scratch partition-scheme route.

\paragraph{Ursell tree bound
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/UrsellTreeBound.lean}).}
Applying the Penrose inequality to the incompatibility graph
$\texttt{polymerSeqIncompatibilityGraph}\,\omega$ and using
$\texttt{ursellCoefficient}\,\omega
= \texttt{alternatingConnectedSubgraphSum}\,(\dots)/n!$ gives the sharp Ursell bound
\[
  |\phi^T(\omega)| \;\le\;
  \frac{\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\texttt{polymerSeqIncompatibilityGraph}\,\omega)}{n!}
  \;\le\;
  \frac{\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n))}{n!}
\]
($\texttt{ursellCoefficient\_abs\_le\_numSpanningTrees\_div\_factorial}$ and its uniform
form via $\texttt{Penrose.numSpanningTrees\_mono}$ with $\texttt{le\_top}$) --- the sharp
replacement of the trivial $2^{|E|}/n!$ bound and the entry point of the
Kotecký--Preiss / tree-sum convergence (combined with a summable spanning-tree-count
majorant: Cayley $n^{n-2}$ or the tree-sum induction).

\paragraph{Complete-graph spanning-tree count bound
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/CompleteGraphTreeBound.lean}).}
The summable majorant for the cluster-expansion convergence requires a bound on
$\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n))$, the
number of spanning trees of the complete graph $K_n$. The exact Cayley value
$n^{n-2}$ is \emph{not} needed: the weaker unconditional bound
\[
  \texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n))
    \;\le\; n^{\,n-1}
\]
($\texttt{numSpanningTrees\_top\_fin\_le\_pow\_pred}$, with the $\texttt{Fin}\,(n{+}1)$ form
$\texttt{numSpanningTrees\_top\_fin\_succ\_le\_pow}$: $\le (n{+}1)^n$) already yields the
finite radius of convergence $1/e$ for the Mayer series, since
$\sum_n n^{n-1}/n!\cdot R^n$ converges absolutely for $|R| < 1/e$ (the ratio
$(1+1/n)^{n-1}\,|R| \to e\,|R|$). The bound is proved by a \emph{parent-function injection}
that avoids Pr\"ufer/Cayley entirely. Root the tree at the vertex $0$. Each non-root
vertex $v$ has a unique \emph{parent} $\texttt{treeParent}\,(v)$: the unique neighbour
with $\texttt{dist}\,(0,v) = \texttt{dist}\,(0,\texttt{treeParent}\,(v)) + 1$
(existence $\texttt{exists\_parent\_adj\_dist\_of\_isTree}$ via the second vertex of a
shortest walk $v \to 0$; uniqueness
$\texttt{parent\_adj\_dist\_unique\_of\_isTree}$ via the uniqueness of paths in a tree,
$\texttt{IsTree.existsUnique\_path}$). The parent code
$\texttt{completeGraphTreeParentCode} : \texttt{Fin}\,n \to \texttt{Fin}\,(n{+}1)$ sends
$\texttt{Fin.succ}\,i \mapsto \texttt{treeParent}\,(\texttt{Fin.succ}\,i)$. The crux is the
edge-set recovery $\texttt{completeGraphTree\_edges\_eq\_parentCode\_image}$: the edge set of
the tree equals the image $\{\,s(\texttt{Fin.succ}\,i, \texttt{treeParent}\,(\texttt{Fin.succ}\,i))\,\}$,
because for any tree edge $s(a,b)$ the endpoint farther from the root (by
$\texttt{IsTree.dist\_eq\_dist\_add\_one\_of\_adj}$) has the other as its unique parent.
Hence the parent code is injective on spanning trees
($\texttt{completeGraphTreeParentCode\_injective}$), and
$\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,(n{+}1)))
  \le |\texttt{Fin}\,n \to \texttt{Fin}\,(n{+}1)| = (n{+}1)^n$ by
$\texttt{Fintype.card\_le\_of\_injective}$ and $\texttt{Fintype.card\_fun}$. This is the
combinatorial heart of milestone~M2 of Issue~\#3954.

\paragraph{Summable Mayer majorant
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/Penrose/SpanningTreeSummable.lean}).}
The spanning-tree count bound feeds the summable majorant for the Mayer/Ursell
series.  For $R$ with $e\,|R| < 1$ (equivalently $|R| < 1/e$),
\[
  \sum_{n} \frac{\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n))}{n!}\,R^n
\]
converges absolutely
($\texttt{summable\_completeGraph\_numSpanningTrees\_div\_factorial\_mul\_pow}$, with the
absolute form \texttt{\_abs\_pow}).  By the count bound
$\texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n)) \le n^{n-1}$
this majorises into the pure-power series
$\sum_n n^{n-1}/n!\cdot R^n$
($\texttt{summable\_nat\_pow\_pred\_div\_factorial\_mul\_pow}$), whose convergence is the
\emph{ratio test} $\texttt{summable\_of\_ratio\_norm\_eventually\_le}$: the eventual ratio is
\[
  \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n} = \Bigl(1 + \tfrac1n\Bigr)^{n-1} |R| \;\le\; e\,|R| < 1 ,
\]
where the elementary bound $\bigl(1 + \tfrac1n\bigr)^{n-1} \le e$
($\texttt{one\_add\_inv\_natCast\_pow\_pred\_le\_exp}$, from $1 + x \le e^x$ at $x = 1/n$ raised
to the $(n-1)$-th power, so that $e^{(n-1)/n} \le e$ --- no limit
$(1+\tfrac1n)^n \to e$ is needed) gives the post-cancellation inequality
$(n+1)^{n-1} \le e\,n^{n-1}$ ($\texttt{succ\_pow\_pred\_le\_exp\_mul\_pow\_pred}$).  This is the
convergent majorant of the cluster expansion (Mayer radius $1/e$); the remaining M2 steps
are the Mayer-term reduction $\texttt{Summable}\,(\texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}\,G\,\cdot)$
(Kotecký--Preiss) and the identity $\log\Xi = \sum_n$ cluster.

\paragraph{Absolute convergence of the Mayer expansion
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/MayerCore/UrsellMajorant.lean}).}
The spanning-tree majorant closes the cluster-expansion absolute convergence.  For an
activity $t$ with $e \cdot A < 1$, where $A := \sum_{P \in \texttt{allPolymers}\,G} |t|^{|P|}$,
\[
  \texttt{Summable}\,\bigl(n \mapsto \texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}\,G\,n\,t\bigr)
\]
($\texttt{summable\_mayerExpansionTerm\_of\_exp\_one\_mul\_activity\_lt\_one}$, with the usable
form $\texttt{summable\_mayerExpansionTerm\_of\_card\_mul\_lt}$ requiring $|t| \le 1$ and
$e \cdot |\texttt{allPolymers}\,G| \cdot |t| < 1$).  The bound chain is: the Ursell coefficient
is uniformly bounded,
$|\phi^T(\omega)| \le \texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top : \texttt{SimpleGraph}\,(\texttt{Fin}\,n))/n!$;
the total absolute activity over $n$-tuples factorises,
\[
  \sum_{\omega \in \texttt{piFinset}(\texttt{allPolymers}\,G)} |z(t,\omega)|
    = \Bigl(\sum_{P} |t|^{|P|}\Bigr)^n
\]
($\texttt{sum\_clusterSeqActivity\_abs\_piFinset}$, by $\texttt{Finset.sum\_prod\_piFinset}$); hence
$|\texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}\,G\,n\,t|
  \le \texttt{numSpanningTrees}\,(\top\,\texttt{Fin}\,n)/n! \cdot A^n$
($\texttt{mayerExpansionTerm\_abs\_le\_tree\_activity\_pow}$), which is exactly the spanning-tree
majorant at $R = A$.  This is the cluster-expansion absolute convergence $\sum_n$ for general
interacting polymers; the remaining M2 steps are $\log\Xi = \sum_n \texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}$
(Kotecký--Preiss) and the high-temperature Ising specialisation $t = \tanh(\beta J)$.

\paragraph{High-temperature convergence of the Ising cluster expansion
(\texttt{ClusterExpansion/MayerCore/MayerTanhConvergence.lean}).}
Specialising the absolute convergence to the Ising activity $t = \tanh(\beta J)$:
$\texttt{summable\_mayerExpansionTerm\_tanh}$ gives
$\texttt{Summable}\,\bigl(n \mapsto \texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}\,G\,n\,(\tanh(\beta J))\bigr)$
whenever $e \cdot |\texttt{allPolymers}\,G| \cdot |\tanh(\beta J)| < 1$ (using $|\tanh| < 1$), with
the ferromagnetic form $\texttt{summable\_mayerExpansionTerm\_tanh\_ferro}$ ($0 \le \beta J$,
$e \cdot |\texttt{allPolymers}\,G| \cdot \tanh(\beta J) < 1$) and the activity-sum form
$\texttt{\_of\_activity}$; the ferromagnetic activity bound
$\texttt{tanh\_activity\_sum\_le\_card\_mul\_tanh}$ reads
$\sum_{P} \tanh(\beta J)^{|P|} \le |\texttt{allPolymers}\,G| \cdot \tanh(\beta J)$.  Since $\tanh$
is continuous with $\tanh 0 = 0$, the criterion holds at high temperature ($\beta J$ near $0$):
the Ising cluster expansion \emph{converges absolutely at high temperature}.  The remaining step
is the Mayer--Montroll identity $\log\Xi = \sum_n \texttt{mayerExpansionTerm}$ (Issue~\#1499 Phase C).
